nodes.name: Non-local operator of variable order $\mathcal L$
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal L$ is the jump operator with kernel $\kappa(x,z)/|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}$, where $\alpha$ is bounded in $[\alpha_1,\alpha_2]$ and $\beta_1$-Hölder and $\kappa$ is symmetric, bounded and $\beta_2$-Hölder.

nodes.name: Equation (1.1)
nodes.statement:
{\mathcal L} f(x)=\int_{\mathds R^d}\big(f(x+z)-f(x)-\langle\nabla f(x), z\rangle \mathds 1_{\{|z|\leqslant 1\}}\big)
\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz,\quad   f \in C_c^2(\mathds R^d),
nodes.label: e1-1

nodes.label: e1-3

nodes.name: Hölder exponent $\beta_0$
nodes.statement: Set $\beta_0= \beta_1\wedge \beta_2$.

nodes.name: Order of the non-local operator
nodes.statement: For this reason, we call $\alpha(x)$ the order of the non-local operator at the point $x\in \mathds R^d$.

nodes.name: Fundamental solution for variable-order operators
nodes.statement:
When $\alpha(x)$ is not a constant, how can we construct a fundamental solution of ${\mathcal L}$ that really satisfies
 the parabolic equation \eqref{t1-1-1} below?  What are upper
and lower bound estimates for this solution (if it exists)? We point out that it had not been established that,
even under additional smoothness assumptions on $\alpha (x)$ and $\kappa (x)$,
the  heat kernel constructed  in \cite{Kol}  by Duhamel formula is actually a solution to the equation \eqref{t1-1-1}.
nodes.statement_short: Construct a genuine fundamental solution of $\mathcal L$ for non-constant $\alpha$ and find its two-sided bounds.

nodes.name: Existence of a strong Markov process for $\mathcal L$
nodes.statement:
When $\alpha(x)$ is not a constant and $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$, is there a strong Markov process
associated with ${\mathcal L}$?  In literature, the existence of strong Markov process was
always assumed a priori  in the study of regularity of harmonic
functions and elliptic Harnack inequalities for such non-local operator ${\mathcal L}$,
see \cite{BK1,BK2, LW} for examples.
nodes.statement_short: Is there a strong Markov process associated with $\mathcal L$ when $\alpha$ is variable and $\kappa$ depends on $z$?

nodes.name: Local regularity in terms of $\alpha(x_0)$
nodes.statement:
In existing literature,
  regularity for the solution to parabolic equation \eqref{t1-1-1} associated
with ${\mathcal L}$ usually depends on
 the uniform bounds $\alpha_1$ and $\alpha_2$ in
\eqref{e1-3}.
Can one establish regularity of the fundamental solution in some neighborhood of  $x_0$ (such  as  gradient estimate) in terms of $\alpha(x_0)$ under some special settings?
nodes.statement_short: Can regularity of the fundamental solution near $x_0$ be expressed through $\alpha(x_0)$ rather than the global bounds?

nodes.name: Open ball $B(x_0,r)$
nodes.statement: For $x_0\in \mathds R^d$ and $r>0$, define  $B(x_0, r):=\{x\in \mathds R^d: |x-x_0|<  r_0\}$.

nodes.name: Space $C_{b,u}(\mathds R^d)$
nodes.statement: Let $C_{b,u}(\mathds R^d)$ denote the set of all bounded and uniformly continuous functions on $\mathds R^d$.

nodes.name: Heat kernel of $\mathcal L$ for $z$-independent $\kappa$
nodes.statement_short: If $\kappa$ does not depend on $z$, $\mathcal L$ has a jointly continuous heat kernel with two-sided bounds governed by $\alpha(x)$, Hölder/gradient estimates, Chapman–Kolmogorov, conservativeness, generator property and uniqueness.

nodes.statement:
\begin{itemize}
\item [(1)] From \eqref{t1-1-4} and \eqref{t1-1-4b}, we know that both upper and lower bounds of
near-diagonal
estimates for $p(t,x,y)$ enjoy the same order $t^{-{d/\alpha(x)}}$, which typically depends on $x$.
In particular, along with \eqref{t1-1-4b}, when $r_0=\infty$ in \eqref{t1-1-4a} (i.e.\ $\alpha(x)\equiv \alpha \in (0,2)$ for all $x\in \mathds R^d$), we arrive at the two-sided heat kernel estimates obtained in
\cite{CZ}.
Furthermore, by \eqref{t1-1-7} and \eqref{t1-1-7a}, the regularity of $p(t,\cdot,y)$ at $x=x_0$ only depends on
$x_0$.

\item [(2)] Compared with these results yielded by  Duhamel's formula in \cite{Kol},  Theorem \ref{t1-1}(v) shows that the function $u_f(t,x):=\int_{\mathds R^d}p(t,x,y)f(y)\,dy$ solves  the Cauchy problem for  ${\mathcal L}$. In particular, by \eqref{t1-1-1} and \eqref{t1-1-3}, we have
\begin{equation*}
\begin{cases}
\frac{\partial }{\partial t} p(t,x,y) = {\mathcal L} p(t,\cdot,y)(x)\\
\lim_{t \downarrow 0} p(t,x,y)=\delta_y(x),
\end{cases}
\end{equation*}
which means that $p(t,x,y)$ is the fundamental solution associated
with ${\mathcal L}$. It is easy to deduce from \eqref{t1-1-7},  \eqref{t1-1-5}, \eqref{t1-1-6},
\eqref{t1-1-2} and \eqref{t1-1-5a} that there is  a conservative Feller process  having the strong Feller property
associated with the operator ${\mathcal L}$;  cf.  Proposition \ref{p4-4} below.
Recall that a Markov process on $\mathds R^d$ is said to be a Feller process if its transition semigroup is a strongly continuous semigroup in the Banach space of continuous functions that vanish at infinity equipped
with the uniform norm.
A Markov process is said to have the strong Feller property if its transition semigroup maps bounded
measurable functions to bounded continuous functions.
\end{itemize}

nodes.statement:
Let $\beta_0^{**}\in(0,\beta_0]\cap(0,{\alpha_2}/{2}).$
For general $\kappa (x, z)$  satisfying  \eqref{e1-3} and \eqref{e1-2}, if
$
 ({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1<\beta_0^{**}/{\alpha_2},
$
 there exists a
jointly continuous non-negative function
$p:(0,1]\times \mathds R^d \times \mathds R^d \rightarrow \mathds R_+$ such that
all the conclusions in Theorem $\ref{t1-1}$ hold
except that the  upper bounds \eqref{t1-1-4}-\eqref{t1-1-4a} in {\rm (i)} and
H\"{o}lder regularity and gradient estimates \eqref{t1-1-7} and \eqref{t1-1-7a}
in {\rm (ii)} are to be replaced
by the following estimates.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)]{\bf (Upper bounds)}\,\, For any $\gamma, c_0>0$, there exist constants $c_1 =c_1(\alpha,\kappa,c_0)>0$ and $c_2 =c_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma,c_0)>0$
such that for all $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in\mathds R^d$,
\begin{equation} p(t,x,y)\leqslant
\begin{cases}
{c_1}{t^{-{d/\alpha(x)}}},&\quad |x-y|< c_0t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}, \smallskip \\
\frac{c_1t^{2-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_2}} \wedge \frac{c_2t^{2-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-\gamma}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}},&\quad
c_0t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}\leqslant |x-y|< 1,  \smallskip \\
\frac{c_1t^{2-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}},&\quad |x-y|\geqslant 1.
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
If, in addition,  there are some $x_0\in\mathds R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(x_0)$ for all $z \in B(x_0,r_0)$, then for any $c_0>0$ there is a positive
constant $c_3:=c_3(\alpha,\kappa,r_0,c_0)$ so that for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $y \in \mathds R^d$,
\begin{equation} p(t,x_0,y)\leqslant
\begin{cases}
{c_3}{t^{-{d/\alpha (x_0)}}},&\quad |y-x_0|< c_0t^{{1/\alpha(x_0)}}, \smallskip \\
\frac{c_3 t^{2-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})}
}{|y-x_0|^{d+\alpha(x_0)}},& \quad
c_0t^{{1/\alpha(x_0)}}\leqslant |y-x_0|< {r_0}/{2}, \smallskip \\
\frac{c_3 t^{2-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})} }{|x-y_0|^{d+\alpha_1}},&\quad |y-x_0|\geqslant {r_0}/{2}.
\end{cases}
\end{equation}


\item[(ii)] {\bf (H\"{o}lder regularity and gradient estimates)}\,\,
For every
$\gamma \in (0, \alpha_1]$,
there exist constants
$c_5 =c_5(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma)$ and $R_1 =R_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma)>0$ such that for all $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,x',y \in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|\leqslant R_1$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
 \big|p(t,x,y)-p(t,x',y)\big|
&\leqslant c_5|x-x'|^{(\alpha_1-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}
\big(\rho^{y,0}_{\gamma_1}(t,x-y)+ \rho^{y,0}_{\gamma_1}(t,x'-y)\big),
\end{split}
\end{equation}
where $\gamma_1:=1-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})+({\gamma}/({2\alpha_2}))$.
Let $\beta_0^*$ and $\tilde \beta_0(x_0)$ be the same constants in
Theorem $\ref{t1-1}$ $(ii)$. If moreover $\tilde \beta_0(x_0)-({\alpha_1\alpha_2}/{\alpha(x_0)})
\big(({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1\big)>1-\alpha_1$ for some
$x_0\in \mathds R^d$, then for every fixed $t \in (0,1]$ and $y \in \mathds R^d$, $p(t,\cdot,y)$ is differentiable
at $x=x_0$. In this case, for every $\gamma>0$, there exists a constant
$c_6:=c_6(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma, x_0)$ such that for all $ t\in (0,1]$ and $y\in \mathds R^d$,
\begin{equation} |\nabla p(t,\cdot,y)(x_0)|\leqslant c_6
\rho^{x,0}_{1-(1/\alpha_1)+(\beta_0^*/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0^*/\alpha_1)-\gamma_2}(t,x_0-y),
\end{equation} where $\gamma_2=(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)-1+\gamma.$
\end{enumerate}

nodes.statement:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)] According to Theorem \ref{t1-2} above, when $\alpha(x)$ is not a constant function and $\kappa(x,z)$
depends on $z$,
we can construct heat kernel associated with the operator ${\mathcal L}$ when
$({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1<\beta_0^{**}/{\alpha_2}$, which indicates that
the oscillation of the index function $\alpha(x)$ could not be too large.
We note that in \cite{BK2}, the elliptic Harnack inequality for ${\mathcal L}$ was established under similar assumptions on the index function $\alpha(x)$.
Note that by \eqref{t1-1-9a} and \eqref{t1-1-4b}, when $\alpha(x)\equiv \alpha \in (0,2)$ for all $x\in \mathds R^d$, two-sided estimates of heat kernel in Theorem \ref{t1-2} are reduced
to those in \cite{CZ}.

\item[(2)] As mentioned in Remark \ref{remark1}(2), Theorem \ref{t1-2} indeed provides us some sufficient conditions
for the existence of a strong Markov process (in fact a Feller process having the strong Feller property)
associated with ${\mathcal L}$
when $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$. Note that, the existence of such
strong Markov process is required and assumed a prior in the proofs of
the H\"{o}lder continuity of harmonic functions in \cite{BK1} and
the elliptic Harnack inequality for ${\mathcal L}$ in \cite{BK2}.

 \end{enumerate}

nodes.statement:
\begin{itemize}
 \item[(1)] By carefully checking the arguments of Theorem \ref{t1-1}, one can see that Theorem \ref{t1-1} still holds true if the condition that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$ is replaced  by the following two assumptions on $\kappa(x,z)$:
\begin{itemize}
\item [(i)] For every fixed $x \in \mathds R^d$, $\kappa(x,\cdot):\mathds R^d \rightarrow \mathds R_+$
is a radial function, i.e., $\kappa(x,z)$ only depends on $|z|$.

\item [(ii)] Let $j(x,r)=\widetilde \kappa(x,r)r^{-d-\alpha(x)}$ for $x \in \mathds R^d$ and $r>0$, where
$\widetilde \kappa(x,r):=\kappa(x,z)$ with $|z|=r$. For every $x \in \mathds R^d$, $j(x,\cdot)$ is non-increasing and differentiable on $(0,\infty)$ such that the function $r\mapsto -\frac{1}{r}\frac{\partial j(x,r)}{\partial r}$ is non-increasing.
\end{itemize}

\item[(2)] Let $\widetilde {\mathcal L} f(x)={\mathcal L} f(x)+\langle b(x), \nabla f(x)\rangle$, where $b:\mathds R^d\rightarrow \mathds R^d$ is bounded and uniformly
H\"older continuous.
It is possible to extend Theorems \ref{t1-1} and \ref{t1-2}  to $\widetilde {\mathcal L}$ under the assumption that $\alpha_1>1$,
When $\alpha_1>1$, the gradient perturbation $\langle b(x), \nabla \rangle$ is of lower order than ${\mathcal L}$.
We  refer the readers to
\cite{BJ, CD, CH, JS, MM, MM1,XZ}
on heat kernel estimates associated
with non-local operators under gradient perturbation.
For heat kernel estimates associated
with non-local operators under non-local perturbations, see \cite{CW, W, CHXZ}.


\item[(3)] By combining with the approach from \cite{CZ4},
it is possible to remove the symmetry assumption of $\kappa (x, z)$ in $z$.
But we will not pursue this extension  in this paper.

\end{itemize}

nodes.statement:
By carefully checking the arguments of Theorem \ref{t1-1}, one can see that Theorem \ref{t1-1} still holds true if the condition that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$ is replaced  by the following two assumptions on $\kappa(x,z)$:
\begin{itemize}
\item [(i)] For every fixed $x \in \mathds R^d$, $\kappa(x,\cdot):\mathds R^d \rightarrow \mathds R_+$
is a radial function, i.e., $\kappa(x,z)$ only depends on $|z|$.

\item [(ii)] Let $j(x,r)=\widetilde \kappa(x,r)r^{-d-\alpha(x)}$ for $x \in \mathds R^d$ and $r>0$, where
$\widetilde \kappa(x,r):=\kappa(x,z)$ with $|z|=r$. For every $x \in \mathds R^d$, $j(x,\cdot)$ is non-increasing and differentiable on $(0,\infty)$ such that the function $r\mapsto -\frac{1}{r}\frac{\partial j(x,r)}{\partial r}$ is non-increasing.

nodes.name: Levi's method ansatz for $p$, $q$, $q_0$
nodes.statement:
According to the Levi's method (cf. \cite[pp.\ 310--311]{Fi}), we
look for the fundamental solution to \eqref{t1-1-1} of the following
form:
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
& p(t,x,y)=p^y(t,x-y)+\int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d}p^z(t-s,x-z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\,ds,
\end{split}
\end{equation}
where $q(t,x,y)$ solves
\begin{equation} q(t,x,y)=q_0(t,x,y)+\int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d}q_0(t-s,x,z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\,ds
\end{equation}
with
$
q_0(t,x,y)=( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y)p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y).
$

nodes.statement_short: Parametrix ansatz: $p=p^y+\int\int p^z q$, where $q$ solves an integral equation driven by $q_0=(\mathcal L^x-\mathcal L^y)p^y$.

nodes.name: Comparability notation $\asymp$, $\preceq$
nodes.statement:
For every measurable function $f,g:(0,1]\times\mathds R^d\times \mathds R^d \rightarrow \mathds R_+$, the notation $f \asymp g$ means that there exists a
constant $1\leqslant c_0<\infty$ such that $c_0^{-1} g(t,x,y)\leqslant f(t,x,y)\leqslant c_0 g(t,x,y)$ for every $(t,x,y) \in (0,1]\times\mathds R^d\times \mathds R^d $,  and the notation $f \preceq g$ (resp.\ $f \succeq g$)  means that there exists a
constant $0<c_1<\infty$ such that $f(t,x,y)\leqslant c_1 g(t,x,y)$ (resp.\ $f(t,x,y)\geqslant c_1g(t,x,y)$) for every $(t,x,y) \in (0,1]\times\mathds R^d\times \mathds R^d $.

nodes.name: Reference function $\rho_{\gamma,R}^{y,\beta}$
nodes.statement:
For each fixed $y \in \mathds R^d$, $\beta \in [0,\infty)$, $\gamma\in \mathds R$ and $R \in (0,\infty)$, we
define a function
$\rho_{\gamma,R}^{y,\beta}:(0,1]\times \mathds R^d \rightarrow (0,\infty)$ as follows
\begin{equation*}
\rho_{\gamma,R}^{y,\beta}(t,x):=t^{\gamma}\big(|x|^{\beta}\wedge 1\big)
\begin{cases}
 \big(t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}+|x|\big)^{-(d+\alpha(y))},&  |x|\leqslant R,\\
 |x|^{-(d+\alpha_1)},& |x|> R,
\end{cases}
\end{equation*} where $\alpha(x)$ is the index function in \eqref{e1-1} and $\alpha_1$
is the lower bound of $\alpha (x)$  in \eqref{e1-3}.
nodes.statement_short: $\rho_{\gamma,R}^{y,\beta}$ is $t^\gamma(|x|^\beta\wedge1)$ times a stable-like kernel of index $\alpha(y)$ inside radius $R$ and of index $\alpha_1$ outside.

nodes.name: Notation $\rho_{\gamma}^{y,\beta}$
nodes.statement:
Therefore, without loss of generality,
we may and do assume that $R=1$ in the definition of
$\rho_{\gamma,R}^{y,\beta},$ and we write
$\rho_{\gamma,1}^{y,\beta}$ as $\rho_{\gamma}^{y,\beta}$, which is exactly the one defined by
\eqref{e3-0}.

nodes.name: Local sup and inf of $\alpha$
nodes.statement:
For every $y \in \mathds R^d$ and $s>0$, define
$
\overline{\alpha}(y;s):=\sup\{\alpha(z): |z-y|\leqslant s\}$ and $  \underline{\alpha}(y;s):=\inf\{\alpha(z): |z-y|\leqslant s\}.
$

nodes.name: Notation $\overline{\alpha}(y;x)$
nodes.statement:
For simplicity, we write $\overline
\alpha(y;|x-y|)$ and $\underline{\alpha}(y;|x-y|)$ as $\overline{\alpha}(y;x)$ and $\underline{\alpha}(y;x)$, respectively.

For every $\beta \in [0,\alpha_2)$, $t \in (0,1]$ and $x \in \mathds R^d$,
\begin{equation} \int_{\mathds R^d}\rho_{0}^{z,\beta}(t,x-z)\,dz\preceq \big(t^{(\beta/\alpha(x))-1}\vee 1\big)\big(1+|\log t|\mathds 1_{\{\beta=\alpha(x)\}}\big)
\preceq t^{(\beta/\alpha_2)-1}\vee 1.
\end{equation}
nodes.name: Integral bound for $\rho_0^{z,\beta}$ with variable index
nodes.statement_short: The space integral of $\rho_0^{z,\beta}(t,x-z)$ in $z$ is at most $t^{\beta/\alpha_2-1}\vee1$ (with a log factor at $\beta=\alpha(x)$).
nodes.label: l3-1

nodes.name: Equation (2.1)
nodes.statement:
\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho_{0}^{z,\beta}(t,x-z)\,dz\preceq \big(t^{(\beta/\alpha(x))-1}\vee 1\big)\big(1+|\log t|\mathds 1_{\{\beta=\alpha(x)\}}\big)
\preceq t^{(\beta/\alpha_2)-1}\vee 1.
nodes.label: l3-1-1

nodes.statement:
Since $\beta\in (0,\alpha_2)$, it suffices to prove the first inequality in \eqref{l3-1-1}.

For every $x,z\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-z|\leqslant 1$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
|x-z|^{-\alpha(z)}&=|x-z|^{-\alpha(x)}|x-z|^{\alpha(x)-\alpha(z)}\preceq |x-z|^{-\alpha(x)}\cdot \exp\left(\left|\log|x-z|\right|\left|\alpha(x)-\alpha(z)\right|\right)\\
&\preceq |x-z|^{-\alpha(x)}\cdot \exp\left(C\left|\log|x-z|\right|\cdot |x-z|^{\beta_0}\right)
\preceq |x-z|^{-\alpha(x)},
\end{split}
\end{equation}
where in the last inequality we have used
$$\sup_{z\in \mathds R^d: |z|\leqslant 1}\exp\big(C|\log
|z||\cdot|z|^{\beta_0}\big)<\infty.$$
Then, for all $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,z\in \mathds R^d$,
\begin{align*}
\frac{1}{(t^{{1}/{\alpha(z)}}+|x-z|)^{d+\alpha(z)}}& \preceq
\begin{cases}
|x-z|^{-d-\alpha(z)},& |x-z|\leqslant 1,\\
t^{-1-({d/\underline{\alpha}(x; t^{1/\alpha_2})})},&  |x-z|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(x)}},
\end{cases}
\\
&\preceq
\begin{cases}
|x-z|^{-d-\alpha(x)},& |x-z|\leqslant 1,\\
t^{-1-({d/\underline{\alpha}(x; t^{1/\alpha_2})})},&  |x-z|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}.
\end{cases}
\end{align*}
Therefore, by the definition of $\rho_{0}^{z,\beta}$ (see \eqref{e3-0}), for all $t\in (0,1]$ and $x\in \mathds R^d$, we have
\begin{align*}
\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho_{0}^{z,\beta}(t,x-z)\,dz \preceq&
\int_{\{|z-x|> 1\}}\frac{1}{|x-z|^{d+\alpha_1}}\,dz +
\int_{\{t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}<|z-x|\leqslant 1\}}\frac{|x-z|^{\beta}}{|x-z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\
&+t^{-1-({d/\underline{\alpha}(x; t^{1/\alpha_2})})}\int_{\{|z-x|\leqslant t^{1/\alpha(x)}\}}
|x-z|^{\beta}\,dz\\
=&:J_1+J_2+J_3.
\end{align*}


It is easy to verify that $J_1\preceq 1$  and $J_2\preceq \big(t^{(\beta-\alpha(x))/{\alpha(x)}}\vee 1\big)
\big(1+|\log t|\mathds 1_{\{\beta=\alpha(x)\}}\big)$, due to the assumption that $\beta\in [0,\alpha_2)$.
At the same time,
\begin{align*}
J_3&\preceq t^{-1-({d/\underline{\alpha}(x; t^{1/\alpha_2}}))}\cdot t^{(\beta+d)/\alpha(x)} \preceq t^{(\beta-\alpha(x))/\alpha(x)}\exp\left(d|\log t| \frac{\alpha(x)-\underline{\alpha}(x;t^{{1/\alpha_2}}) }{\alpha(x)\underline{\alpha}(x;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})}\right) \\
&\preceq t^{(\beta-\alpha(x))/\alpha(x)}\exp\big(c|\log t| t^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}}\big)\preceq t^{{(\beta-\alpha(x))}/{\alpha(x)}},
\end{align*}
where in the forth inequality we have used
$$
\frac{\alpha(x)-\underline{\alpha}(x;t^{{1/\alpha_2}}) }{\alpha(x)\underline{\alpha}(x;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})}\preceq t^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}},
$$
 thanks to \eqref{e1-3}.
Combining all the estimates above, we get the first inequality in \eqref{l3-1-1}. The proof is complete.

nodes.statement_short: Compare $|x-z|^{-\alpha(z)}$ with $|x-z|^{-\alpha(x)}$ via Hölder continuity of $\alpha$, then split the integral into three regions and bound each.

nodes.name: Equation (2.2)

nodes.statement:
By the proof of \cite[Lemma 2.1(i)]{CZ}, we can obtain that for every $\beta \in [0,\alpha_2)$, $t \in (0,1]$ and $x \in \mathds R^d$,
\begin{equation} \int_{\mathds R^d}\rho_{0}^{x,\beta}(t,x-z)\,dz\preceq \big(t^{({\beta}/{\alpha(x)})-1}\vee 1\big)\big(1+|\log t|\mathds 1_{\{\beta=\alpha(x)\}}\big)\preceq t^{({\beta}/{\alpha_2})-1}\vee 1.
\end{equation}
Note that although the definition of $\rho^{x,\beta}_{0}(t,x)$ here is a little
different from that in \cite{CZ} when $|x|>1$, the proof of
\cite[Lemma 2.1]{CZ}  still works  for the first inequality in \eqref{l3-1-1-00}. We emphasize that in the present setting we
need  estimate \eqref{l3-1-1}, where in the integrand
$\rho^{z,\beta}_0$ the index $\alpha(z)$ depends on $z$.

nodes.statement:
For every $\gamma>0$, there exist constants $R_1:=R_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma)\in (0,{1}/{2})$ and $c_1:=c_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma)>0$ such that
for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y,w\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
&\big|\big( {\mathcal L}^x - {\mathcal L}^y\big)p^y(t,w)\big| \leqslant c_1\big(|x-y|^{\beta_0}\wedge 1\big)
\cdot
\begin{cases}
t^{-\gamma}\rho_0^{y,0}(t,w), &\ |w|\leqslant {1}/{2},\\
(t^{-\gamma}+|\log |w||)\rho_0^{y,0}(t,w),&\ |w|>{1}/{2}.
\end{cases}\end{split}
\end{equation} In particular, for every $t\in(0,1]$ and $x,y\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$,
\begin{equation} \big|q_0(t,x,y)\big|\preceq \rho_{-\gamma}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x-y).
\end{equation}

If, in addition, there are some $y_0\in \mathds R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(y_0)$ for all $z \in B(y_0,r_0)$,
then
there exists a constant
$c_2:=c_2(\alpha,\kappa, \gamma, r_0)>0$ such that for every $t\in(0,1]$ and $x \in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y_0|<r_0$,
\begin{equation} |q_0(t,x,y_0)|\leqslant c_2\big(|x-y_0|^{\beta_0}\wedge 1\big)\cdot
\frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(y_0)}}+|x-y_0|)^{d+\alpha(y_0)}}.
\end{equation}
nodes.name: Estimate of $(\mathcal L^x-\mathcal L^y)p^y$ near the diagonal
nodes.statement_short: For $|x-y|\le R_1$, $|(\mathcal L^x-\mathcal L^y)p^y(t,w)|\preceq(|x-y|^{\beta_0}\wedge1)t^{-\gamma}\rho_0^{y,0}(t,w)$, hence $|q_0|\preceq\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}$.
nodes.label: l1-2

|q_0(t,x,y_0)|\leqslant c_2\big(|x-y_0|^{\beta_0}\wedge 1\big)\cdot
\frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(y_0)}}+|x-y_0|)^{d+\alpha(y_0)}}.
nodes.label: l1-2-1b

nodes.statement:
(i)
Applying the mean value theorem to the function $r\mapsto a^r$, we find that for every $x,y,z \in \mathds R^d$ with
$|z|>0$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
&\bigg|\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}-\frac{\kappa(y,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\bigg|\\
&\preceq |\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|\bigg(\frac{|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|\leqslant 1\}}+
\frac{\log|z|}{|z|^{d+\underline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|> 1\}}\bigg)  +\frac{|\kappa(x,z)-\kappa(y,z)|}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\\
&\preceq \big(|x-y|^{\beta_0}\wedge
1\big)\bigg(\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline
\alpha(y;x)}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|\leqslant 1\}}+ \frac{1+\log|z|}{|z|^{d+\underline
\alpha(y;x)}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|> 1\}}\bigg),
\end{split}
\end{equation}
where in the last inequality we have used \eqref{e1-2}, \eqref{e1-3} and the
fact that
\begin{equation*}
\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\preceq \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\overline
\alpha(y;x)}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|\leqslant 1\}}+ \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\underline
\alpha(y;x)}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|> 1\}}.
\end{equation*}
Combining \eqref{e:pp} with \eqref{e2-3}, we can obtain that
\begin{align*}
 \big|\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)p^y(t,w)\big|
& \preceq
\big(|x-y|^{\beta_0}\wedge 1\big) \int_{\mathds R^d}|\delta_{p^y}(t,w;z)|\bigg(
\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|\leqslant 1\}}+\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\underline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|> 1\}}\bigg)\,dz\\
&\preceq\big(|x-y|^{\beta_0}\wedge 1\big)\cdot \big(I_1(t,x,y,w)+I_2(t,x,y,w)+\rho^{y,0}_1(t,w)I_3(t,x,y)\big),
\end{align*}
where in the second inequality we have used \eqref{p1-1-2}, and $I_1$, $I_2$ and $I_3$ are defined in \eqref{l1-1-0}.
Hence, Lemma \ref{l1-1} yields that
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
&\big|\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)p^y(t,w)\big|\\
&\preceq  \!\big(|x-y|^{\beta_0}\wedge 1\big) \!\cdot\!
\begin{cases}
(1+|\log t|)t^{1-({\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)})}\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w),\ \ &\ |w|\leqslant {1}/{2},\\
\big(1+|\log |w||+(1+|\log t|)t^{1-({\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)})}\big)\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w),\ \
&\ |w|>{1}/{2}.
\end{cases}
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Note that due to \eqref{e1-3},
\begin{equation*}
\overline{\alpha}(y;x)\leqslant \alpha(y)+c_0|x-y|^{\beta_0}\leqslant
\alpha(y)+c_0R_1^{\beta_0}\quad\textrm{ for all } x,y\in\mathds R^d\textrm{ with }|x-y|\leqslant R_1.
 \end{equation*}
Therefore, choosing $R_1\in(0,{1}/{2})$ small enough such that
$c_0R_1^{\beta_0} /\alpha_1 < \gamma$, we have
\begin{equation*}
(1+|\log t|)t^{1-({\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)})}\preceq t^{-\gamma}\quad\textrm{ when }|x-y|\leqslant R_1.
\end{equation*}
This, along with \eqref{l1-2-2}, immediately implies \eqref{l1-2-1}.


Estimate  \eqref{l1-2-1a} follows from \eqref{l1-2-1} by taking $w=x-y$.

\smallskip

(ii) Suppose, in addition, that  there are some $y_0\in\mathds R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such that
 $\alpha(x)=\alpha(y_0)$ for all $x \in B(y_0,r_0)$. Then \eqref{e:pp} is reduced to
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
&\bigg|\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}-\frac{\kappa(y_0,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y_0)}}\bigg|\preceq \big(|x-y|^{\beta_0}\wedge
1\big)\cdot\bigg(\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y_0)}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|\leqslant 1\}}+ \frac{1}{|z|^{d+
\alpha(y_0)}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|> 1\}}\bigg)
\end{split}
\end{equation*} for all $x\in B(y_0,r_0)$.
Having this at hand and repeating the same argument above, we can
easily see that the second assertion holds in this case.
nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.7
nodes.statement_short: Mean value theorem bounds the kernel difference by $|x-y|^{\beta_0}$ times log-weighted kernels; Lemma 2.3 then bounds the resulting integrals.

nodes.name: Equation (2.28)
nodes.statement:
\begin{split}
&\bigg|\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}-\frac{\kappa(y,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\bigg|\\
&\preceq |\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|\bigg(\frac{|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|\leqslant 1\}}+
\frac{\log|z|}{|z|^{d+\underline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|> 1\}}\bigg)  +\frac{|\kappa(x,z)-\kappa(y,z)|}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\\
&\preceq \big(|x-y|^{\beta_0}\wedge
1\big)\bigg(\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline
\alpha(y;x)}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|\leqslant 1\}}+ \frac{1+\log|z|}{|z|^{d+\underline
\alpha(y;x)}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|> 1\}}\bigg),
\end{split}
nodes.label: e:pp

nodes.name: Equation (2.29)
nodes.label: l1-2-2

nodes.statement:
Let $R_1=R_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma)$, where $R_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma)$ is the constant in
Lemma \ref{l1-2}. According to Lemma \ref{l1-2},  we only need to
treat the case that $|x-y|> R_1$.

(1)  We first assume that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$.


By \eqref{e2-3}, for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y \in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|>R_1$, we have
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
 | {\mathcal L}^x p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)|
& \preceq \int_{\{|z|\leqslant {R_1}/{2}\}}|\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)|\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\
&\quad +\int_{\{|z|>{R_1}/{2}\}} \big(p^y(t,x-y\pm z)+p^y(t,x-y)\big)\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\
&=:J_1+J_2.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Applying \eqref{p1-1-1} and using the mean value theorem, we can get
\begin{align*}
J_1&\preceq \int_{\{|z|\leqslant {R_1}/{2}\}}|\nabla^2 p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y+\theta_{x,y,z}z)||z|^{2-d-\alpha(x)}\, dz\\
&\preceq \int_{\{|z|\leqslant {R_1}/{2}\}}\frac{t}{(t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}+|x-y+\theta_{x,y, z}z|)^{d+\alpha(y)+2}}
|z|^{2-d-\alpha(x)}\, dz\\
&\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)+2}}\int_{\{|z|\leqslant
{R_1}/{2}\}}|z|^{2-d-\alpha(x)}\, dz\preceq
\frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)+2}}\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}=\rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y),
\end{align*}
where in the first inequality $\theta_{x,y,z}$ is a constant depending on
$x,y,z$ such that $|\theta_{x,y,z}|\leqslant 1$, and the third inequality follows
from the fact that $$|x-y+\theta_{x,y,z}z|\geqslant {|x-y|}/{2}\geqslant
{R_1}/{2} \geqslant C_0 t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}\quad\textrm{ for any } z\in \mathds R^d\textrm{ with } |z|\leqslant
{R_1}/{2}.$$
On the other hand, according to \eqref{p1-1-1-1-0} and \eqref{r1-1-1}, we have
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
J_2&\preceq \int_{\{|z|>{R_1}/{2}\}}\rho^{y,0}_1(t,x-y\pm z)\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz +
\rho^{y,0}_1(t,x-y) \int_{\{|z|>{R_1}/{2}\}}\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz \preceq  \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Hence, for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|>R_1$,
$$| {\mathcal L}^x p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)|\preceq\rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y).$$


Following the same argument above, we have for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|>R_1$,
\begin{equation} | {\mathcal L}^y p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)|\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}\preceq \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y).\end{equation}
Therefore, for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|>R_1$,
\begin{align*}
|q_0(t,x,y)|&\leqslant | {\mathcal L}^x p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)|+| {\mathcal L}^y p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)|\preceq
\rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y).
\end{align*}
By now we have shown the second case in the estimate \eqref{l2-1-2}.
From \eqref{l1-2-1b} and \eqref{l2-1-2}, we arrive at
\eqref{l2-1-33a} immediately.

(2) Now we suppose the general case that $\kappa(x,z)$ may depend on $z$. We still define $J_1$ and $J_2$ by those in \eqref{l2-1-3a}. It is not
difficult to verify that \eqref{e:ref1} also holds for this case.
On the other hand, according to \eqref{p1-1-2}, it holds that
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
J_1&\preceq \int_{\{|z|\leqslant {R_1}/{2}\}}\big[(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2)\wedge 1\big]\cdot\rho^{y,0}_1(t,x-y\pm z)\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\
&\quad +\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x-y)\int_{\{|z|\leqslant {R_1}/{2}\}}\big[(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2)\wedge 1\big]\cdot\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\
&\preceq\frac{t^{1-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}\int_{\{|z|\leqslant
t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}\}}|z|^{2-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz  +
\frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}\int_{\{t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}\leqslant |z|\leqslant {R_1}/{2}\}}|z|^{-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz\\
&\quad + \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}
\int_{\{|z|\leqslant {R_1}/{2}\}}\big[(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2)\wedge 1\big]|z|^{-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz\\
&\preceq \frac{t^{1-({\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)})}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}\leqslant  \frac{t^{1-(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Here the second step follows from
\begin{equation*}
\rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y+ z)\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}\quad\textrm{
when } |x-y|> R_1\textrm{ and }|z|\leqslant {R_1}/{2},
\end{equation*}
which is due to the fact that for $ |x-y|> R_1$ and $ |z|\leqslant {R_1}/{2}$
$$|x-y+ z| \geqslant |x-y|-|z|\geqslant  {|x-y|}/{2}\geqslant
{R_1}/{2}\geqslant C_0t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}.$$

Note also that \eqref{l2-1-4} is still true for this case. Combining all the estimates above, we obtain
\begin{align*}
|q_0(t,x,y)|&\preceq
| {\mathcal L}^x p^y(t,x-y)|+| {\mathcal L}^y p^y(t,x-y)| \preceq J_1+J_2+| {\mathcal L}^yp^y(t,x-y)|\preceq t^{1-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})}\rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y),
\end{align*}
where in the last step we used the fact that $t^{-{\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)}}\leqslant t^{-{\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1}}$ for all $t \in (0,1].$
Thus, the second case of \eqref{l2-1-1} is proved.
nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.5
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to $|x-y|>R_1$ via Lemma 2.7, then bound $\mathcal L^x p^y$ and $\mathcal L^y p^y$ separately using regularity of $p^y$, in both cases of $\kappa$.

nodes.name: Equation (2.30)
nodes.label: l2-1-3a

nodes.name: Equation (2.31)
nodes.label: e:ref1

nodes.label: l2-1-4

nodes.name: Equation (2.33)
nodes.label: l2-1-5

nodes.name: Pointwise upper bounds for $q_0$
nodes.statement_short: $|q_0|$ is at most $t^{-1-d/\alpha(y)}$ near the diagonal and $|x-y|^{-d-\alpha_2}\vee|x-y|^{-d-\alpha_1}$ off it.
nodes.label: p2-1

nodes.name: Equation (2.34)
nodes.label: p2-1-1

nodes.name: Equation (2.35)
nodes.label: p2-1-1a

nodes.statement:
(1) We first suppose that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$.

{\bf Case (a): $|x-y|\leqslant t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}.$}

According to \eqref{l1-2-1a}, we can choose $0<\gamma<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$ and adjust the constants properly to get that
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
|q_0(t,x-y)|&\preceq \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}(t,x-y)\preceq t^{-\gamma}|x-y|^{\beta_0}\cdot\rho^{y,0}_{0}(t,x-y)\\
&\preceq t^{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}\rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y)\preceq \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y)\preceq t^{-({d}/{\alpha(y)})-1},
\end{split}
\end{equation}
where in the third inequality we have used the fact that $|x-y|\leqslant t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}\leqslant t^{{1}/{\alpha_2}}$, and the
fourth inequality follows from $\gamma<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$.

{\bf Case (b): $|x-y|>t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}.$}

By \eqref{e2-3}, it holds that
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
| {\mathcal L}^x p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)|&
\preceq \int_{\{|z|\leqslant {|x-y|}/{2}\}}\left|
\delta_{p^y}\left(t,x-y;z\right)\right|\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\
&\quad +\int_{\{|z|> {|x-y|}/{2}\}}\left|
\delta_{p^y}\left(t,x-y;z\right)\right|\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\
&=:J_1+J_2.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Then, using the mean value theorem, we have
\begin{align*}
J_1&\preceq \int_{\{|z|\leqslant {|x-y|}/{2}\}}
\left|\nabla^2 p^y(t,x-y+\theta_{x,y,z} z)\right|\cdot |z|^2\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\
&\preceq \int_{\{|z|\leqslant {|x-y|}/{2}\}}
\frac{t}{\left(t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}+|x-y+\theta_{x,y,z} z|\right)^{d+\alpha(y)+2}}
\cdot |z|^{2-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz\\
&\preceq \frac{t}{\left(t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}+|x-y|\right)^{d+\alpha(y)+2}}
\int_{\{|z|\leqslant {|x-y|}/{2}\}} |z|^{2-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz\\
&\preceq \frac{|x-y|^{\alpha(y)}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)+2}}\cdot |x-y|^{2-\alpha(x)}\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}},
\end{align*}
where in the first inequality  $\theta_{x,y,z}$ is a constant depending on $x,y,z$ such that
$|\theta_{x,y,z}|\leqslant 1$, in the second inequality we have used \eqref{p1-1-1}, the third inequality follows
from the fact that $|x-y+\theta_{x,y,z} z|\geqslant |x-y|-|z|\geqslant {|x-y|}/{2}$, and the fourth inequality is due to
the fact that $t\leqslant |x-y|^{\alpha(y)}$.


On the other hand,
by \eqref{p1-1-2} and the fact that $|z|>{|x-y|}/{2}\geqslant t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2$, we have
$ \left|\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)\right|\preceq \rho^{y,0}_1(t,x-y\pm z)+\rho^{y,0}_1(t,x-y),$ and so \begin{align*}
J_2&\preceq  \int_{\{|z|>{|x-y|}/{2}\}}\!\!
\rho^{y,0}_1(t,x-y\pm z)\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz +
\rho^{y,0}_1(t,x-y)\int_{\{|z|>{|x-y|}/{2}\}}\!\!
\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz=:J_{21}+J_{22}.
\end{align*}
It holds that
\begin{align*}
J_{21}&\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}} \int_{\{|z|>{|x-y|}/{2}\}}\rho^{y,0}_1(t,x-y\pm z)\,dz\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\int \rho^{y,0}_1(t,x-y\pm z)\,dz\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}},
\end{align*}
where in the first inequality we have used following fact
$$ \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\quad\textrm{ for } |z|>{|x-y|}/{2},$$
and the last inequality follows from \eqref{l3-1-1-00}.
Furthermore, it is easy to verify that
\begin{align*}
J_{22}&\preceq \rho^{y,0}_1(t,x-y)
\int_{\{|z|>{|x-y|}/{2}\}}\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\, dz\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)+\alpha(y)}}\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}},
\end{align*} where in the last inequality we used $|x-y|\leqslant t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}$.

Combining all these estimates above, we arrive at
$$ \left| {\mathcal L}^xp^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)\right|\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}}.$$
Following the same arguments as above, we also have
$$ \left| {\mathcal L}^yp^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)\right|\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)}}.$$
Hence,
\begin{align*}
|q_0(t,x,y)|&\preceq
\left| {\mathcal L}^x p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)\right|+\left| {\mathcal L}^yp^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)\right|\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}}+\frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)}},
\end{align*}
from which we can get \eqref{p2-1-1} immediately.

(2) Next we consider the case that $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$.
With the estimate \eqref{l2-1-1} and the condition
${\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}>({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1$ at hand, we can follow the same argument as in \eqref{p2-1-2a} to verify the
upper bound in \eqref{p2-1-1a} for the case that $|x-y|\leqslant t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}$.

When $|x-y|>t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}$, we still define
$J_1$ and $J_2$ via \eqref{p2-1-2}. By carefully tracking the proof above, we find that the argument for the
estimates of $J_2$ in part (1) still works. So it remains to consider upper bound for
$J_1$.
According to \eqref{p1-1-2}, we have
\begin{align*}
J_1&\preceq \int_{\{|z|\leqslant {|x-y|}/{2}\}}
\big[\big(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\big)\wedge 1\big] \cdot
\big(\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x-y\pm z)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x-y)\big)\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\
&\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\int
\big[\big(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\big)\wedge 1\big] \cdot
\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\
&\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\cdot \bigg(\int_{\{|z|\leqslant t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}\}}
t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^{2-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz+\int_{\{|z|> t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}\}}|z|^{-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz\bigg)\\
&\preceq t^{1-({\alpha(x)}/{\alpha(y)})}\cdot \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\preceq t^{1-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})}\cdot \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)}},
\end{align*}
where the second inequality above follows from
$$ \rho^{y,0}_1(t,x-y\pm z)\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\quad\textrm{ for any }|z|\leqslant {|x-y|}/{2}.$$
Combining this with the estimate of $J_2$ in part (1) yields
\begin{align*}
|q_0(t,x,y)|&\preceq
\left| {\mathcal L}^x p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)\right|+\left| {\mathcal L}^xp^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)\right|\preceq t^{1-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})}\cdot \bigg(\frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}}+\frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\bigg),
\end{align*}
which implies that \eqref{p2-1-1a} holds for every $x,y \in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|>t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}$. The proof is complete.

(1)  According to the proofs of \cite[Lemma 2.1 (ii) and (iii)]{CZ}, we know that for $0\leqslant s\leqslant t\leqslant 1$, $x,y\in \mathds R^d$ and $\beta_1,\beta_2
\in (0,1)$, $\theta_1,\theta_2\in \mathds R$, it holds that
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
&\int_{\mathds R^d} \rho_{\theta_1}^{y,\beta_1}(t-s,x-z)\rho_{\theta_2}^{y,\beta_2}(s,z-y)\, dz\\
 &\preceq \Big[(t-s)^{\theta_1+[((\beta_1+\beta_2)/{\alpha(y)})\wedge 1]-1}s^{\theta_2}
 \big(1+|\log (t-s)|\mathds 1_{\{\beta_1+\beta_2=\alpha(y)\}}\big)\\
 &\qquad+(t-s)^{\theta_1}
s^{\theta_2 +[((\beta_1+\beta_2)/{\alpha(y)})\wedge 1]-1} \big(1+|\log s|\mathds 1_{\{\beta_1+\beta_2=\alpha(y)\}}\big)\Big]\rho_{0}^{y,0}(t,x-y)\\
&\qquad +(t-s)^{\theta_1+[({\beta_1}/{\alpha(y)})\wedge 1]-1}s^{\theta_2} \big(1+|\log (t-s)|\mathds 1_{\{\beta_1=\alpha(y)\}}\big)\rho_{0}^{y,\beta_2}(t,x-y)\\
&\qquad
+(t-s)^{\theta_1}s^{\theta_2+[({\beta_2}/{\alpha(y)})\wedge 1] -1} \big(1+|\log s|\mathds 1_{\{\beta_2=\alpha(y)\}}\big)\rho_0^{y,\beta_1}(t,x-y).
\end{split}
\end{equation} If, in addition, $\beta_1+\beta_2<\alpha(x)$, $({\beta_1}/{\alpha(y)})+\theta_1>0$ and $({\beta_2}/{\alpha(y)})+\theta_2>0$, then it also holds
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
&\int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{y,\beta_1}_{\theta_1}(t-s,x-z)
\rho^{y,\beta_2}_{\theta_2}(s,z-y)\,dz\,ds\\
&\preceq
\mathscr{B}\big(({\beta_1}/{\alpha(y)})+\theta_1,({\beta_2}/{\alpha(y)})+\theta_2\big)\\
&\quad \times \big(\rho^{y,0}_{\theta_1+\theta_2+(({\beta_1+\beta_2})/{\alpha(y)})} +\rho^{y,\beta_1}_{\theta_1+\theta_2+({\beta_2}/{\alpha(y)})}(t,x-y)
+\rho^{y,\beta_2}_{\theta_1+\theta_2+({\beta_1}/{\alpha(y)})}\big)(t,x-y).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Note that in \eqref{l3-2-1-} and \eqref{r3-2-1} the index $\alpha(y)$ is independent of the
integrand variable $z$. However, in the present setting we also need \eqref{l3-2-0} and \eqref{l3-2-1} as well as the
convolution inequalities \eqref{l3-3-0} and \eqref{l3-3-1}, where the index $\alpha(z)$ will
depend on the integrand variable $z$.


(2) For every fixed $\varepsilon>0$ small enough, $\gamma\in \mathds R$,
$\theta \in \mathds R_+$ and $x, y \in \mathds R^d$, define
\begin{equation} \tilde \rho_{\gamma,\varepsilon}^{y,\theta }(t,x)=t^{\gamma}(|x|^{\theta}\wedge
1)
\begin{cases}
\frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}+|x|)^{d+\alpha(y)}},&  |x|\leqslant 1,\\
\frac{1}{|x|^{d+\alpha_1-\varepsilon}},& |x|>1.
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
By carefully tracking the proofs of Lemma \ref{l3-1}, Lemma \ref{l3-2}, Corollary
\ref{l3-3} and  \cite[Lemma 2.1 (ii) and (iii)]{CZ}, we know that the inequalities \eqref{l3-1-1},
\eqref{l3-1-1-00},  \eqref{l3-2-0}, \eqref{l3-2-1}, \eqref{l3-3-0}, \eqref{l3-3-1},  \eqref{l3-2-1-} and \eqref{r3-2-1}
are valid with
$\rho$ replaced by $\tilde \rho$. (In particular, \eqref{l3-2-6} holds true.) For simplicity, in the remainder of this paper we often omit
the parameter $\varepsilon$ in $\tilde \rho$.

nodes.statement:
Without loss of generality, throughout the proof we will assume that $\beta_0< \alpha_2$ and $\beta_0^*=\beta_0$; otherwise, we will replace $\beta_0$ by $\beta_0^*.$


(i) According to \eqref{l2-1-2}, if $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$, then
$$|q_0(t,x,y)|\preceq \rho_{-\gamma}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x-y),\quad t\in(0,1] \textrm{ and } x,y \in \mathds R^d.$$
Therefore, by Corollary \ref{l3-3},
\begin{align*}|q_1(t,x,y)|\preceq&\int_0^t\int \rho_{-\gamma}^{z,\beta_0}(t-s,x-z) \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}(s,z-y)\,dz\,ds\\
\preceq& \mathscr{B}\big(({\widehat\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma, ({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma\big)
\big(\rho_{2(({\widehat
\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma+(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,\beta_0}\big)(t,x-y),\end{align*}
where $\widehat \beta_0:=\beta_0 \wedge (\alpha_2/2)$.


Suppose now that
$$|q_n(t,x,y)|\leqslant \omega_n\Big(\rho_{(n+1)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma+n(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y),\quad n\geqslant0,$$
where the constant $\omega_n$ is to be determined later.
Hence, according to Corollary \ref{l3-3} again,
\begin{align*}|q_{n+1}(t,x,y)|\leqslant& C\int_0^t\int \rho_{-\gamma}^{z,\beta_0}(t-s,x-z) \omega_n \Big(\rho_{(n+1)(({\widehat\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma+n(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(s,z-y)\,dz\,ds\\
\leqslant&C \omega_n \mathscr{B}(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma, (n+1)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)) \Big(\rho_{(n+2)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma+(n+1)(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y)\\
=&: \omega_{n+1}\Big(\rho_{(n+2)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma+(n+1)(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y), \end{align*} where $$ \omega_{n+1}= C \mathscr{B}\big(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma, (n+1)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)\omega_n ,$$
and $C$ is a constant independent of $t,n,x$ and $y$.
Note that $\omega_0\leqslant C$ and $\mathscr{B}(\gamma, \beta)=\frac{\Gamma(\gamma)\Gamma(\beta)}{\Gamma(\gamma+\beta)}$, where $\Gamma$ is the standard Gamma function. By iteration procedure we have
\begin{align*}\omega_n\leqslant &C^{n+1}\mathscr{B}\big(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma, n(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)\\
&\times\mathscr{B}\big(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma, (n-1)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)\cdots\mathscr{B}\big(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma, ({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma\big)\\
=&\frac{\big[C \Gamma(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma )\big]^{n+1}}{\Gamma\big((n+1)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)}.\end{align*}
Therefore,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
|q_n(t,x,y)|\leqslant &\frac{\big[C \Gamma(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma )\big]^{n+1}}{\Gamma\big((n+1)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)} \Big(\rho_{(n+1)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}
+\rho_{-\gamma+n(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y),\end{split}
\end{equation}
and so combing all estimates together
$$\sum_{n=0}^\infty |q_n(t,x,y)|\leqslant \left(\sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{\big[C \Gamma(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma )\big]^{n+1}}{\Gamma\big((n+1)(({\widehat\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)}\right)\Big(\rho_{2(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y),$$ which means that $q(t,x,y):=\sum_{n=0}^\infty q_n(t,x,y)$ is absolutely convergent, and
$$|q(t,x,y)|\leqslant C_1  \Big(\rho_{2(({\widehat\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y).$$
Thus, \eqref{p3-1-1} is proved by using the fact that $\beta_0\leqslant 2\widehat \beta_0$ and changing the constant $\gamma$ properly. From \eqref{eq3-1}
and the fact $q(t,x,y)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}q_n(t,x,y)$, it is easy to see that $q(t,x,y)$ solves the equation \eqref{eq2-2}.

(ii) Suppose that there are some $y_0\in \mathds R^d$ and $r\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(y_0)$ for all $z\in B(y_0,r_0)$.
According to \eqref{l2-1-33a}, it is easy to verify that for every $z \in \mathds R^d$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
|q_0(s,z,y_0)|&\preceq \big(|z-y_0|^{\beta_0}\wedge 1\big)\cdot
\begin{cases}
\frac{1}{(s^{{1/\alpha(y_0)}}+|z-y_0|)^{d+\alpha(y_0)}},& |z-y_0|\leqslant r_0,\\
\frac{1}{|z-y_0|^{d+\alpha_1}},&|z-y_0|> r_0
\end{cases}\\
&\preceq \rho^{y_0,\beta_0}_0(s,z-y_0).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
This along with the fact that $|q_0(t-s,x,z)|\preceq \rho^{z,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}(t-s,x-z)$ for every $x,z\in \mathds R^d$ yields that for all $x\in \mathds R^d$,
\begin{align*}
|q_1(t,x,y_0)|&\preceq \int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{z,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}(t-s,x-z)\rho^{y_0,\beta_0}_0(s,z-y_0)\,dz\,ds\\
&\leqslant C\mathscr{B}\big(({\widehat\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma,({ \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma\big)
\big(\rho^{y_0,0}_{({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})+(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}+\rho^{y_0,\beta_0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}\big)(t,x-y_0).
\end{align*}
Following the same arguments in part (i), we find that for every $n \geqslant 0$,
\begin{align*} |q_n(t,x,y_0)|
&\leqslant \frac{\big[C \Gamma(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma )\big]^{n+1}}{\Gamma\big((n+1)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)}
\Big(\rho_{({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})+n(({\widehat\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y_0,0}+\rho_{n(({ \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y_0,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y_0),\end{align*}
which implies $q(t,x,y):=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}q_n(t,x,y)$ is absolutely convergent and gives us \eqref{p3-1-2b} immediately.

(iii) It suffices to prove \eqref{p3-1-1a} for the case that $|x-x'|\leqslant R_1$  holds with some $R_1>0$, since the case
that $|x-x'|>1$ follows from \eqref{p3-1-1} immediately.
For any (fixed) $\varepsilon>0$ small enough, let $\tilde \rho^{y,\beta}_{\gamma}$ be defined by \eqref{p3-1-7}.  By \eqref{p3-1-1a-1}, we have
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
&|q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|\\
&\preceq (|x-x'|^{\tilde \theta}\wedge 1)\times \bigg[\left(\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x)})}\right)(t,x-y)  + \left(\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x')})}\right)(t,x'-y)\bigg],
\end{split}
\end{equation}
where $\tilde \theta:=\alpha_1(\beta_0-\alpha_2\theta)/{\alpha(x)}$. Since $\beta_0^*=\beta_0<\alpha(x)$, by  \eqref{e1-3} we can find a constant
$R_1>0$ small enough such that $\beta_0< \alpha(x)\wedge\alpha(x')$ for any $x'\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|\leqslant R_1$.
Then, according to \eqref{eq2-2}, it holds that
\begin{align*}
&|q(t,x,y)-q(t,x',y)|\\
&\leqslant |q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|+\int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d}
|q_0(t-s,x,z)-q_0(t-s,x',z)||q(s,z,y)|\,dz\,ds\\
&\preceq (|x-x'|^{\tilde \theta}\wedge 1)\\
&\quad\times\bigg\{ \Big[\big(\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x)})}\big)(t,x-y)
+ \left(\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x')})}\right)(t,x'-y)\Big]\\
&\quad \quad+\int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d} \Big[\big(\tilde \rho^{z,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{z,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x)})}\big)(t-s,x-z)\\
&\qquad\qquad\quad\qquad+ \big(\tilde \rho^{z,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{z,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x')})}
\big)(t-s,x'-z)\Big]
\Big[\big(
\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}\big)(s,z-y)\Big]\,dz\,ds \bigg\}\\
&\preceq (|x-x'|^{\tilde \theta}\wedge 1)\cdot\Big[\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-2\gamma
+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}(t,x-y)
+ \tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-2\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}(t,x'-y)\Big].
\end{align*}
Here the second inequality follows from \eqref{p3-1-1} and \eqref{p3-1-8a}, thanks to the fact that
$\beta_0< \alpha(x)\wedge \alpha(x')$, and the last inequality is due to Remark \ref{r3-3}(2) (which indicates that the convolution inequality \eqref{l3-3-0} holds for $\tilde \rho$) and the fact that $\gamma<\theta$.



(iv) Now we are going to prove the case that $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$.
Due to the assumption $({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1<{\beta_0^{**}}/{\alpha_2}$, we can choose $\gamma>0$ small enough such that
$\gamma+({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1=:\gamma_2 <{\beta_0^{**}}/{\alpha_2}$. Using \eqref{l2-1-1} and following the same arguments in part (i) with $\gamma_2 $ instead of $\gamma$, we can obtain that for
every $n\geqslant 1$ and $(t,x,y)\in (0,1]\times \mathds R^d \times \mathds R^d$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
|q_n(t,x,y)|\leqslant &\frac{\big[C \Gamma(({\beta_0^{**}}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma_2  )\big]^{n+1}}{\Gamma\big((n+1)(({\beta_0^{**}}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma_2 )\big)} \bigg(\rho_{(n+1)(({\beta_0^{**}}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma_2 )}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma_2 +n({\beta_0^{**}}/{\alpha_2}
-\gamma_2 )}^{y,\beta_0} \bigg)(t,x-y).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Using this and \eqref{l2-1-1}, we find immediately that $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}|q_n(t,x,y)|<\infty$ and so
\eqref{p3-1-2} is true.

Note that, according to Proposition \ref{p3-1-1a-p}(2), in this case \eqref{p3-1-8a} holds with
$\gamma_2$ in place of  $\gamma $. (Note that here $\beta_0$ is not replaced by $\beta_0^{**}$.) This along with \eqref{p3-1-2} and the same argument in (iii) gives us \eqref{p3-1-2a}.


(v) Suppose that the assumptions in part (2) of the Proposition hold, and that there are some $y_0\in \mathds R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(y_0)$ for all $z \in B(y_0,r_0)$. Then, using \eqref{l2-1-33} and repeating the arguments in part (ii) above,
we can prove \eqref{p3-1-2c}.

nodes.statement:
Without loss of generality, throughout the proof we still assume that $\beta_0< \alpha_2/2$ and $\beta_0^{**}=\beta_0$.

We first suppose that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$.
As in the proof of Proposition \ref{p3-1}(1), we know that
$q(t,x,y)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}q_n(t,x,y)$
is absolutely convergent. In particular, \begin{equation} |q(t,x,y)|\leqslant |q_0(t,x,y)|+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}|q_n(t,x,y)|.
\end{equation}
According to \eqref{p3-1-6a}, we have
\begin{align*}
 \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}|q_n(t,x,y)|
& \leqslant
 \left(\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{\big[C \Gamma(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big]^{n+1}}{\Gamma\big((n+1)(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)}
 \right)\Big(\rho_{3(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-2\gamma}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y) \preceq \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y),
\end{align*}
where in the last inequality we choose $\gamma>0$ small enough such that
$\gamma<{\beta_0}/({2\alpha_2})$.
Combining this estimate with \eqref{p2-1-1} and  \eqref{p3-1-9},  we obtain \eqref{p3-1-2e} immediately.

If $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and ${\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}>({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1$, then one can use \eqref{p2-1-1a} and follow
the same procedure above to prove \eqref{p3-1-2f}.

nodes.statement:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(1)] If $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$, then $p(t,x,y)$ is well defined by
\eqref{eq2-1}, and for every $\gamma,c_0>0$, there exist positive
constants $c_1:=c_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma,c_0)$ and $R_0:=R_0(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma,c_0)$ such that for any $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$,
\begin{equation} p(t,x,y)\leqslant
\begin{cases}
c_1t^{-{d/\alpha(x)}}, & |y-x|\leqslant c_0t^{{1/\alpha(x)}},\\
\frac{c_1t^{1-\gamma}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}},& c_0t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}\leqslant |y-x|\leqslant R_0,\\
\frac{c_1t^{1-\gamma}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}},&|y-x|> R_0.
\end{cases}
\end{equation} Suppose additionally that there are some $x_0 \in \mathds R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such that
$\alpha(z)=\alpha(x_0)$ for every $z \in B(x_0,r_0)$. Then we can
find a constant $c_2:=c_2(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma,r_0)>0$ such that for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $y \in
\mathds R^d$,
\begin{equation} p(t,x_0,y)\leqslant
\begin{cases}
\frac{c_2 t }{(t^{{1/\alpha(x_0)}}+|x_0-y|)^{d+\alpha(x_0)}},& |x_0-y|\leqslant {r_0}/{2},\\
\frac{c_2 t^{1-\gamma} }{|x_0-y|^{d+\alpha_1}},&|x_0-y|>{r_0}/{2}.
\end{cases}
\end{equation}


\item[(2)] If $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and $({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1<\min\{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2},1/2\}$, then $p(t,x,y)$ is well defined by
\eqref{eq2-1}, and for every $\gamma, c_0>0$, there exist constants
$c_1:=c_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma,c_0)$ and $R_0:=R_0(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma,c_0)$ such that for any $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$,
\begin{equation} p(t,x,y)\leqslant
\begin{cases}c_1t^{-{d/\alpha(x)}}, & |y-x|\leqslant c_0 t^{{1/\alpha(x)}},\\
\frac{c_1t^{1-\tilde\gamma}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}},& c_0 t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}\leqslant |y-x|\leqslant R_0,\\
\frac{c_1t^{1-\tilde\gamma }}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}},&|y-x|> R_0,
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
where $\tilde\gamma:=({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1+\gamma$. Suppose additionally there exist some
$x_0 \in \mathds R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(x_0)$ for
every $z \in B(x_0,r_0)$. Then, for any $c_0>0$, we can find a constant
$c_2:=c_2(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma,r_0,c_0)>0$ such that for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $y \in \mathds R^d$,
\begin{equation} p(t,x_0,y)\leqslant
\begin{cases}
{c_2}{t^{-{d/\alpha (x_0)}}},&\quad |y-x_0|< c_0t^{{1/\alpha(x_0)}},\\
\frac{c_2 t^{2-{(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}} }{|y-x_0|^{d+\alpha(x_0)}},& \quad
c_0t^{{1/\alpha(x_0)}}\leqslant |y-x_0|< {r_0}/{2},\\
\frac{c_2 t^{1-\tilde\gamma} }{|x-y_0|^{d+\alpha_1}},&\quad |y-x_0|\geqslant
{r_0}/{2}.
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
\end{itemize}

nodes.statement:
Without loss of generality, throughout this proof we will assume that $2\beta_0<\alpha_2$ and $\beta_0^{**}=\beta_0$; otherwise, we will replace $\beta_0$ by $\beta_0^{**}\in (0,\beta_0]\cap (0,{\alpha_2}/{2}).$ For simplicity, we only verify the case that $c_0=1$.

(i) We first consider the case that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$.
Note that $$p^z(t,x-z)\preceq \rho_1^{z,0}(t,x-z),\quad t\in (0,1],x,z\in \mathds R^d.$$ This, along with
\eqref{p3-1-1} and \eqref{l3-3-1}, yields that for every $(t,x,y)\in
(0,1]\times \mathds R^d \times \mathds R^d$ and {any constant
$0<\gamma<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2},$}
\begin{equation*}
\int_0^t \int_{\mathds R^d} p^z(t-s,x-
z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\,ds\preceq
\big(\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{1-\gamma}+
\rho^{y,0}_{1+({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}\big)\big(t,x-y\big).
\end{equation*}
Therefore, $p(t,x,y)$ is well defined by \eqref{eq2-1}, and
\begin{equation} p(t,x,y)\preceq \Big(\rho^{y,0}_1+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{1-\gamma}+
\rho^{y,0}_{1+({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}\Big)\big(t,x-y\big)\preceq
\big(\rho^{y,0}_1+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{1-\gamma}\big)\big(t,x-y\big).
\end{equation}

When $|x-y|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha_2}}$,
$$\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{1-\gamma}\big(t,x-y\big)\preceq t^{-\gamma}|x-y|^{\beta_0}\rho^{y,0}_1\big(t,x-y\big)
\preceq t^{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}\rho^{y,0}_1\big(t,x-y\big).$$
Hence, due to $\gamma<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$, we get
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
p(t,x,y)\preceq \rho^{y,0}_1\big(t,x-y\big)\preceq t^{-{d/\alpha(y)}}\preceq
t^{-{d}/{\overline{\alpha}(y;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})}}\preceq t^{-{d/\alpha(x)}},
\end{split}
\end{equation}
where the third inequality follows from \eqref{l3-2-8}.

Next, we will verify the other two cases in the upper bound \eqref{p3-2-1}. Observe that
for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ such that
$|x-y|\leqslant 1$ and $|z|\leqslant 1$,
\begin{align*}
 \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(y)}}
&=
\frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}t^{({1/\alpha(y)})-({1/\alpha(x)})}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(y)}}
 \preceq \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}t^{{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1^2}}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(y)}}\\
&\preceq \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}t^{{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1^2}}+|z|t^{{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1^2}})^{d+\alpha(y)}}\\
&=t^{-{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|(d+\alpha(y))}/{\alpha_1^2}}\cdot\frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}+|z|)^{\alpha(y)-\alpha(x)}}\cdot
\frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(x)}}\\
&\preceq t^{-{(d+\alpha_2)|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1^2}}\cdot
t^{-{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1}}\cdot
\frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(x)}} \preceq
\frac{t^{-C_1R_0^{\beta_0}}}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(x)}},
\end{align*}
where the second inequality we used
$t^{{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1^2}}\leqslant 1$, and the third inequality follows from the fact that for all $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ with $|z|\leqslant 1$,
\begin{align*}
\frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}+|z|)^{\alpha(y)-\alpha(x)}}\preceq t^{-{|\alpha(y)-\alpha(x)|}/{\alpha(x)}}.
\end{align*}
Thus, choosing $R_0:=R_0(\alpha,\gamma)$ small enough  such that
$C_1R_0^{\beta_0}<\gamma$ and using the definition of $\rho^{x,0}_0$, we can
get that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ with
$|x-y|\leqslant R_0$ and $|z|\leqslant 1$,
\begin{equation} \rho^{y,0}_0(t,z)\preceq t^{-\gamma}\rho^{x,0}_0(t,z).
\end{equation}
By the definition of \eqref{e3-0}, we know immediately that \eqref{l4-1-5} still holds for
every $|x-y|\leqslant R_0$ and $|z|> 1$. This is, \eqref{l4-1-5} holds for all $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_0$.

Hence, combining \eqref{p3-2-3}, \eqref{p3-2-3a} with \eqref{l4-1-5} and changing the constant $\gamma$ properly, we find that
\begin{align*}
p(t,x,y)&\preceq
 \big(\rho^{y,0}_{1}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{1-\gamma}
\big)\big(t,x-y\big)\preceq \begin{cases}t^{-{d/\alpha(x)}}, & |y-x|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(x)}},\\
\frac{t^{1-\gamma}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}},& t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}\leqslant |y-x|\leqslant R_0,\\
\frac{t^{1-\gamma}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}},&|y-x|> R_0.
\end{cases}
\end{align*}

(ii) If there are some $x_0 \in \mathds R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such
that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(x_0)$ for all $z \in B(x_0,r_0)$, then for
every $y \in B(x_0,{r_0}/{2})$ and $z \in
B(y,{r_0}/{2})$,
$
\alpha(z)=\alpha(y)=\alpha(x_0).
$
Hence, by \eqref{p3-1-2b}, we have
\begin{equation*}
|q(t,x,y)|\preceq
\Big(\rho^{y,0}_{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_0\Big)(t,x-y)\quad\textrm{ for all }
x\in \mathds R^d\textrm{ and }y \in B\big(x_0,{r_0}/{2}\big).
\end{equation*}
Based on the inequality above, the computation in part (i) is valid
with $\gamma=0$ for $x=x_0$ and $y \in B(x_0,{r_0}/{2})$, which
proves \eqref{p3-2-2} for the case that $y \in
B(x_0,{r_0}/{2})$. The upper bound for the case
$|y-x_0|>{r_0}/{2}$ is just the same as that of \eqref{p3-2-1}.


(iii) If $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and
${(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}-1<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$, then, according to
\eqref{p3-1-2}, we know that the computation in part (i) holds with
$\gamma$ replaced by $\tilde\gamma$. Thus, following the argument in part
(i), we can obtain \eqref{p3-2-1a}. Similarly as in (ii),
\eqref{p3-2-2a} could be verified by using \eqref{p3-1-2c}.

nodes.label: l4-1-5

nodes.statement:
The estimate \eqref{p3-2-2} indicates that if $\alpha(x)$ is a
constant $\alpha\in(0,2)$ locally, then we can get a upper bound for
$p(t,x,y)$ which is also locally comparable with that for the heat
kernel of rotationally symmetric $\alpha$-stable process.  In particular, when
$\alpha(x)\equiv\alpha$ for all $x \in \mathds R^d$, \eqref{p3-2-2a} coincides with
the upper bound given in \cite[Therem 1.1]{CZ}.

nodes.statement:
We write  $ {\mathcal L}^y={\mathcal L}_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}^y+{\mathcal L}_{\widehat \kappa}^y$ with
\begin{align*}
{\mathcal L}_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}^y f(x)&=\frac{1}{2}\int_{\mathds R^d}\delta_{f}(x;z)\frac{\kappa_1}{2}\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\,dz,\quad f\in C_c^2(\mathds R^d),\\
{\mathcal L}_{\widehat \kappa}^y f(x)&=\frac{1}{2}\int_{\mathds R^d}\delta_{f}(x;z)\frac{\widehat \kappa(y,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\,dz,\quad f\in C_c^2(\mathds R^d),
\end{align*}
where $\kappa_1>0$ is the constant in \eqref{e1-2}, $\widehat \kappa(y,z):=\kappa(y,z)-\kappa_1/2$ and
$$\delta_f(x;z)=f(x+z)+f(x-z)-2f(x).$$ Then, we have
\begin{equation} p^y(t,x)=\int_{\mathds R^d}p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(t,x-z)p^y_{\widehat \kappa}(t,z)\,dz,\ \ x\in \mathds R^d, t\in (0,1],
\end{equation}
where $p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}$ and $p^y_{\widehat \kappa}$ denote the fundamental solutions (i.e.\ heat kernel) associated with
the operators ${\mathcal L}_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}^y$ and ${\mathcal L}_{\widehat \kappa}^y$, respectively.

We first show that \eqref{l4-4-1} holds for $p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}$. Indeed, for every $x,x'\in \mathds R^d$ such that $|x-x'|\leqslant 1$,
\begin{align*}
\big|\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(1,x)-\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(1,x')\big|&=
\left|\int_0^1 \frac{d}{d \theta}\left(\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}
\left(1,x+\theta(x'-x)\right)\right)\,d\theta\right|\\
&\leqslant |x-x'|\cdot\int_0^1 \left|\nabla^2 p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}
\left(1,x+\theta(x'-x)\right)\right|\,d\theta\\
&\preceq |x-x'|\cdot \int_0^1 \left(1+\left|x+\theta(x'-x)\right|\right)^{-d-\alpha(y)-2}\,d\theta\\
&\preceq |x-x'|\cdot \left(1+|x|\right)^{-d-\alpha(y)-2},
\end{align*}
where in the third inequality we have used \eqref{p1-1-1}, and the last inequality is due to
the fact that for all $\theta\in [0,1]$ and $x,x'\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|\leqslant 1$
\begin{equation*}
\left(1+\left|x+\theta(x'-x)\right|\right)^{-1}\preceq \left(1+|x|\right)^{-1}.
\end{equation*}
Also by \eqref{p1-1-1}, we have that for every
$x,x'\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|>1$,
\begin{align*}
\big|\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(1,x)-\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(1,x')\big|&
\leqslant \big|\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(1,x)\big|+
\big|\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(1,x')\big|\\
&\preceq (1+|x|)^{-d-\alpha(y)-1}+
(1+|x'|)^{-d-\alpha(y)-1}.
\end{align*}
Combining both estimates above yields that for all $x,x'\in \mathds R^d$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
\big|\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(1,x)-\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(1,x')\big|
\preceq &\left(|x-x'|\wedge 1\right)\left(
(1+|x|)^{-d-\alpha(y)}+
(1+|x'|)^{-d-\alpha(y)}\right).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Since the Markov process $(X_t^{y,{\kappa_1}/{2}})_{t\geqslant0}$ associated with
$ {\mathcal L}^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}$ is a constant time-change of standard rotationally invariant $\alpha(y)$-stable process, by
the scaling property, for all $t>0$ and $x \in \mathds R^d$,
$$
 p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(t,x)= t^{-d/\alpha(y)} p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(1,t^{-1/\alpha(y)}x).
$$
This along with \eqref{l4-4-3} yields that for all $x,x'\in \mathds R^d$ and $t\in (0,1]$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
\big|\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(t,x)-\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(t,x')\big|
\preceq &\left[\left(t^{-1/\alpha(y)}|x-x'|\right)\wedge 1\right]\left(
\rho_{1-(1/\alpha(y))}^{y,0}(t,x)+\rho_{1-(1/\alpha(y))}^{y,0}(t,x')\right).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Therefore,  for every $x,x'\in \mathds R^d$ and $t\in (0,1]$,
\begin{align*}
&\left|\nabla p^y(t,x)-\nabla p^y(t,x')\right|\\
&=\left|\int_{\mathds R^d}\big(\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(t,x-z)-\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(t,x'-z)\big)
\cdot p^y_{\widehat \kappa}(t,z)\,dz\right|\\
&\leqslant \int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(t,x-z)-\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(t,x'-z)\big|
\cdot p^y_{\widehat \kappa}(t,z)\,dz\\
&\preceq \left[\left(t^{-1/\alpha(y)}|x-x'|\right)\wedge 1\right]\cdot
\Bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{y,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(y))}(t,x-z)\rho^{y,0}_1(t,z)\,dz+\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{y,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(y))}(t,x'-z)\rho^{y,0}_1(t,z)\,dz\Bigg)\\
&\preceq  \left[\left(t^{-1/\alpha(y)}|x-x'|\right)\wedge 1\right]\cdot
\left(\rho^{y,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(y))}(t,x)
+\rho^{y,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(y))}(t,x')\right),
\end{align*}
where the equality above is due to \eqref{l4-4-2}, the second inequality follows from
\eqref{l4-4-4} and \eqref{p1-1-1-1-0}, and in the last inequality we have used
\eqref{l3-2-1-}. By now we have finished the proof.

nodes.label: l4-1-1a

nodes.statement:
(i) Note that for all $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y,z \in \mathds R^d$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
 p^x(t,z)-p^y(t,z)
&=\int_0^t \frac{d}{ds}\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}p^x(s,w)p^y(t-s,z-w)\,dw\bigg)\,ds\\
&=\int_0^t \bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\big( {\mathcal L}^x p^x(s,w)\,p^y(t-s,z-w) -p^x(s,w)\, {\mathcal L}^y
p^y(t-s,z-w)\big)\,dw\bigg)\,ds\\
&=\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big) p^x(s,w)\,p^y(t-s,z-w)\,dw\,ds\\
&\quad +\int_{{t}/{2}}^t\int_{\mathds R^d} p^x(s,w)\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)
p^y(t-s,z-w)\,dw\,ds\\
&=\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big) p^x(s,w)
\big(p^y(t-s,z-w)-p^y(t-s,z)\big)\,dw\bigg)\,ds\\
&\quad +\int_{{t}/{2}}^t\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d} \big(p^x(s,w)-p^x(s,z)\big) \big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)
p^y(t-s,z-w)\,dw\bigg)\,ds\\
&=:J_1+J_2.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Here, the first equality is due to the following estimate which we will verify later
\begin{equation*}
\int_0^t \left|\frac{d}{ds}\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}p^x(s,w)p^y(t-s,z-w)\,dw\bigg)\,\right|ds<\infty.\end{equation*}
By estimates for $p^x(\cdot, \cdot)$ and $p^y(\cdot, \cdot)$ in Lemma \ref{p1-1},
we can change the order of derivatives and integrals in the second equality. The third and the fourth equalities above follow from the
following facts respectively
\begin{align*}
\int_{\mathds R^d}  {\mathcal L}^x f(z_1) g(z_1) \,dz_1=\int_{\mathds R^d} f(z_1)  {\mathcal L}^x g(z_1) \,dz_1,\quad f,g \in C_c^{\infty}(\mathds R^d),
\end{align*}
\begin{align*}
\int_{\mathds R^d}  {\mathcal L}^y f(z_1) g(z_1)\, dz_1=\int_{\mathds R^d} f(z_1)  {\mathcal L}^y g(z_1) \, dz_1, \quad f,g \in C_c^{\infty}(\mathds R^d)
\end{align*} and
\begin{align*}
\int_{\mathds R^d}  {\mathcal L}^x f(z_1)\,dz_1=\int_{\mathds R^d}  {\mathcal L}^y f(z_1)\,dz_1=0,\quad f \in C_c^{\infty}(\mathds R^d).
\end{align*}
Note that, also due to estimates for $p^x(\cdot, \cdot)$ and $p^y(\cdot, \cdot)$,  the equalities above are still true for $p^x(t,\cdot)$ and $p^y(t,\cdot)$.

By Lemma \ref{l1-2}, for any $\gamma>0$ there is a constant $R_0:=R_0(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma)\in(0,1)$ such that for all $t\in(0,1]$ and $x,y,w\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_0$,
\begin{equation} \big|\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)p^x(t,w)\big|\preceq (|x-y|^{\beta_0}\wedge 1)\cdot\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-\gamma}(t,w).
\end{equation}
On the other hand, for any $\theta \in (0,1)$ and $\gamma\in (0,1)$, there exists a
constant $R_1:=R_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma)\in(0,R_0)$ such that for all
 $x,y,z\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$, $0<s\leqslant t\leqslant1$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
 \big|p^y(t-s,z-w)-p^y(t-s,z)\big|
&\preceq \big[\big((t-s)^{-{1/\alpha(y)}}|w|\big)\wedge 1\big]\cdot
\big[\rho^{y,0}_1(t-s,z-w)+\rho^{y,0}_1(t-s,z)\big]\\
&\preceq \big[\big((t-s)^{-{1/\alpha(y)}}|w|\big)^{\theta}\wedge 1\big]\cdot
\big[\rho^{y,0}_1(t-s,z-w)+\rho^{y,0}_1(t-s,z)\big]\\
&\preceq \big[\big((t-s)^{-{1}/{\alpha_1}}|w|\big)^{\theta}\wedge 1\big]\cdot
\big[\rho^{x,0}_{1-\gamma}(t-s,z-w)+\rho^{x,0}_{1-\gamma}(t-s,z)\big]\\
&\preceq \big(|w|^{\theta}\wedge 1\big)\cdot
\big[\rho^{x,0}_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t-s,z-w)+\rho^{x,0}_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t-s,z)\big],
\end{split}
\end{equation}
where the first inequality follows from \eqref{p1-1-3} and in the third inequality we have used \eqref{l4-1-5}.

Next, we choose $\theta\in(0,1\wedge \alpha_1)$ and $0<\gamma<({\theta}/{\alpha_2})\wedge ((1-({\theta}/{\alpha_1}))/2)$. Then, according to
\eqref{l4-1-4} and \eqref{l4-1-6}, for any $t\in(0,1]$ and $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$,
\begin{align*}
J_1&\preceq |x-y|^{\beta_0}\cdot\bigg(\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{x,\theta}_{-\gamma}(s,w)\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t-s,z-w)\,dw\,ds\\
&\qquad\qquad \qquad +\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{x,\theta}_{-\gamma}(s,w)
\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t-s,z)\,dw\,ds\bigg)\\
&=:|x-y|^{\beta_0}\cdot \big(J_{11}+J_{12}\big).
\end{align*}
As mentioned in Remark \ref{r3-3}(2), \eqref{r3-2-1} holds for $\tilde \rho$, from which we can obtain that
\begin{equation*}
J_{11}\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{1-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,z).
\end{equation*}
At the same time, observe that for every $0<s<{t}/{2}$,
\begin{equation*}
\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t-s,z)\preceq \tilde
\rho^{x,0}_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,z),
\end{equation*}
then we have
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
J_{12}&\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,z)
\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{x,\theta}_{-\gamma}(s,w)\,dw\,ds \\
&\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,z) \int_0^{{t}/{2}}s^{-1-\gamma+({\theta}/{\alpha_2})}\,ds \preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{1-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,z),
\end{split}
\end{equation}
where in the second inequality we used the fact that \eqref{l3-1-1-00} is true for $\tilde \rho$, see again
Remark \ref{r3-3}(2).
By both estimates for $J_{11}$ and $J_{12}$, we get that for any $t\in(0,1]$ and $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$,
\begin{equation*}
J_1 \preceq |x-y|^{\beta_0}\cdot\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{1-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,z).
\end{equation*}
 For $J_2$, we need to handle the singularity near $s=t$. As the same way as before, we can obtain that for all $t\in (0,1]$ and
$x,y,z,w\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$,
\begin{align*}
\big|\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)p^y(t-s,z-w)\big|
&\preceq \big(|x-y|^{\beta_0}\wedge 1\big)\cdot\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{-\gamma}(t-s,z-w)\preceq \big(|x-y|^{\beta_0}\wedge 1\big)\cdot \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-2\gamma}(t-s,z-w)\end{align*} and
\begin{align*}
\big|p^x(s,w)-p^x(s,z)\big|\preceq \big(|z-w|^{\theta}\wedge 1\big) \cdot\big(\rho^{x,0}_{1-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(s,z)+\rho^{x,0}_{1-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(s,w)\big).
\end{align*}
Using both estimates above and following the same argument as that for $J_1$, we can get that  for any $t\in(0,1]$ and $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$, $$J_2 \preceq
|x-y|^{\beta_0}\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{1-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,z).$$ Then, \eqref{l4-1-1} is proved.

(ii) Following the  argument of  \eqref{l4-1-2}, we can verify that
for all $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y,z \in \mathds R^d$,
\begin{align*}
&\nabla p^x(t,z)-\nabla p^y(t,z)\\
&=\int_0^t \frac{d}{ds}\left(\int_{\mathds R^d}
\nabla p^x(s,w)p^y(t-s,z-w)\,dw\right)\,ds\\
&=\int_0^t\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\Big( {\mathcal L}^x p^x(s,w)\nabla p^y(t-s,z-w) -\nabla p^x(s,w)\, {\mathcal L}^y
p^y(t-s,z-w)\Big)\,dw\bigg)\,ds\\
&=\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big) p^x(s,w)\,\nabla p^y(t-s,z-w)\,dw\,ds\\
&\quad +\int_{{t}/{2}}^t\int_{\mathds R^d} \nabla p^x(s,w)\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)
p^y(t-s,z-w)\,dw\,ds\\
&=\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big) p^x(s,w)
\big(\nabla p^y(t-s,z-w)-\nabla p^y(t-s,z)\big)\,dw\bigg)\,ds\\
&\quad +\int_{{t}/{2}}^t\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d} \big(\nabla p^x(s,w)-\nabla p^x(s,z)\big)  \big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)
p^y(t-s,z-w)\,dw\bigg)\,ds\\
&=:I_1+I_2,
\end{align*} where in the first and the second equalities we used the integration by part formula
and  in the second equality we also used the fact that $\nabla  {\mathcal L}^x p^y(t,w)= {\mathcal L}^x \nabla p^y(t,w)$.

Observe that
$$
t^{-d/\alpha(y)}\leqslant t^{-d/\alpha(x)}t^{-\big|\frac{d}{\alpha(y)}-\frac{d}{\alpha(x)}\big|}\leqslant
t^{-d/\alpha(x)}t^{-\frac{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(z)|}{\alpha_1^2}}\leqslant t^{-d/\alpha(x)}t^{-C|x-z|^{\beta_0}}.
$$
Then, according to \eqref{l4-4-1} and the proof of \eqref{l4-1-6},
for any $\theta \in (0,1)$, $\gamma\in (0,1)$, there exists a
constant $R_1:=R_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma)\in(0,R_0)$ such that for all $0<t \leqslant 1$ and
 $x,y\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
&\left|\nabla p^y(t,z-w)-\nabla p^y(t,z)\right|\\
&\preceq \big(|w|^{\theta}\wedge 1\big)\cdot
\big[\rho^{x,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x))-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,z-w)+\rho^{x,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x))-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,z)\big].
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Choosing $\theta\in(0,1\wedge \alpha_1)$ and $0<\gamma<({\theta}/{\alpha_2})\wedge ((1-({\theta}/{\alpha_1}))/2)$, and using
\eqref{l4-1-4} and \eqref{l4-1-7}, we arrive at that for any $t\in(0,1]$ and $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$,
\begin{align*}
I_1&\preceq |x-y|^{\beta_0}\cdot\bigg(\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{x,\theta}_{-\gamma}(s,w)\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x))-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t-s,z-w)\,dw\,ds\\
&\qquad\qquad \qquad\quad +\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{x,\theta}_{-\gamma}(s,w)
\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x))-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t-s,z)\,dw\,ds\bigg)\\
&=:|x-y|^{\beta_0}\cdot \big(I_{11}+I_{12}\big).
\end{align*}
Noticing that, by Remark \ref{r3-3}(2),  \eqref{l3-2-1-} still holds for $\tilde \rho$, we have
\begin{align*}
I_{11}&\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_0(t,z)\int_0^{t/2}
\Big(s^{-\gamma}(t-s)^{-(1/\alpha(x))-\gamma-(\theta/\alpha_1)}+s^{-1+\theta/\alpha_2-\gamma}(t-s)^{1-(1/\alpha(x))-\gamma-(\theta/\alpha_1)}\Big)\,ds\\
&\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_0(t,z) \cdot t^{1-(1/\alpha(x))-2\gamma-(\theta/\alpha_1)}\preceq
 \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x))-2\gamma-(\theta/\alpha_1)}(t,z).
\end{align*}
On the other hand, following the argument of  \eqref{l4-1-8}, we can obtain that
\begin{align*}
I_{12}&\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x))-\gamma-(\theta/\alpha_1)}(t,z)\cdot\int_0^{t/2}
\int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{x,\theta}_{-\gamma}(s,w)\,dw\,ds\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x))-2\gamma-(\theta/\alpha_1)}(t,z).
\end{align*}

By the same argument as that for $I_1$, we can also obtain that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and
$x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$,
\begin{equation*}
I_2\preceq |x-y|^{\beta_0}\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x))-2\gamma-(\theta/\alpha_1)}(t,z).
\end{equation*}
Combining all estimates together, we have shown
\eqref{l4-1-1-1}.

(iii) Following the same procedure as these of \eqref{l4-1-1} and \eqref{l4-1-1-1}, we can also
verify \eqref{l4-1-1a}.

nodes.statement:
\begin{split}
 p^x(t,z)-p^y(t,z)
&=\int_0^t \frac{d}{ds}\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}p^x(s,w)p^y(t-s,z-w)\,dw\bigg)\,ds\\
&=\int_0^t \bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\big( {\mathcal L}^x p^x(s,w)\,p^y(t-s,z-w) -p^x(s,w)\, {\mathcal L}^y
p^y(t-s,z-w)\big)\,dw\bigg)\,ds\\
&=\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big) p^x(s,w)\,p^y(t-s,z-w)\,dw\,ds\\
&\quad +\int_{{t}/{2}}^t\int_{\mathds R^d} p^x(s,w)\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)
p^y(t-s,z-w)\,dw\,ds\\
&=\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big) p^x(s,w)
\big(p^y(t-s,z-w)-p^y(t-s,z)\big)\,dw\bigg)\,ds\\
&\quad +\int_{{t}/{2}}^t\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d} \big(p^x(s,w)-p^x(s,z)\big) \big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)
p^y(t-s,z-w)\,dw\bigg)\,ds\\
&=:J_1+J_2.
\end{split}

nodes.statement:
For simplicity, we assume that $\beta_0< {\alpha_2}/{2}$ and $\beta_0^{**}=\beta_0$ as before.

(1) We first suppose that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$. According
to  \eqref{p1-1-3}, for any $\gamma>0$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
&\big|p^z(t-s,x-z)-p^z(t-s,x'-z)\big|\\
&\preceq \big[\big((t-s)^{-{1}/{\alpha(z)}}|x-x'|\big)\wedge 1\big]\cdot
\big[\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x-z)+\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x'-z)\big]\\
&\preceq
\big[\big((t-s)^{-{1}/{\alpha(z)}}|x-x'|\big)^{(\alpha(x)-\gamma)_+\wedge
1}\wedge 1\big]
\big[\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x-z)+\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x'-z)\big]\\
&\preceq |x-x'|^{(\alpha(x)-\gamma)_+\wedge
1}(t-s)^{-{(\alpha(x)-\gamma)_+}/{\alpha(z)}}
\times\big[\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x-z)+\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x'-z)\big].
\end{split}
\end{equation}

On the one hand, observing that
$$\frac{\alpha(x)-\gamma}{\alpha(z)}\leqslant 1+\frac{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(z)|}{\alpha_1}-\frac{\gamma}{\alpha_2}\leqslant
1+\frac{C|x-z|^{\beta_0}}{\alpha_1}-\frac{\gamma}{\alpha_2},$$ we can find a constant
$R_2:=R_2(\alpha,\gamma)>0$ such that for every $x,x',z\in \mathds R^d$ satisfying
$|x-x'|\leqslant R_2$ and $|x-z|\leqslant 2R_2$ (which imply that $|x'-z|\leqslant
3R_2$), it holds
\begin{equation*}
\frac{\alpha(x)-\gamma}{\alpha(z)}\leqslant 1-\frac{2\gamma}{3\alpha_2},
\end{equation*}
which in turn yields that for every $0<s\leqslant t\leqslant 1$ and $x,x',z\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|\leqslant
R_2$ and $|x-z|\leqslant 2R_2$
\begin{align*}
\big|p^z(t-s,x-z)-p^z(t-s,x'-z)\big|
&\preceq
|x-x'|^{(\alpha(x)-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}\left(\rho^{z,0}_{{2\gamma}/({3\alpha_2})}(t-s,x-z)+\rho^{z,0}_{{2\gamma}/({3\alpha_2})}(t-s,x'-z)\right).
\end{align*}

On the other hand, when $|x-x'|\leqslant R_2$ and $|z-x|>2R_2$ (which
imply that $|z-x'|>R_2$), we obtain from \eqref{p1-1-1} and the mean
value theorem that
\begin{align*}
|p^z(t-s,x-z)-p^z(t-s,x'-z)|
&\leqslant |x-x'|\cdot|\nabla p^z(t-s,x-z+\tilde \theta_{x,x',z}(x'-x))|\\
&\preceq |x-x'|\cdot \frac{t-s}{((t-s)^{{1}/{\alpha(z)}}+|x-z|)^{d+\alpha(z)+1}}\\
&\preceq |x-x'|\cdot \frac{t-s}{|x-z|^{d+\alpha_1}}\preceq |x-x'|\cdot \rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x-z).
\end{align*}
where in the first inequality $|\tilde \theta_{x,x'z}|\leqslant 1$ is a
constant (which may depend on $x$, $x'$ and $z$), in the second inequality
we have used the fact that
$$|x-z+\tilde \theta_{x,x',z}(x'-x)|\geqslant |x-z|-|x'-x|\geqslant {|x-z|}/{2},$$
and the fourth inequality follows from
$|z-x|>R_2>C(t-s)^{{1}/{\alpha(z)}}$.

As a result, we obtain that for all $x,x',z\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|\leqslant R_2$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
\big|p^z(t,x-z)-p^z(t,x'-z)\big|
&\preceq
|x-x'|^{(\alpha(x)-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}\Big(\rho^{z,0}_{{2\gamma}/({3\alpha_2})}(t,x-z)
+\rho^{z,0}_{{2\gamma}/({3\alpha_2})}(t,x'-z)\Big).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Then, using \eqref{p3-1-1} and \eqref{l3-3-1} and changing the constant $\gamma$ properly, we arrive at for every
$|x-x'|\leqslant R_2$,
\begin{align*}
&\int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d}|p^z(t-s,x-z)-p^z(t-s,x'-z)||q(s,z,y)|\,dz\,ds\\
&\preceq |x-x'|^{(\alpha(x)-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}\!\cdot\Big[\Big(\rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})\!+({\gamma}/({2\alpha_2}))}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{{\gamma/(2\alpha_2)}}\Big)(t,x-y)\!+
\Big(\rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})\!+({\gamma}/({2\alpha_2}))}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{{\gamma/(2\alpha_2)}}\Big)(t,x'-y)\Big].
\end{align*}

Combining all the estimates together with \eqref{eq2-1} and using again \eqref{pppxy}, we can prove \eqref{t4-2-1} immediately.

(2) Now we assume that $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and ${(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}-1<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$.
Replacing $\alpha(x)$ by $\alpha(z)$ in \eqref{t4-2-1a}, we find that for every
$x,x'\in \mathds R^d$,
\begin{align*}
&\big|p^z(t-s,x-z)-p^z(t-s,x'-z)\big|\\
&\preceq (|x-x'|^{(\alpha_1-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}\wedge 1)(t-s)^{-{(\alpha(z)-\gamma)_+}/{\alpha(z)}} \big(\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x-z)+\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x'-z)\big)\\
&\preceq (|x-x'|^{(\alpha_1-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}\wedge 1)
\big[\rho^{z,0}_{{\gamma}/{\alpha_2}}(t-s,x-z)+\rho^{z,0}_{{\gamma}/{\alpha_2}}(t-s,x'-z)\big].
\end{align*}
Combining this with \eqref{eq2-1}, \eqref{p3-1-2} and \eqref{l3-3-1}, and following the
same arguments above,  we arrive at for all $x,x'\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|\leqslant R_2$,
\begin{align*}
 \big|p(t,x,y)-p(t,x',y)\big|
&\preceq |x-x'|^{(\alpha_1-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}\\
&\quad\times
\Big[\big(\rho^{y,0}_{{\gamma}/{\alpha_2}}(t,x-y)+
\rho^{y,0}_{{\gamma}/{\alpha_2}}(t,x'-y)\big)\\
&\qquad\,\,+\int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d}
\big(\rho^{z,0}_{{\gamma}/{\alpha_2}}(t-s,x-z)+\rho^{z,0}_{{\gamma}/{\alpha_2}}(t-s,x'-z)\big)\\
&\qquad \qquad  \times \big(\rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-[{(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}-1+{\gamma}/({2\alpha_2})]}+
\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-[{(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}-1+{\gamma}/({2\alpha_2})]}\Big)(s,z-y)\,dz\, ds \Big]\\
&\preceq |x-x'|^{(\alpha_1-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}
\big[\big(\rho^{y,0}_{\beta_0/\alpha_2+\gamma_1}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\gamma_1}\big)(t,x-y)+
\big(\rho^{y,0}_{\beta_0/\alpha_2+\gamma_1}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\gamma_1}\big)(t,x'-y)\big],
\end{align*}
where $\gamma_1:=1-\alpha_2/\alpha_1+\gamma/(2\alpha_2)$. By now we have verified \eqref{t4-2-1aa}. The proof is complete.
