nodes.statement:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(1)]
Suppose that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$. Let $\beta_0^*:=\beta_0\wedge\alpha_2$.
If $\tilde \beta_0(x_0):=({\alpha_1\beta_0}/{\alpha(x_0)})\wedge\alpha_1>1-\alpha(x_0)$ for some $x_0 \in \mathds R^d$, then for every fixed $t \in (0,1]$ and $y \in \mathds R^d$,
$p(t,\cdot,y)$ is differentiable at $x=x_0$. Moreover,
for every $\gamma>0$,
\begin{equation} |\nabla p(t,\cdot,y)(x_0)|\leqslant c_1\rho^{y,0}_{1-({1/\alpha(x_0)})+(\beta_0^*/\alpha_2)-
(\beta_0^*/\alpha_1)-\gamma}(t,x_0-y)
\end{equation}
holds for some $c_1:=c_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma,x_0)>0$.

\item[(2)]  Suppose that $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and ${(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}-1<\beta_0^{**}/\alpha_2$, where $\beta_0^{**}:=\beta_0\wedge (\alpha_2/2)$.
If $\tilde \beta_0(x_0)
-({\alpha_1\alpha_2}/{\alpha(x_0)})(({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1)>1-\alpha_1$ for some
$x_0\in \mathds R^d$ with $\tilde \beta_0(x_0)$ defined in $(i)$,
then for every fixed $t \in (0,1]$ and $y \in \mathds R^d$, $p(t,\cdot,y)$ is differentiable at
$x_0\in \mathds R^d$. Furthermore, for every $\gamma>0$, there exists a constant
$c_2:=c_2(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma,x_0)>0$ such that
\begin{equation} |\nabla p(t,\cdot,y)(x_0)|\leqslant c_2\rho^{y,0}_{1-({1}/{\alpha_1})+(\beta_0^*/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0^*/\alpha_1)-\gamma_2 }(t,x_0-y),
\end{equation}
where $\gamma_2 :={(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}-1+\gamma$.
\end{itemize}

nodes.label: t5-1-2

nodes.statement:
(1) We first suppose that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$. For simplicity, we assume
that $\beta_0< \alpha(x_0)$, and so $\beta_0^*=\beta_0$ and
$\tilde \beta_0(x_0)={\alpha_1\beta_0}/{\alpha(x_0)}$. We will show that we can take the gradient with respect to variable $x$ in the equation \eqref{eq2-1}.
Note that
\begin{align*}
&\int_0^t \left|\int_{\mathds R^d}\nabla p^z(t-s,x_0-z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\right|\,ds\\
&=\int_0^{t/2}\left|\int_{\mathds R^d}\nabla p^z(t-s,x_0-z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\right|\,ds\\
&\quad+\int_{t/2}^t\left|\int_{\mathds R^d}\nabla p^z(t-s,x_0-z)\left(q(s,z,y)-q(s,x_0,y)\right)\,dz\right|\,ds\\
&\quad+\int_{t/2}^t\left|\int_{\mathds R^d}\left(\nabla p^z(t-s,x_0-z)-\nabla p^{x_0}(t-s,x_0-z)\right)
q(s,x_0,y)\,dz\right|\,ds\\
&=:\int_0^{t/2}\left|\int_{\mathds R^d}J_1(s,z)\,dz\right|\,ds+\int_{t/2}^t
\left|\int_{\mathds R^d}J_2(s,z)\,dz\right|\,ds+\int_{t/2}^t
\left|\int_{\mathds R^d}J_3(s,z)\,dz\right|\,ds.
\end{align*}



According to \eqref{p1-1-1},
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
|\nabla p^z(t,x-z)|&\preceq \frac{t}{(t^{{1}/{\alpha(z)}}+|x-z|)^{d+\alpha(z)+1}}.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Observing that
\begin{equation*}
\Big|\frac{1}{\alpha(z)}-\frac{1}{\alpha(x)}\Big|\leqslant
\frac{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(z)|}{\alpha_1^2}\leqslant C|x-z|^{\beta_0},
\end{equation*}
we find by \eqref{t5-1-3} that for every (small enough) $\gamma>0$, there is a constant $R_1:=R_1(\alpha, \kappa,\gamma)>0$ such that
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
|\nabla p^z(t,x-z)|&\preceq
\begin{cases}
\rho^{z,0}_{1-({1}/{\alpha(z)})}(t,x-z),\ &|x-z|\leqslant R_1,\\
\frac{t}{|x-z|^{d+\alpha_1+1}}
,\ & |x-z|>R_1
\end{cases}\\
&\preceq \rho^{z,0}_{1-({1/\alpha(x)})-\gamma}(t,x-z). \end{split}
\end{equation}

Thus, choosing $\gamma>0$ small enough such that $\gamma<\beta_0/\alpha_2$, and using \eqref{l3-2-0}, \eqref{p3-1-1} and
\eqref{t5-1-4}, we can find that
\begin{align*}
&\int_0^{t/2}\int_{\mathds R^d}|J_1(s,z)|\,dz\,ds\\
&\preceq
\int_0^{t/2}\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{z,0}_{1-({1/\alpha(x_0)})-\gamma}(t-s,x_0-z)
\big(
\rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}(s,z-y)+
\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}(s,z-y)\big)\,dz\,ds\\
&\preceq \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x_0-y)\!\bigg(\!\int_0^{t/2}\!(t\!-\!s)^{-(1/\alpha(x_0))-\gamma}s^{(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-\gamma}\! +\!
(t\!-\!s)^{1-(1/\alpha(x_0))-\gamma}s^{-1+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-\gamma}\,ds \bigg)\\
&\preceq \rho^{y,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x_0))-2\gamma}(t,x-y).
\end{align*}

On the other hand, according to \eqref{p3-1-1a}, \eqref{t5-1-4} and the fact that $\beta_0<\alpha(x_0)$, we arrive at
\begin{align*}
 \int_{t/2}^t\int_{\mathds R^d}|J_2(s,z)|\,dz\,ds
&\preceq \int_{t/2}^t\int_{\mathds R^d}
\bigg(\rho^{z,\widehat \beta_0}_{1-({1/\alpha(x_0)})-\gamma}(t-s,x_0-z)\tilde\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-{(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}}
(s,z-y)
\\
&\qquad\qquad
+\rho^{z,\widehat \beta_0}_{1-({1/\alpha(x_0)})-\gamma}(t-s,x_0-z)\tilde\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-{(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}}(s,x_0-y)\bigg)\,dz\,ds\\
&=:\int_{t/2}^t \int_{\mathds R^d}(J_{21}(s,z)+J_{22}(s,z))\,dz\,ds,
\end{align*}
where $\widehat \beta_0=\widehat \beta_0(\theta):={\alpha_1(\beta_0-\alpha_2\theta)}/{\alpha(x_0)}$.

Since $\tilde \beta_0(x_0)>1-\alpha(x_0)$, we can choose
$\theta, \gamma>0$ small enough such that $1+(\widehat \beta_0/\alpha(x_0))-(1/\alpha(x_0))-\gamma>0$, which along with
\eqref{l3-2-0} yields
\begin{align*}
\int_{t/2}^t \int_{\mathds R^d}J_{21}(s,z)\,dz\,ds
&\preceq \tilde \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x_0-y)\cdot\Big(
\int_{t/2}^t (t-s)^{1-(1/\alpha(x_0))-\gamma}s^{-1+\theta-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}\\
&\quad \quad +(t-s)^{(\widehat \beta_0/\alpha(x_0))-
(1/\alpha(x_0))-\gamma}s^{\theta-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}\,ds\Big)\\
&\preceq\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x_0))+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)-2\gamma}(t,x_0-y).
\end{align*}
On the other hand, noting that for $t/2<s\leqslant t$, it holds that
\begin{equation} \tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-{(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}}(s,x_0-y)\preceq
\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-{(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}}(t,x_0-y).
\end{equation}
Since $\tilde \beta_0>1-\alpha(x_0)$, by \eqref{l3-1-1} we have
\begin{align*}
 \int_{t/2}^t \int_{\mathds R^d}J_{22}(s,z)\,dz\,ds
&\preceq
\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}(t,x_0-y)
\int_{t/2}^t\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{z,\widehat \beta_0}_{1-({1/\alpha(x_0)})-\gamma}(t-s,x_0-z)\,dz\,ds\\
&\preceq \tilde \rho^{y,0}_{1+(\widehat \beta_0/\alpha(x_0))-(1/\alpha(x_0))+
(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)-2\gamma}(t,x_0-y).
\end{align*}



According to \eqref{l4-1-1-1} for the case that $|x_0-z|\leqslant R_1$ and \eqref{t5-1-4} for the case
that $|x_0-z|>R_1$), we arrive at that (by changing the constant $\gamma$ properly) for any $t>0$ and $x_0,z\in \mathds R^d$,
\begin{align*}
\left|\nabla p^{x_0}(t,x_0-z)-\nabla p^z(t,x_0-z)\right|\preceq
\tilde \rho^{z,\beta_0}_{1-1/\alpha(x_0)-\gamma}(t,x_0-z).
\end{align*}
This, along with \eqref{p3-1-1} yields
\begin{align*}
\int_{t/2}^t\int_{\mathds R^d}|J_3(s,z)|\,dz\,ds
&\preceq \tilde \rho^{y,0}_{-\gamma}(t,x_0-y)\int_{t/2}^t\int_{\mathds R^d} \rho^{z,\beta_0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x_0))-\gamma}(t-s,x_0-z)\,dz\,ds\\
&\preceq \tilde \rho^{y,0}_{1+(\beta_0/\alpha(x_0))-1/\alpha(x_0)-2\gamma}(t,x_0-y),
\end{align*} where in the last inequality we used the fact that $\beta_0\geqslant\tilde \beta_0(x_0)>1-\alpha(x_0)$.

Combining all estimates together, we obtain that
\begin{equation*}
\int_0^t \left|\int_{\mathds R^d}\nabla p^z(t-s,x_0-z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\right|\,ds
\preceq  \tilde \rho^{y,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x_0))+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)-2\gamma}(t,x_0-y).
\end{equation*}
According to the estimate above and the dominated convergence theorem,  we know that
$\nabla p(t,\cdot)(x_0)$ exists, and \eqref{t5-1-1} holds by changing $\theta$ and $\gamma$ properly.


(2) Suppose that $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and
${(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}-1<{\beta_0^{**}}/{\alpha_2}$. If for some $x_0\in \mathds R^d$,
$\tilde \beta_0(x_0)-({\alpha_1\alpha_2}/{\alpha(x_0)})
\big(({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1\big)>1-\alpha_1$, then, by \eqref{l4-1-1-1} and
\eqref{t5-1-3},
$$
|\nabla p^z(t,x-z)|\preceq t^{-{1}/{\alpha(z)}}\rho^{z,0}_1(t,x-z)\preceq
\rho^{z,0}_{1-(1/\alpha_1)}(t,x-z)
$$
and $$
|\nabla p^x(t,x-z)-\nabla p^z(t,x-z)|\preceq
\tilde \rho^{z,\beta_0}_{1-(1/\alpha_1)-\gamma}(t,x-z).
$$
In the following, we choose $\theta,\gamma$ small enough such that
$$\widehat \beta_0:={\alpha_1}\big(\beta_0-\alpha_2\theta\big)/{\alpha(x_0)}>-1+(1/\alpha_1)+\gamma.$$
Using estimates and following the same argument in part (1), we can obtain that
for every fixed $t \in (0,1]$ and $y \in \mathds R^d$, $p(t,\cdot,y)$ is differentiable at $x_0\in \mathds R^d$ and
\eqref{t5-1-2} holds.

nodes.statement:
We only consider the case that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$, and the other case can be verified similarly.

According to \eqref{eq2-1}, \eqref{p3-1-1} and \eqref{p3-2-1}, we know
immediately the continuity of $p$ with respect to time variable.
It remains to show the continuity of $p$ with respect to space variables.

For $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ and any $\varepsilon>0$
\begin{align*}
|p^{y+\varepsilon z}(t,x-y-\varepsilon)-
p^{y}(t,x-y)|
&\leqslant  |p^{y+\varepsilon z}(t,x-y-\varepsilon)-
p^{y+\varepsilon z}(t,x-y)|+
|p^{y+\varepsilon z}(t,x-y)-p^{y}(t,x-y)|.
\end{align*}
According to \eqref{p1-1-3} and \eqref{l4-1-1}, we can show that
$(x,y)\mapsto p^y(t,x-y)$ is continuous. On the other hand,  \eqref{p1-1-4}, \eqref{p3-1-1a-1} and \eqref{l4-1-1a} imply that
$(x,y)\mapsto q_0(t,x,y)$ is continuous. By the iteration estimates in Proposition \ref{p3-1} and the
dominated convergence theorem, we also can verify that $(x,y)\mapsto q(t,x,y)$ is continuous.
Due to the expression \eqref{eq2-1} and again the dominated convergence theorem,  we know that
$(x,y)\mapsto p(t,x,y)$ is continuous. The proof is finished.

nodes.label: p4-1-1

nodes.statement:
Throughout the proof, we will assume that $\beta_0<\alpha_2$ and $\beta_0^*=\beta_0$ for simplicity.
Noting that $\int_{\mathds R^d}p^x(t,x-y)\,dy=1$ for all $x\in \mathds R^d$ and $t\in (0,1]$, we have
\begin{align*}
\bigg|\int_{\mathds R^d}p^y(t,x-y)\,dy-1\bigg|&=\bigg|
\int_{\mathds R^d}p^y(t,x-y)\,dy-\int_{\mathds R^d}p^x(t,x-y)\,dy\bigg|\\
&\leqslant \int_{\mathds R^d}|p^x(t,x-y)-p^y(t,x-y)|\,dy\\
&\leqslant \int_{\{|x-y|\leqslant R_1\}}|p^x(t,x-y)-p^y(t,x-y)|\,dy\\
&\quad +\int_{\{|x-y|>R_1\}}|p^x(t,x-y)-p^y(t,x-y)|\,dy\\
&=:J_1+J_2,
\end{align*}
where $R_1$ is the constant in Lemma \ref{l4-1}.

On the one hand, \eqref{l4-1-1} yields that
\begin{align*}
J_1& \preceq \int_{\mathds R^d} \tilde \rho^{x,\beta_0}_{1-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y)\,dy\preceq t^{(\beta_0/{\alpha_2})-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})},
\end{align*}
where the last inequality follows from the fact that \eqref{l3-1-1-00} holds for $\tilde \rho$.

On the other hand,
\begin{align*}
J_2& \preceq \int_{\{|x-y|>R_1\}}\big(\rho^{x,0}_1(t,x-y)+\rho^{y,0}_1(t,x-y)\big)\,dy\\
&\preceq \int_{\{|x-y|>R_1\}}\bigg(\frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}}+\frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\bigg)\,dy\preceq t \int_{\{|x-y|>R_1\}}\frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}\,dy \preceq t.
\end{align*}
Combining with both estimates for $J_1$ and $J_2$, we prove \eqref{p4-1-1-e}.


Choosing $\gamma,\theta>0$ small enough such that $2\gamma+({\theta}/{\alpha_1})<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$, we immediately get \eqref{p4-1-1}.
nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.1

nodes.name: Estimate of $\delta_{p^x}-\delta_{p^y}$
nodes.statement_short: The jump-weighted integral of $|\delta_{p^x}-\delta_{p^y}|$ is bounded by $\tilde\rho^{x,\beta_0}_{-2\gamma-\theta/\alpha_1}(t,x-y)$.
nodes.label: l4-2

nodes.name: Equation (5.3)
nodes.label: l4-2-1

nodes.statement:
By using \eqref{l4-1-2}, we can verify that
\begin{align*}
& \delta_{p^x}(t,x-y;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)\\
&=\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)p^x(s,w)
\big(\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y-w;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y;z)\big)\,dw\bigg)\,ds\\
&\quad+\int_{{t}/{2}}^t\!\!\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)p^y(t-s,x-y-w)
\big(\delta_{p^x}(s,w;z)-\delta_{p^x}(s,x-y;z)\big)\,dw\bigg)\,ds.
\end{align*}
Therefore,
\begin{align*}
& \int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\delta_{p^x}(t,x-y;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)\big|\cdot\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\
& \leqslant \int_0^{{t}/{2}}\bigg[\int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)p^x(s,w)\big|
\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y-w;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y;z)\big|\cdot \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\bigg)\,dw\bigg]\,ds\\
&+\int_{{t}/{2}}^t\bigg[\int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)p^y(t-s,x-y-w)\big|
\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\delta_{p^x}(s,w;z)-\delta_{p^x}(s,x-y;z)\big|\cdot \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\bigg)\,dw\bigg]\,ds\\
&=:J_1+J_2.
\end{align*}


According to \eqref{p1-1-4} and \eqref{l4-1-5}, for every $\theta \in (0,1)$ and $\gamma>0$, there exists a constant
$R_1:=R_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma)>0$ such that for every $0<s<t<1$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
&\big|\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y-w;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y;z)\big|\\
&\preceq \big[\left((t-s)^{-{1/\alpha(y)}}|w|\right)^{\theta}\wedge 1\big]\cdot
\left[\left((t-s)^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\right)\wedge 1\right]
\\
&\quad\times\big[
\rho_1^{y,0}(t-s,x-y)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t-s,x-y-w)
+\rho_1^{y,0}(t-s,x-y\pm z)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t-s,x-y-w\pm z)\big]\\
&\preceq \left(|w|^{\theta}\wedge 1\right)\cdot
\left[\left((t-s)^{-{2}/{\alpha(x)}}|z|^2\right)\wedge 1\right]
 \cdot\big[
\rho_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}^{x,0}(t-s,x-y)+\rho_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}^{x,0}(t-s,x-y-w)\\
&\qquad\qquad\qquad\quad
+\rho_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}^{x,0}(t-s,x-y\pm z)+\rho_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}^{x,0}(t-s,x-y-w\pm z)\big].
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Furthermore, following the argument of Lemma \ref{l1-1}, we can derive that for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y \in \mathds R^d$
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
&\int_{\mathds R^d} \left[\left(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(x)}}|z|^2\right)\wedge 1\right]
\cdot \rho_{1}^{x,0}(t,y \pm z)\cdot |z|^{-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz
\preceq \rho^{x,0}_{0}(t,y),\\
&\int_{\mathds R^d} \left[\left(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(x)}}|z|^2\right)\wedge 1\right]
\cdot \rho_{1}^{x,0}(t,y)\cdot |z|^{-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz
\preceq \rho^{x,0}_{0}(t,y).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Combining \eqref{l4-1-4} with \eqref{l4-2-2} and \eqref{l4-2-3}, we find that for  all $t\in(0,1]$ and  $x,y\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$,
\begin{align*}
J_1 &\preceq |x-y|^{\beta_0}\cdot \bigg[
\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{x,\theta}_{-\gamma}(s,w)\cdot
\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t-s,x-y-w)\,dw\,ds\\
&\qquad\qquad\qquad+\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{x,\theta}_{-\gamma}(s,w)\cdot
\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t-s,x-y)\,dw\,ds\bigg]\\
&=:|x-y|^{\beta_0}\cdot(J_{11}+J_{12}).
\end{align*}
Since \eqref{l3-2-1-} holds true for $\tilde \rho$ as mentioned in Remark \ref{r3-3}(2),
for every $0<\theta<\alpha_1$ and $0<\gamma<({\theta}/{\alpha_2})\wedge ((1-({\theta}/{\alpha_1}))/2)$, we have
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
J_{11}&\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_0(t,x-y) \int_0^{{t}/{2}}\big(s^{-1-\gamma+({\theta}/{\alpha_2})}(t-s)^{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}
+s^{-\gamma}(t-s)^{-1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}\big)\,ds\\
&\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_0(t,x-y) \bigg(t^{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}\int_0^{{t}/{2}}s^{-1-\gamma+({\theta}/{\alpha_2})}\,ds+
t^{-1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}\int_0^{{t}/{2}} s^{-\gamma}\,ds\bigg)\\
& \preceq  \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
On the other hand, note that for every $0<s<{t}/{2}$, $$\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t-s,x-y)\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y).$$
Then, it holds that
\begin{align*}
J_{12}&\preceq  \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y)\cdot
\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{x,\theta}_{-\gamma}(s,w)\,dw\,ds\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y),
\end{align*} where \eqref{l3-1-1-00} was used in the last inequality.
Hence, we find that for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y \in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$,
\begin{equation*}
J_1 \preceq \tilde \rho^{x,\beta_0}_{-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y).
\end{equation*}

By estimates for
 the terms
$$\big|\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)p^y(t-s,x-y-w)\big|$$ and $$\big|
\delta_{p^x}(s,w;z)-\delta_{p^x}(s,x-y;z)\big|,$$ we can deal with the singularity
as $s$ near $t$ by the same arguments above and obtain that for all $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$,
\begin{equation*}
J_2 \preceq \tilde \rho^{x,\beta_0}_{-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y).
\end{equation*}


Combining both of the estimates for $J_1$ and $J_2$, we finally obtain that \eqref{l4-2-1} holds true.

nodes.statement:
(i) We first assume that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$.
We will prove that $p(t,x,y)$ constructed by \eqref{eq2-1} satisfies all the assertions.

According to Proposition \ref{t4-1}, \eqref{t1-1-1} holds. By
Propositions \ref{p3-2} and \ref{p3-3}, \eqref{t1-1-4} and \eqref{t1-1-4a} hold true.
Propositions \ref{t4-2} and \ref{t5-1} imply
\eqref{t1-1-7} and \eqref{t1-1-7a}, respectively. By Proposition \ref{p4-5},  we know that
$p:(0,1]\times\mathds R^d\times \mathds R^d\rightarrow \mathds R_+$ is continuous. The lower bounds
\eqref{t1-1-4b}  will be shown in Corollary \ref{c-lower}, which is a consequence of Propositions
\ref{p4-3} and \ref{t4-4} in the next subsection.

\smallskip

(ii) According to  the proof of Proposition \ref{t4-1}, we can
obtain that for every $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$, there exist a constant
$C(\varepsilon)>0$ and a measurable function $\eta:\mathds R^d \to  \mathds R_+$ such that
$\int_{\mathds R^d}\eta(y)\,dy<\infty$,

\begin{equation*}
\sup_{t \in (\varepsilon,1)}\Big|\frac{\partial p(t,x,y)}{\partial t}\Big|\leqslant C(\varepsilon)\eta(x-y)
\end{equation*} and
\begin{equation*}\begin{split}
&\sup_{t \in (\varepsilon,1),\sigma>0}\bigg|\int_{\{|z|>\sigma\}}\big(p(t,x+z,y)+p(t,x-z,y)-2p(t,x,y)\big)
\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\bigg|\leqslant C(\varepsilon)\eta(x-y).\end{split}
\end{equation*}
Thus, by the dominated convergence theorem, it is easy to verify
that ${\mathcal L} u_f (t, \cdot) (x)$ exists for each $t>0$ and $x\in \mathds R^d$, $t\mapsto {\mathcal L} u_f (t, \cdot) (x)$
is continuous,  and that \eqref{t1-1-2} holds.

\smallskip

(iii) We have by \eqref{eq2-1} that
\begin{align*}
u_f(t,x)-f(x)&=\int_{\mathds R^d}p^y(t,x-y)\big(f(y)-f(x)\big)\,dy+
f(x)\left(\int_{\mathds R^d}p^y(t,x-y)\,dy-1\right)\\
&\quad +\int_{\mathds R^d} f(y)\int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d}p^z(t-s,x-z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\,ds\,dy\\
&=:J_1+J_2+J_3.
\end{align*}

For any $f\in C_{b,u}(\mathds R^d)$ and for every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists
a constant $\delta:=\delta(\varepsilon)>0$ such that $|f(x)-f(y)|<\varepsilon$ for all $x,y \in \mathds R^d$ with
$|x-y|\leqslant \delta$. Thus,
\begin{align*}
|J_1|&\leqslant \int_{\{|y-x|\leqslant \delta\}}p^y(t,x-y)|f(y)-f(x)|\,dy+
\int_{\{|y-x|>\delta\}}p^y(t,x-y)|f(y)-f(x)|\,dy\\
&\leqslant \varepsilon \int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{y,0}_1(t,x-y)\,dy+
C(\varepsilon)\|f\|_{\infty}\int_{\{|y-x|>\delta\}}\frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}\,dy\leqslant C\varepsilon+C(\varepsilon,\delta)t,
\end{align*}
where in the last inequality we have used \eqref{l3-1-1}.
According to \eqref{p4-1-1}, it holds that $\lim_{t \downarrow 0}\sup_{x \in \mathds R^d}|J_2|=0$.
Furthermore, by \eqref{p3-1-1} and \eqref{l3-3-1}, we obtain that for $\gamma<\beta_0^*/{\alpha_2}$ with $\beta^*\in (0,\beta]\cap(0,\alpha_2/2)$,
\begin{align*}
|J_3|&\preceq \|f\|_{\infty}\Bigg[\int_{\mathds R^d}
\int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x-z)
\Big(\rho^{y,0}_{{(\beta_0^*/\alpha_2)}-\gamma}(s,z-y)+ \rho^{y,\beta_0^*}_{-\gamma}(s,z-y)\Big)\,dz\,ds\,dy\Bigg]\\
&\preceq \|f\|_{\infty}\int_{\mathds R^d}
\Big(\rho^{y,0}_{1+{(\beta_0^*/\alpha_2)}-\gamma}+\rho^{y,\beta_0^*}_{1-\gamma}\Big)(t,x-y)\,dy\preceq t^{{(\beta_0^*/\alpha_2)}-\gamma}\|f\|_{\infty}.
\end{align*}
Combining all the estimates above together, we arrive at
\begin{equation*}
\lim_{t \downarrow 0}\sup_{x \in \mathds R^d}\big|u_f(t,x)-f(x)\big|\leqslant \varepsilon.
\end{equation*}
Since $\varepsilon$ is arbitrary, we know that \eqref{t1-1-3} holds.

\smallskip

(iv) Denote by $C_{b}^{\varepsilon}(\mathds R^d)$ the set of bounded H\"{o}lder continuous functions, and by $C_{b}^{2,\varepsilon}(\mathds R^d)$ the set of bounded twice differentiable functions whose second derivatives are uniformly H\"{o}lder continuous.  We first suppose that $f \in C_{b}^{2,\varepsilon}(\mathds R^d)$. Let
\begin{equation*}
\tilde u_f(t,x):=f(x)+\int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d}p(s,x,y){\mathcal L} f(y)\,dy\,ds=f(x)+\int_0^t
u_{{\mathcal L} f}(s,x)\,ds.
\end{equation*}
Since ${\mathcal L} f \in C_{b}^{\varepsilon}(\mathds R^d)$, it is easy to see that
\begin{equation*}
\frac{\partial \tilde u_f(t,x)}{\partial t}=\int_{\mathds R^d}p(t,x,y){\mathcal L} f(y)\,dy
=u_{{\mathcal L} f}(t,x),\quad t\in (0,1]
\end{equation*} and
\begin{equation*}
\lim_{t \downarrow 0}\sup_{x\in\mathds R^d}|\tilde u_f(t,x)-f(x)|=0.
\end{equation*}

On the other hand, due to ${\mathcal L} f \in C_{b}^{\varepsilon}(\mathds R^d)$ again, it follows from \eqref{t1-1-2} that
$ {\mathcal L} u_{{\mathcal L} f}(t,x)=\frac{\partial u_{{\mathcal L} f}(t,x)}{\partial t}$. Furthermore, following the
proof of Proposition \ref{t4-1}, we will get
\begin{align*}
\int_0^t \Big|\int_{\mathds R^d} {\mathcal L}^x p^z(t-s,x-z){\mathcal L} f(z)\,dz\Big|\,ds
&\leqslant \int_0^t \Big|\int_{\mathds R^d} {\mathcal L}^z p^z(t-s,x-z){\mathcal L} f(z)\,dz\Big|\,ds\\
&\quad +\int_0^t \Big|\int_{\mathds R^d}( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^z) p^z(t-s,x-z){\mathcal L} f(z)\,dz\Big|\,ds<\infty
\end{align*} and so $$\int_0^t {\mathcal L} u_{{\mathcal L} f}(s,x)\,ds$$ is well defined.
Hence,
\begin{align*}
{\mathcal L}\tilde u_f(t,x)&={\mathcal L} f(x)+\int_0^t
 {\mathcal L} u_{{\mathcal L} f}(s,x)\,ds={\mathcal L} f(x)+\int_0^t \frac{\partial u_{{\mathcal L} f}(s,x)}{\partial s}\,ds\\
&={\mathcal L} f(x)+u_{{\mathcal L} f}(t,x)-{\mathcal L} f(x)=u_{{\mathcal L} f}(t,x),
\end{align*}
where in the third equality we used
$\lim_{t \downarrow 0}\sup_{x\in\mathds R^d}|u_{{\mathcal L} f}(t,x)-{\mathcal L} f(x)|=0$, thanks to \eqref{t1-1-3}.
Therefore, both $u_f$ and $\tilde u_f$ are solutions of the following PDE
\begin{equation} \begin{cases}
\frac{\partial u(t,x)}{\partial t}= {\mathcal L} u(t,x),\\
\lim_{t \downarrow 0}\sup_{x \in \mathds R^d}|u(t,x)-f(x)|=0.
\end{cases}
\end{equation}

Let $w_f(t,x):=u_f(t,x)-\tilde u_f(t,x)$. Then,  \eqref{t4-3-2a} and \eqref{t4-3-1} hold for $w_f$ with $w_f(0,x)\equiv 0$. At the same time, it is easy to verify from \eqref{eq2-1}
that the function $t \mapsto {\mathcal L} w_f(t,x)$ is continuous on $(0,1]$, and that
\eqref{t1-1-7} implies \eqref{t4-3-2} holds for $w_f$. Thus, by Theorem \ref{t4-3}, we have
\begin{equation*}
w_f(t,x)\leqslant w_f(0,x)=0,\quad (t,x)\in (0,1]\times \mathds R^d.
\end{equation*}
Furthermore, applying the argument above to $-w_f$, we finally get that \begin{equation*}
w_f(t,x)\equiv 0,\quad  (t,x)\in (0,1]\times \mathds R^d.
\end{equation*}
Therefore, $u_f(t,x)=\tilde u_f(t,x)$ for any $t \in (0,1]$ and $x \in \mathds R^d$, which further implies that
\begin{equation*}
\int_{\mathds R^d} {\mathcal L} p(t,\cdot,y)(x)f(y)\,dy=\frac{\partial u_f(t,x)}{\partial t}
=\frac{\partial \tilde u_{f}(t,x)}{\partial t}=\int_{\mathds R^d}p(t,x,y){\mathcal L} f(y)\,dy.
\end{equation*}
Thus, \eqref{t1-1-5a} holds. Observe that
\begin{equation*}
u_f(t,x)=\tilde u_f(t,x)=f(x)+\int_0^t u_{{\mathcal L} f}(s,x)\,ds.
\end{equation*}
According to \eqref{t1-1-3}, we arrive at \eqref{t1-1-5b} immediately.
By the standard approximation procedure, we know that \eqref{t1-1-5a} and
\eqref{t1-1-5b} still hold for every $f \in C_{b,u}^2(\mathds R^d)$.

\smallskip

(v) Let $u(t,x)=:\int_{\mathds R^d}p(t,x,y)\,dy$. Then, according to \eqref{t1-1-2} and \eqref{t1-1-3}, we know that
$u$ satisfies the following equation
\begin{equation} \begin{cases}
\frac{\partial u(t,x)}{\partial t}= {\mathcal L} u(t,x),\\
\lim_{t \downarrow 0}\sup_{x \in \mathds R^d}\big|u(t,x)-1\big|=0.
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
At the same time, $v(t,x)\equiv 1$ satisfies the equation \eqref{t1-1-11} above. Note that \eqref{t4-3-2} and the time continuity condition hold for both
$u(t,x)$ and $v(t,x)$. Then, using the same argument as in (iv)  and applying Theorem \ref{t4-3}, we obtain
\begin{equation*}
\int_{\mathds R^d}p(t,x,y)\,dy=u(t,x)=1,\quad (t,x)\in (0,1]\times \mathds R^d,
\end{equation*}
which is \eqref{t1-1-6}.

For every fixed $s \in (0,1)$ and $y \in \mathds R^d$, we define $$u_{s,y}(t,x):=\int_{\mathds R^d}p(t,x,z)p(s,z,y)\,dz.$$
 Again by \eqref{t1-1-2} and \eqref{t1-1-3}, the following equation holds for $u_{s,y}$:
\begin{equation} \begin{cases}
\frac{\partial u_{s,y}(t,x)}{\partial t}= {\mathcal L} u_{s,y}(t,x),\\
\lim_{t \downarrow 0}\sup_{x \in \mathds R^d}|u_{s,y}(t,x)-p(s,x,y)|=0.
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
On the other hand, it is easy to verify that $v_{s,y}(t,x):=p(t+s,x,y)$ satisfies
\eqref{t1-1-12}, and \eqref{t4-3-2} and the time continuity condition hold for both
$u_{s,y}(t,x)$ and $v_{s,y}(t,x)$.  Following the procedure above and applying Theorem \ref{t4-3}, we arrive at
$$\int_{\mathds R^d}p(t,x,z)p(s,z,y)\,dz=u_{s,y}(t,x)=v_{s,y}(t,x)=p(t+s,x,y),$$
which is \eqref{t1-1-5}.

\smallskip

(vi)
Suppose that $\widehat p(t,x,y)$ is another
jointly continuous function  on $(0, 1]\times \mathds R^d\times \mathds R^d$
that is bounded for each $t>0$ and
 satisfies  \eqref{t1-1-7} and \eqref{t1-1-2a}-\eqref{t1-1-3}.
For every $f \in C_{b,u}(\mathds R^d)$, let
$$\widehat u_f(t,x):=\int_{\mathds R^d}\widehat p(t,x,y)f(y)\,dy \quad \hbox{and} \quad
\widehat w_f(t,x):=u_f(t,x)-\widehat u_f(t,x).
$$
 Then both $u_f$ and $\widehat u_f$ satisfy \eqref{t1-1-2}. By the same argument above, we have
$\widehat w_f(t,x)=0$ for each $(t,x)\in (0,1]\times \mathds R^d$. This implies
that for every $f \in C_{b,u}(\mathds R^d)$,
\begin{equation*}
\int_{\mathds R^d} p(t,x,y)f(y)\,dy=\int_{\mathds R^d} \widehat p(t,x,y)f(y)\,dy.
\end{equation*}
Consequently, $p(t,x,y)=\widehat p(t,x,y)$ for a.e.\ $y \in \mathds R^d$ and hence for every $y\in \mathds R^d$.

\smallskip

(vii) Suppose that $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$.  The desired upper and lower estimates and the regularity can be proved in a similar way as before. On the other hand, the condition ${(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}-1<\beta_*/\alpha_2<{1}/{2}$ implies that
$\alpha_2-\alpha_1<{\alpha_1}/{2}<1$, which ensures that
\eqref{t4-3-2} holds with $u_f(t,x):=\int_{\mathds R^d}p(t,x,y)f(y)\,dy$ for every
$f \in C_{b,u}(\mathds R^d)$. Therefore, following the arguments in steps (i)-(vi), we can verify that \eqref{t1-1-5}-\eqref{t1-1-5b} hold in such case.

nodes.statement:
In Theorem \ref{t1-1} we assume that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$.
According to its proof, the reason why we need such condition is only due to that this implies the
gradient estimate \eqref{p1-1-1}. Thus, for the upper bound estimates for $|\nabla p^y(t,x)|$
and  $|\nabla^2 p^y(t,x)|$, the time singularity factor $t^{-{1/\alpha(y)}}$ will not appear when $|x|$ is large and $t$ is small. This point is
crucial for estimates \eqref{l2-1-2} and \eqref{p3-1-1a-1}, which yield Theorem \ref{t1-1}.

Now, we turn to these two assumptions in Remark \ref{rrr-000}(1). According to \cite[Theorem 1.5]{KR} and  \cite[Corollary 7 and Theorem 21]{BGR}, the following gradient estimate \begin{equation*}
|\nabla^k p^y(t,x)|\preceq \frac{t}{|x|^{d+\alpha(y)+k}},\quad k=1,2
\end{equation*} holds for all $t \in (0,1]$ and $x\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x|$ is large,
which also ensures that
the required estimates \eqref{l2-1-2} and \eqref{p3-1-1a-1} hold true.
nodes.name: Proof of Remark 1.5
nodes.statement_short: Known gradient estimates for radial monotone kernels replace the $z$-independence assumption in the proof of Theorem 1.1.

nodes.statement_short: Either $\kappa$ is independent of $z$, or it depends on $z$ with $(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)-1<\beta_0^{**}/\alpha_2$.

nodes.statement:
{\bf (On diagonal lower bounds)} There exists a positive constant $c_1:=c_1(\alpha,\kappa)$ such that for all $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y \in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant 5
(t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}}\vee t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}})$,
\begin{equation} p(t,x,y) \geqslant c_1t^{-{d}/{\alpha(x)}}.
\end{equation}

nodes.statement: p(t,x,y) \geqslant c_1t^{-{d}/{\alpha(x)}}.
nodes.label: p4-3-1

nodes.statement:
For simplicity, we only prove the case that $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and $({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1<\beta_0^{**}/{\alpha_2}$, since the other case can be
tackled similarly and easily.

First, according to \eqref{l3-2-8}, for any $t\in(0,1]$ and $x,y\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant 5
(t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}}\vee t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}})\leqslant 5t^{{1}/{\alpha_2}}$,
\begin{equation} t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}}\asymp t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}.
\end{equation}
It is well known that for any $t>0$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$, $$p^y(t,x-y)\asymp \frac{t}{(t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}+|x-y|)^{d+\alpha(y)}}.$$
Thus, for all $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in\mathds R^d$,
\begin{equation} p^y(t,x-y)\succeq t^{-{d}/{\alpha(y)}}
\quad\textrm{ when }|x-y|\leqslant 5(t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}}\vee t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}).
\end{equation}

Second, \eqref{p3-1-2} and \eqref{l3-3-1}  yield that for all $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant 5t^{{1}/{\alpha_2}}$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
&\int_0^t \int_{\mathds R^d}
p^z(t-s,x-z)|q(s,z,y)|\,dz\,ds\\
&\preceq\int_0^t \int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x-z)
\cdot\Big(\rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0^{**}}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma_2 }+\rho^{y,\beta_0^{**}}_{-\gamma_2 }\Big)(s,z,y)\,dz\,ds\\
&\preceq \rho^{y,\beta_0^{**}}_{1-\gamma_2 }(t,x-y)+\rho^{y,0}_{1+({\beta_0^{**}}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma_2 }(t,x-y)\\
& \preceq
|x-y|^{\beta_0^{**}}t^{-{d}/{\alpha(y)}-\gamma_2 }+t^{-({d}/{\alpha(y)})+({\beta_0^{**}}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma_2 }\preceq t^{-({d}/{\alpha(y)})+({\beta_0^{**}}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma_2 },
\end{split}
\end{equation}
where in the first inequality $\gamma_2: =({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1+\gamma$ and the fourth inequality
follows from the fact that $|x-y|\leqslant 5t^{{1}/{\alpha_2}}$.

The assumption $({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1<{\beta_0^{**}}/{\alpha_2}$ ensures that we can choose
$\gamma>0$ small enough such that $\gamma_2 <{\beta_0^{**}}/{\alpha_2}$. Combining \eqref{p4-3-4}
with \eqref{p4-3-3}, \eqref{eq2-1} and \eqref{p4-3-2}, we arrive at that there is a constant $t_0\in(0,1]$ such that for all $t\in (0,t_0]$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant 5(t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}}\vee t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}})$,
\begin{equation} p(t,x,y)\succeq t^{-{d}/{\alpha(y)}}\asymp t^{-{d}/{\alpha(x)}}.
\end{equation}
Note that, according to the argument above, \eqref{pnte} still holds for all $t\in (0,t_0]$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\preceq
(t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}}\vee t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}})$. Furthermore, due to \eqref{p4-3-2}, for any $y,z\in \mathds R^d$ with $|z-y|\leqslant 5t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}$, we have $|x-z|\leqslant |z-y|+|x-y|\preceq t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}}$ for any $x\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\preceq (t^{1/\alpha(x)}\vee t^{1/\alpha(y)})$, and so $$p(t,x,z)\succeq t^{-{d}/{\alpha(z)}}\asymp t^{-{d}/{\alpha(x)}},\quad t\in (0,t_0],$$ thanks to \eqref{p4-3-2} again. Therefore, according to the Chapman-Kolmogorov equation
\eqref{t1-1-5} and \eqref{pnte}, for every $t\in [t_0,2t_0]$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant
5t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}}$,
\begin{align*}
p(t,x,y)&=\int_{\mathds R^d}p(t_0,x,z)p(t-t_0,z,y)\,dz\succeq (t-t_0)^{-{d}/{\alpha(y)}}\int_{\{|z-y|\leqslant 5(t-t_0)^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}\}}
p(t_0,x,z)\,dz\\
&\succeq (t-t_0)^{-{d}/{\alpha(y)}}t_0^{-{d}/{\alpha(x)}}(t-t_0)^{{d}/{\alpha(y)}}\succeq
t^{-{d}/{\alpha(x)}}.
\end{align*}
Iterating the arguments above $[{1}/{t_0}]+1$ times, we can
obtain \eqref{p4-3-1}.

nodes.statement:
Note that, from the Chapman-Kolmogorov equation \eqref{t1-1-5} and the properties \eqref{t1-1-2} and \eqref{t1-1-5a}, it is standard to prove the following result. Since the proof is almost the same as \cite[Theorem 4.5]{CZ},
we omit it here.

nodes.statement:
$(1)$ There is a strong Markov process $X:=\big((X_t)_{t \geqslant 0}; (\mathds P_x)_{x\in \mathds R^d}\big)$ such that for every
$f \in C_b^2(\mathds R^d)$,
\begin{equation} M_t^f:=f(X_t)-f(X_0)-\int_0^t {\mathcal L} f(X_s)\,ds,\quad t \in (0,1]
\end{equation}
is a martingale with respect to the natural filtration $\mathscr{F}_t:=\sigma\{X_s,0\leqslant s\leqslant t\}$ under probability
measure $\mathds P_x$ for all $x \in \mathds R^d$. Moreover, $X$ has the strong Feller property.

$(2)$ For every non-negative measurable function $g:(0,1]\times \mathds R^d \times \mathds R^d \rightarrow \mathds R_+$  vanishing
on $\{(s,x,y)\in (0,1]\times \mathds R^d \times \mathds R^d: x=y\}$ and any stopping time $T$, we have
\begin{equation} \mathds E_x\left(\sum_{s \leqslant T\wedge 1}g(s,X_{s-},X_s)\right)=\mathds E_x \bigg(\int_0^{T\wedge 1}\int_{\mathds R^d}
g(s,X_s,y)J(X_s,y)\,dy\,ds\bigg),
\end{equation} where $$J(x,y):=\frac{\kappa(x,y-x)}{|y-x|^{d+\alpha(x)}},\quad x,y \in \mathds R^d.$$

nodes.statement:
For any $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in\mathds R^d$, it holds that
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
&\mathds P_x\big(X_{\lambda t}\in B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}})\big)\\
&\geqslant \mathds P_x\big(\sigma_{B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2)}\leqslant \lambda t;
\sup_{s \in (\sigma_{B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2)},\lambda t)}\big|X_s-X_{\sigma_{B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2)}}\big|\leqslant t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2\big)\\
&\geqslant\mathds P_x\big(\sigma_{B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2)}\leqslant \lambda t ;\mathds P_{X_{\sigma_{B(y,
t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2)}}}\big(\sup_{0\leqslant s \leqslant \lambda t}|X_s-X_0|\leqslant
 t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2\big)\big)\\
&\geqslant \mathds P_x\big(\sigma_{B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2)}\leqslant \lambda t\big)
\cdot \inf_{z \in B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2)}\mathds P_z\big(
\tau_{B(z,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2)}>\lambda t\big),
\end{split}
\end{equation}
where in the second inequality we have used the strong Markov property.

Following the proof of \eqref{l3-2-8}, we know that
$t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}\geqslant C_1 t^{{1}/{\alpha(z)}}$ for every $z \in B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2)$.
Hence, there exists a constant $0<\lambda_0<1$ such that for all $0<\lambda<\lambda_0$
and $z \in B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2)$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
&\mathds P_z\big(\tau_{B(z,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2)}>\lambda t\big)
\geqslant \mathds P_z\big(\tau_{B(z,{C_1t^{{1}/{\alpha(z)}}}/{2})}>\lambda t\big)\geqslant {1}/{2},
\end{split}
\end{equation}
where the last inequality  follows from \eqref{l4-3-1}.
On the other hand, by the L\'evy system \eqref{p4-4-1}, for $\lambda>0$ small enough and for any $x,y\in \mathds R^d$ with $
|x-y|>5\max\{t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}},t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}\}$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
 \mathds P_x\big(\sigma_{B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2)}\leqslant \lambda t\big)
&\geqslant \mathds P_x\big(X_{\lambda t \wedge \tau_{B(x,t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}})}}\in B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2)\big)\\
&=\mathds E_x\bigg(\int_0^{\lambda t \wedge \tau_{B(x,t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}})}}
\int_{B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2)}\frac{du}{|X_s-u|^{d+\alpha(X_s)}}\,ds\bigg)\\
&\succeq \lambda t^{1+({d}/{\alpha(y)})}\cdot \inf_{z \in B(x,t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}})}\frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(z)}}
\cdot \mathds P_x\big(\tau_{B(x,t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}})}\geqslant \lambda t\big)\\
&\succeq \frac{t^{1+({d}/{\alpha(y)})}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}},
\end{split}
\end{equation}
where in the first inequality we used the fact that
$|x-y|\geqslant 5\max\{t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}},t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}\}$ implies $B(x,t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}})\cap
B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2)=\emptyset$, the second inequality follows from the fact that
$|z-u|\preceq |x-y|$ for any $z \in B\big(x,t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}}\big)$
and $u \in B\big(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2\big)$, and in the last inequality we used
\eqref{l4-3-1} and the fact that for any $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\geqslant 5t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}}$ and $z \in
B(x,t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}})$ and for every $0<t\leqslant 1$,
\begin{align*}
|x-y|^{-d-\alpha(z)}&\succeq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha(x)+C_2|x-z|^{\beta_0}}\succeq t^{C_2t^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_1}}}|x-y|^{-d-\alpha(x)}\succeq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha(x)}.
\end{align*}

According to \eqref{t4-4-2}, \eqref{t4-4-3} and \eqref{t4-4-4}, we obtain
that for any $|x-y|>5t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}}$ and $\lambda$ small enough,
\begin{equation} \mathds P_x\big(X_{\lambda t}\in B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}})\big)\succeq
\frac{t^{1+({d}/{\alpha(y)})}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}}.
\end{equation}
Hence, we arrive at
\begin{align*}
p(t,x,y)&=\int_{\mathds R^d}p(\lambda t,x,z)p((1-\lambda)t,z,y)\,dz\\
&\geqslant \int_{B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}})}
p(\lambda t,x,z)p((1-\lambda)t,z,y)\,dz\\
&\geqslant \inf_{|z-y|\leqslant t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}}p((1-\lambda)t,z,y)
\int_{B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}})}p(\lambda t,x,z)\,dz\\
&\succeq \inf_{|z-y|\leqslant C_3t^{{1}/{\alpha(z)}}}p((1-\lambda)t,z,y)
\int_{B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}})}p(\lambda t,x,z)\,dz\\
&\succeq t^{-{d}/{\alpha(y)}} \mathds P_x\big(X_{\lambda t}\in B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}})\big)\succeq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}},
\end{align*}
where the third inequality follows from the fact that $t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}\asymp t^{{1}/{\alpha(z)}}$ for every
$|y-z|\leqslant t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}$, in the forth inequality we used \eqref{p4-3-1}, and in the last inequality we used \eqref{t4-4-5}.
Therefore, \eqref{t4-4-1} has been proved.

nodes.statement:
{\bf{Case (c): $|w|>{1}/{2}$}.}

By adjusting the constants properly, it is easy to verify that
\begin{align*}
I_1+I_2&\preceq \int_{\{|z|\leqslant {1}/{4}\}}\big[\big(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\big)\wedge 1\big]
\rho^{y,0}_1(t,w{+} z)\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\,dz +\int_{\{|z|>{1}/{4}\}}\rho^{y,0}_1(t,w{+} z)\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\underline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\,dz\\
&=:J_1+J_2.
\end{align*}
Note that when $|w|>{1}/{2}$ and $|z|\leqslant {1}/{4}$,
$|w{+} z|\geqslant |w|-|z|\geqslant {|w|}/{2}>{1}/{4}$, which implies
that
$$\rho^{y,0}_1(t,w{+} z)\preceq \frac{t}{|w|^{d+\alpha_1}}.$$ On the other hand,
\begin{align*}
&\int_{{\{|z|\leqslant 1\}}}\big[\big(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\big)\wedge 1\big]
\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\,dz\\
&\preceq \int_{{\{|z|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}\}}}\big(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\big)
\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\,dz+\int_{\{t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}<|z|\leqslant 1\}}\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\,dz\\
&\preceq (1+|\log t|)t^{-{\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)}}.
\end{align*}
Therefore, we obtain
\begin{align*}
J_1&\preceq \frac{t}{|w|^{d+\alpha_1}} \int_{{\{|z|\leqslant {1}/{4}\}}}\big[\big(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\big)\wedge 1\big]
\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\,dz\\
&\preceq \frac{\big(1+|\log t|\big)t^{1-({\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)})}}{|w|^{d+\alpha_1}}\preceq \big(1+|\log t|\big)t^{1-({\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)})}\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w).
\end{align*}
Meanwhile,
\begin{align*}
J_2&\preceq \int_{\{|z|>{|w|}/{2}\}}\!\!\rho^{y,0}_1(t,w{+} z)\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\underline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\,dz +\!
\int_{\{{1}/{4}<|z|<{|w|}/{2}\}}\!\!\rho^{y,0}_1(t,w{+} z)\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\underline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\,dz\\
&\preceq
\frac{1+|\log|w||}{|w|^{d+\underline{\alpha}(y;x)}} \int_{\{|z|>{|w|}/{2}\}}\!\!
\rho^{y,0}_1(t,w{+} z)\,dz +\!
\frac{t}{|w|^{d+\alpha_1}}\int_{\{|z|>{1}/{4}\}}\!\!\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\alpha_1}}\,dz\\
&\preceq \frac{1+|\log |w||}{|w|^{d+\alpha_1}}\preceq (1+|\log |w||)\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w),
\end{align*}
where the second step above follows from  the following property
\begin{equation*}
\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w{+} z)\preceq |w|^{-d-\alpha_1}\quad \textrm{ when }
|z|<{|w|}/{2}\textrm{ and }\ |w|>{1}/{2},
\end{equation*}
and the third step is due to \eqref{l3-1-1-00}.
Hence, for all $w\in \mathds R^d$ with $|w|>{1}/{2}$,
$$ I_1\preceq J_1+J_2\preceq \big[1+|\log |w||+(1+|\log t|)t^{-{\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)}}\big]\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w)$$ and
$$ I_2\preceq J_2\preceq  (1+|\log |w||)\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w).
$$
Combining all the three cases together,  we finish the proof.

nodes.name: $z$-independent $\kappa$: bound $J_1$, $J_2$ and $\mathcal L^y p^y$
nodes.statement:
(1)  We first assume that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$.


By \eqref{e2-3}, for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y \in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|>R_1$, we have
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
 | {\mathcal L}^x p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)|
& \preceq \int_{\{|z|\leqslant {R_1}/{2}\}}|\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)|\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\
&\quad +\int_{\{|z|>{R_1}/{2}\}} \big(p^y(t,x-y\pm z)+p^y(t,x-y)\big)\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\
&=:J_1+J_2.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Applying \eqref{p1-1-1} and using the mean value theorem, we can get
\begin{align*}
J_1&\preceq \int_{\{|z|\leqslant {R_1}/{2}\}}|\nabla^2 p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y+\theta_{x,y,z}z)||z|^{2-d-\alpha(x)}\, dz\\
&\preceq \int_{\{|z|\leqslant {R_1}/{2}\}}\frac{t}{(t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}+|x-y+\theta_{x,y, z}z|)^{d+\alpha(y)+2}}
|z|^{2-d-\alpha(x)}\, dz\\
&\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)+2}}\int_{\{|z|\leqslant
{R_1}/{2}\}}|z|^{2-d-\alpha(x)}\, dz\preceq
\frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)+2}}\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}=\rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y),
\end{align*}
where in the first inequality $\theta_{x,y,z}$ is a constant depending on
$x,y,z$ such that $|\theta_{x,y,z}|\leqslant 1$, and the third inequality follows
from the fact that $$|x-y+\theta_{x,y,z}z|\geqslant {|x-y|}/{2}\geqslant
{R_1}/{2} \geqslant C_0 t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}\quad\textrm{ for any } z\in \mathds R^d\textrm{ with } |z|\leqslant
{R_1}/{2}.$$
On the other hand, according to \eqref{p1-1-1-1-0} and \eqref{r1-1-1}, we have
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
J_2&\preceq \int_{\{|z|>{R_1}/{2}\}}\rho^{y,0}_1(t,x-y\pm z)\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz +
\rho^{y,0}_1(t,x-y) \int_{\{|z|>{R_1}/{2}\}}\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz \preceq  \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Hence, for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|>R_1$,
$$| {\mathcal L}^x p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)|\preceq\rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y).$$


Following the same argument above, we have for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|>R_1$,
\begin{equation} | {\mathcal L}^y p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)|\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}\preceq \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y).\end{equation}
Therefore, for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|>R_1$,
\begin{align*}
|q_0(t,x,y)|&\leqslant | {\mathcal L}^x p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)|+| {\mathcal L}^y p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)|\preceq
\rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y).
\end{align*}
By now we have shown the second case in the estimate \eqref{l2-1-2}.
From \eqref{l1-2-1b} and \eqref{l2-1-2}, we arrive at
\eqref{l2-1-33a} immediately.
nodes.statement_short: $z$-independent $\kappa$: bound $J_1$, $J_2$ and $\mathcal L^y p^y$

nodes.statement:
(2) Next we consider the case that $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$.
With the estimate \eqref{l2-1-1} and the condition
${\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}>({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1$ at hand, we can follow the same argument as in \eqref{p2-1-2a} to verify the
upper bound in \eqref{p2-1-1a} for the case that $|x-y|\leqslant t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}$.

When $|x-y|>t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}$, we still define
$J_1$ and $J_2$ via \eqref{p2-1-2}. By carefully tracking the proof above, we find that the argument for the
estimates of $J_2$ in part (1) still works. So it remains to consider upper bound for
$J_1$.
According to \eqref{p1-1-2}, we have
\begin{align*}
J_1&\preceq \int_{\{|z|\leqslant {|x-y|}/{2}\}}
\big[\big(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\big)\wedge 1\big] \cdot
\big(\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x-y\pm z)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x-y)\big)\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\
&\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\int
\big[\big(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\big)\wedge 1\big] \cdot
\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\
&\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\cdot \bigg(\int_{\{|z|\leqslant t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}\}}
t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^{2-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz+\int_{\{|z|> t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}\}}|z|^{-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz\bigg)\\
&\preceq t^{1-({\alpha(x)}/{\alpha(y)})}\cdot \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\preceq t^{1-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})}\cdot \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)}},
\end{align*}
where the second inequality above follows from
$$ \rho^{y,0}_1(t,x-y\pm z)\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\quad\textrm{ for any }|z|\leqslant {|x-y|}/{2}.$$
Combining this with the estimate of $J_2$ in part (1) yields
\begin{align*}
|q_0(t,x,y)|&\preceq
\left| {\mathcal L}^x p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)\right|+\left| {\mathcal L}^xp^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)\right|\preceq t^{1-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})}\cdot \bigg(\frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}}+\frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\bigg),
\end{align*}
which implies that \eqref{p2-1-1a} holds for every $x,y \in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|>t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}$. The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: General $\kappa$: same argument with the extra factor $t^{1-\alpha_2/\alpha_1}$

nodes.name: Notation for $\nabla p^y$
nodes.statement: In the remainder of this paper, we denote $\nabla p^y(t,\cdot)(x)$ by $\nabla p^y(t,x)$ for simplicity.
nodes.statement_short: Notation for $\nabla p^y$

nodes.name: $z$-independent $\kappa$: five cases
nodes.statement_short: $z$-independent $\kappa$: five cases

nodes.name: Set up the five-case analysis
nodes.statement: (1) We first consider the case that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$. Let $R_1:=R_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma)$ be a positive constant to be determined later. The proof is split into the following five different cases.
nodes.statement_short: Set up the five-case analysis

nodes.name: Case $|x-x'|>R_1$
nodes.statement_short: Case $|x-x'|>R_1$

nodes.name: Case $C_0t^{1/\alpha(y)}\le|x-x'|\le R_1$
nodes.statement:
{\bf Case (b): $C_0t^{1/\alpha(y)}\leqslant |x-x'|\leqslant R_1$ for some small
constant $C_0>0$.}


According to \eqref{l2-1-2} again, we have
\begin{align*} |q_0(t,x,y)|\preceq& \rho_{-\gamma}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x-y)\preceq t^{{(\beta_0-\alpha(x)\theta)}/{\alpha(x)}} \rho_{-\gamma+\theta-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x)})}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x-y) \\
\preceq&|x-x'|^{{{\alpha(y)(\beta_0-\alpha(x)\theta)}/{\alpha(x)}}} \rho_{-\gamma+\theta-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x)})}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x-y) \\
\preceq&|x-x'|^{{\alpha_1(\beta_0-\alpha_2\theta)/{\alpha(x)}}} \rho_{-\gamma+\theta-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x)})}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x-y),  \end{align*}
where the third inequality is due to $t\preceq |x-x'|^{\alpha(y)}$.
Then
\begin{align*}&|q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|\\
&\leqslant |q_0(t,x,y)|+|q_0(t,x',y)|\\
&\preceq |x-\!x'|^{{\alpha_1(\beta_0-\alpha_2\theta)/{\alpha(x)}}} \! \rho_{-\gamma+\theta-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x)})}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x-y)  +
|x-\!x'|^{{\alpha_1(\beta_0-\alpha_2\theta)/{\alpha(x')}}}\!
\rho_{-\gamma+\theta-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x')})}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x'\!-y)\\
&\preceq |x-\!x'|^{{\alpha_1(\beta_0-\alpha_2\theta)/{\alpha(x)}}}\Big(
\rho_{-\gamma+\theta-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x)})}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x\!-y)+
\rho_{-\gamma+\theta-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x')})}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x'\!-y)\Big).\end{align*}
Here in the last inequality we have used the fact that for $ x,x'\in
\mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|\leqslant R_1,$
\begin{equation} |x-x'|^{{\alpha_1(\beta_0-\alpha_2\theta)/{\alpha(x')}}}\preceq
|x-x'|^{{\alpha_1(\beta_0-\alpha_2\theta)/{\alpha(x)}}},
\end{equation}
which can be verified by following the argument of \eqref{l3-1-1a}.

Next, we mainly treat the case that $|x-x'|\leqslant C_0t^{1/\alpha(y)}$,
which we divide into three cases.
nodes.statement_short: Case $C_0t^{1/\alpha(y)}\le|x-x'|\le R_1$

nodes.name: Case $|x-x'|$ small and $|x-y|\ge R_1$: Taylor expansion of $\delta_{p^y}$
nodes.statement:
{\bf Case (c): $|x-x'|\leqslant C_0t^{1/\alpha(y)}$ and $|x-y|\geqslant R_1$.}

By the definition of $q_0(t,x,y)$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
 |q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|
&=\frac{1}{2}\bigg|\int_{\mathds R^d} \delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)\bigg(\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}-\frac{\kappa(y,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}} \bigg)\,dz\\
&\qquad\quad-\int_{\mathds R^d} \delta_{p^y}(t,x'-y;z)\bigg(\frac{\kappa(x',z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x')}}-\frac{\kappa(y,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}} \bigg)\,dz\bigg|\\
&\leqslant \frac{1}{2}\int_{\mathds R^d} |\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x'-y;z)| \bigg|\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}-\frac{\kappa(y,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}} \bigg|\,dz\\
&\quad+ \frac{1}{2}\int_{\mathds R^d} |\delta_{p^y}(t,x'-y;z)| \bigg|\frac{\kappa(x',z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x')}}-\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}} \bigg|\,dz\\
&=:J_1+J_2.
\end{split}
\end{equation}


Note that \begin{equation} \begin{split} \delta_{p^y}(t,x;z)=&p^y(t,x+z)+p^y(t,x-z)-2p^y(t,x)\\
=&\int_0^1 \frac{d}{d\theta}\Big(p^y(t,x+\theta z)+p^y(t,x-\theta z)\Big)\,d\theta\\
=&\int_0^1 \langle \nabla p^y(t,x+\theta z)-\nabla p^y(t,x-\theta z),z\rangle \,d\theta\\
=&\int_0^1 \Big\langle \int_{-1}^1 \frac{d}{d \theta'}\left(\nabla p^y(t,x+\theta'\theta z)\right)d\theta',z \Big\rangle \,d\theta\\
=&\int_0^1\int_{-1}^1 \nabla^2 p^y(t,x+\theta'\theta z)(\theta z, z)d\theta'\,d\theta,\end{split}\end{equation}
and so
\begin{align*}  \delta_{p^y}(t,x;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x';z)
&=\int_0^1\int_{-1}^1 \big(\nabla^2 p^y(t,x+\theta'\theta z)- \nabla^2 p^y(t,x'+\theta'\theta z)\big)(\theta z, z)\,d\theta'\,d\theta\\
&=\int_0^1\int_{-1}^1\int_0^1  \frac{d}{d\theta''}\Big(\nabla^2 p^y(t,x'+\theta''(x-x')+\theta'\theta z)\Big)
(\theta z, z)\,d\theta''d\theta'\,d\theta\\
&=\int_0^1\int_{-1}^1\int_0^1  \nabla^3 p^y(t,x'+\theta''(x-x')+\theta'\theta z)
(x-x',\theta z, z)\,d\theta''d\theta'\,d\theta,\end{align*} which implies that
\begin{align*}
 |\delta_{p^y}(t,x;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x';z) |
&\leqslant \Big(\int_0^1\int_{-1}^1\int_0^1 |\nabla^3 p^y(t,x'+\theta''(x-x')+\theta'\theta z)|\,\,d\theta''d\theta'\,d\theta\Big)
\cdot |z|^2|x-x'|.
\end{align*}
For every $x,x',z\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|\leqslant C_0 t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$, $|x|\geqslant cR_1$, $|x'|\geqslant cR_1$ and $|z|\leqslant {cR_1}/{4}$
for $C_0$ small enough, there exists a constant $c'>0$ such that for every $\theta\in(0,1)$, $\theta'\in(-1,1)$ and $\theta''\in(0,1)$, we have
$|x'+\theta''(x-x')+\theta'\theta z|\geqslant c'|x'|\geqslant c''R_1,$ which along with \eqref{p1-1-1} yields that
$$|\nabla^3 p^y(t,x'+\theta''(x-x')+\theta'\theta z)| \preceq \frac{t}{|x'|^{d+\alpha(y)+3}}.$$ Combining with all the estimates above, we arrive at that
for $|x-x'|\leqslant C_0t^{1/\alpha(y)}$, $|x|\geqslant cR_1$, $|x'|\geqslant cR_1$ and $|z|\leqslant {cR_1}/{4}$,
\begin{equation} |\delta_{p^y}(t,x;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x';z) |\preceq \frac{t|z|^2|x-x'|}{|x'|^{d+\alpha(y)+3}}.
   \end{equation}


Since $|x-x'|\leqslant C_0t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}\leqslant C_0$, $|x'-y|\geqslant cR_1$ holds for some constant $c>0$.
By taking $x=x-y$ and $x'=x'-y$ in \eqref{e:conpr1}, we obtain that for all $z\in\mathds R^d$ with $|z|\leqslant {cR_1}/{4}$,
\begin{equation} |\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x'-y;z) |\preceq \frac{t|z|^2|x-x'|}{|x'-y|^{d+\alpha(y)+3}}.  \end{equation}

Let \begin{equation} \begin{split}
J_1=&\frac{1}{2}\int_{\{|z|\leqslant {cR_1}/{4}\}} |\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x'-y;z)| \bigg|\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}-\frac{\kappa(y,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}} \bigg|\,dz\\
&+ \frac{1}{2}\int_{\{|z|> {cR_1}/{4}\}} |\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x'-y;z)| \bigg|\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}-\frac{\kappa(y,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}} \bigg|\,dz\\
=&:J_{11}+J_{12}.
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
 By \eqref{e:conpr2},
 \begin{align*}J_{11}\preceq &|x-x'|\frac{t}{|x'-y|^{d+\alpha(y)+3}} \int_{\{|z|\leqslant {cR_1}/{4}\}}\bigg( \frac{|z|^2}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}+\frac{|z|^2}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}} \bigg)\,dz\\
 \preceq& |x-x'|\frac{t}{|x'-y|^{d+\alpha(y)+3}} \preceq |x-x'|\frac{1}{|x'-y|^{d+\alpha_1}},
 \end{align*} where the last inequality is due to $|x'-y|>cR_1$ and $t\leqslant 1$.
On the other hand, according to \eqref{r1-1-1}, we have for any $x,y\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|>R_1$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
&\int_{\{|z|>{cR_1}/{4}\}} \rho_1^{y,0}(t,x-y\pm z) \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha (x)}}\,dz \preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}},\\
&\int_{\{|z|>{cR_1}/{4}\}} \rho_1^{y,0}(t,x-y) \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha (x)}}\,dz \preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Combining \eqref{p1-1-4} with \eqref{l3-1-3b} and the fact that $|z|>{cR_1}/{4}$ implies $|z|>C_1t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$, we arrive at
\begin{align*}
J_{12}&\preceq t^{-{1/\alpha(y)}}|x-x'| \int_{\{|z|>{cR_1}/{4}\}}\Big(\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x-y\pm z)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x-y)\\
&\qquad \qquad\qquad\qquad +\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x'-y\pm z)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x'-y)\Big)
\bigg(\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}+\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}} \bigg)\,dz\\
&\preceq t^{-{1/\alpha(y)}}|x-x'| \left( \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}+
\frac{1}{|x'-y|^{d+\alpha_1}} \right). \end{align*} By both of the
estimates above, we obtain that
 \begin{align*}J_1&\preceq t^{-{1/\alpha(y)}}|x-x'| \big( \rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y)+\rho_0^{y,0}(t,x'-y)\big)\preceq  |x-x'| \big( \rho_{-{1/\alpha(y)}}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x-y)+\rho_{-{1/\alpha(y)}}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x'-y)\big), \end{align*}
where the last inequality follows from the facts that $|x-y|\geqslant cR_1$ and $|x'-y|\geqslant c R_1$.


Let \begin{equation} \begin{split}
J_2=&\int_{\{|z|\leqslant {cR_1}/{4}\}} |\delta_{p^y}(t,x'-y;z)| \bigg|\frac{\kappa(x',z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x')}}-\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}} \bigg|\,dz\\
&+ \int_{\{|z|> {cR_1}/{4}\}} |\delta_{p^y}(t,x'-y;z)| \bigg|\frac{\kappa(x',z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x')}}-\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}} \bigg|\,dz\\
=&:J_{21}+J_{22}.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Since $|x'-y|>cR_1$, by \eqref{e:conpr0} and \eqref{p1-1-1}, we find that for any $|z|<{cR_1}/{4} $,
\begin{align*}|\delta_{p^y}(t,x'-y;z)|&\leqslant |z|^2\int_0^1\int_{-1}^1 |\nabla^2 p^y(t,x'-y+\theta'\theta z)|\,d\theta'\,d\theta \preceq |z|^2 \frac{ t}{ |x'-y|^{d+\alpha(y)+2}}.\end{align*}
 Thus,
 due to \eqref{e:pp},
 \begin{align*}J_{21} \preceq& |x-x'|^{\beta_0} \frac{t}{|x'-y|^{d+\alpha(y)+2}}\int_{\{|z|\leqslant {cR_1}/{4}\}} \!\!\frac{1+|\log |z||}{|z|^{d+\overline\alpha(x;x')}}|z|^2\,dz
 \preceq  |x-x'|^{\beta_0} \frac{1}{|x'-y|^{d+\alpha_1}},\end{align*} where we have used the facts that $|x'-y|>cR_1$ and $t<1$ in the second inequality.
On the other hand, when $|z|> {cR_1}/{4}$,
$$|\delta_{p^y}(t,x'-y;z)|\preceq p^y(t,x'-y\pm z)+p^y(t,x'-y).$$
Having this at hand and using \eqref{r1-1-2} and \eqref{p1-1-1-1-0}, we know that
$$\int_{\{|z|>{cR_1}/{4}\}} |\delta_{p^y}(t,x'-y;z)|\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\underline{\alpha}(x;x')}}\,dz
\preceq \frac{\log(1+|x'-y|)}{|x'-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}.$$
Then, by \eqref{e:pp}, we find that
\begin{align*}
J_{22}&\preceq |x-x'|^{\beta_0}\cdot \int_{\{|z|>{cR_1}/{4}\}}|\delta_{p^y}(t,x'-y;z)|\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\underline{\alpha}(x;x')}}\,dz  \preceq   |x-x'|^{\beta_0}\frac{\log(1+|x'-y|)}{|x'-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}.
\end{align*}
By the estimates for $J_{21}$ and $J_{22}$, we have
\begin{equation*}
J_2\preceq |x-x'|^{\beta_0}\log(1+|x'-y|)\rho^{y,0}_0(t,x'-y).
\end{equation*}

Putting the estimates of $J_1$ and $J_2$ together, we finally arrive at
\begin{align*}
|q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|\preceq & |x-x'|\big( \rho_{-{1/\alpha(y)}}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x-y)+\rho_{-{1/\alpha(y)}}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x'-y)\big)\\
&+|x-x'|^{\beta_0}\log(1+|x'-y|)\rho^{y,0}_0(t,x'-y).
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Case $|x-x'|$ small and $|x-y|\ge R_1$: Taylor expansion of $\delta_{p^y}$

nodes.name: Case $|x-x'|$ small and $t^{1/\alpha(y)}\le|x-y|<R_1$
nodes.statement_short: Case $|x-x'|$ small and $t^{1/\alpha(y)}\le|x-y|<R_1$

nodes.name: Case $|x-x'|$ small and $|x-y|<t^{1/\alpha(y)}$
nodes.statement_short: Case $|x-x'|$ small and $|x-y|<t^{1/\alpha(y)}$

nodes.name: General $\kappa$: adapt the argument
nodes.statement:
(2) Now we study the estimate for $|q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|$ under the assumption that
$\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$.
Recall that, by  \eqref{l2-1-1}, we have
\begin{equation} |q_0(t,x,y)|\preceq \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma_2 }(t,x-y),\quad (t,x,y)\in (0,1]\times \mathds R^d \times \mathds R^d,
\end{equation}
where $\gamma_2 =:\gamma+({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1$.

Using \eqref{p3-1-8} and following the arguments in {\bf Case (a)} and {\bf Case (b)} of  part (1) above, we derive that for every $(t,x,y)\in (0,1]\times \mathds R^d \times \mathds R^d$ such that
$|x-x'|\geqslant C_0t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$ (which includes both $|x-x'|>R_1$
and $C_0t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}\leqslant |x-x'|\leqslant R_1$, and where as in (1) the constant $C_0$ is chosen to be small enough) and $\gamma_2 <\theta<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$,
\begin{align*}
|q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|& \preceq
\big(|x-x'|^{\alpha_1(\beta_0-\alpha_2\theta)/{\alpha(x)}}\wedge 1\big)\\
&\quad\times\big(\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma_2 +\theta-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x)})}(t,x-y)
+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma_2 +\theta-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x')})}(t,x'-y)\big).
\end{align*}

Note that
in the proofs of {\bf Case (d)} and {\bf Case (e)} above, we do not need the assumption that
$\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$, so the conclusions there are still true, which in particular means that
\eqref{p3-1-2a-1} holds for {\bf Case (d)} and {\bf Case (e)}.
Now we turn to the case that $|x-x'|\leqslant C_0t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$ and $|x-y|>R_1$, i.e., the {\bf Case (c)} above.
We still define
$J_{11}$, $J_{12}$, $J_{21}$ and $J_{22}$ as those in \eqref{p3-1-2aa}, \eqref{p3-1-3a} and \eqref{p3-1-4a}, respectively.


For $J_{11}$, we apply \eqref{p1-1-4} instead of \eqref{e:conpr2} in part (1), and derive that
\begin{align*}
J_{11}\preceq \,&t^{-{1/\alpha(y)}}|x-x'|\int_{\{|z|\leqslant {cR_1}/{4}\}}
[(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}} |z|^2)\wedge 1]\\
&\times\Big(
\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x-y)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x'-y)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x-y\pm z)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x'-y\pm z)\Big)\cdot\bigg(\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}
+\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\bigg)\,dz.
\end{align*}
Note that $|x-y|>R_1$. By \eqref{r1-1-1a}, we arrive at
\begin{align*}
&\int_{\{|z|\leqslant {cR_1}/{4}\}}[(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}} |z|^2)\wedge 1]
\big(
\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x-y)
+\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x-y\pm z)\big) \bigg(\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}
+\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\bigg)\,dz\preceq \frac{t^{1-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}},
\end{align*}
which yields that
\begin{equation*}
J_{11}\preceq\, |x-x'|\big(\rho_{-\gamma_2-({1/\alpha(y)})}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x-y)
+\rho_{-\gamma_2-({1/\alpha(y)})}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x'-y)\big).
\end{equation*}
Similarly, using \eqref{p1-1-2} instead of \eqref{p1-1-1} in the estimate of $J_{21}$ and applying
\eqref{r1-1-2a}, we obtain
\begin{align*}
J_{21} &\preceq |x-x'|^{\beta_0}\cdot \bigg(
\int_{\{|z|\leqslant {cR_1}/{4}\}}[(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}} |z|^2)\wedge 1]
\big[\rho^{y,0}_1(t,x'-y\pm z)+\rho^{y,0}_1(t,x'-y)\big]
\frac{1+|\log |z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(x;x')}}\,dz\bigg)\\
&\preceq |x-x'|^{\beta_0}(1+|\log t|+|\log|x'-y||)\rho_{1-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})}^{y,0}(t,x'-y).
\end{align*}
As explained before, the proofs for estimates of $J_{12}$ and
$J_{22}$ in (1) do not require the condition that $\kappa(x,z)$ is
independent of $z$, so those estimates still hold here.

By the estimates for $J_{11}$, $J_{12}$, $J_{21}$ and $J_{22}$, we know that for
every $|x-x'|\leqslant C_0t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$ and $|x-y|>R_1$,
\begin{align*}
|q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|
 \preceq& |x-x'|\cdot\big[
\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma_2-({1/\alpha(y)})}(t,x-y)
+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma_2-({1/\alpha(y)})}(t,x'-y)\big]\\
&+|x-x'|^{\beta_0}\big(1+\log(1+|x'-y|)\big)\rho^{y,0}_{-\gamma_2}(t,x'-y).
\end{align*}
Combining the estimates above for all the cases, we can find a constant $C_0>0$ small enough such that for
every $|x-x'|\leqslant C_0 t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$ and
$\gamma,\varepsilon>0$,
\begin{align*}
|q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|\preceq& |x-x'|\cdot\big[
\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma_2 -({1/\alpha(y)})}(t,x-y)
+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma_2 -({1/\alpha(y)})}(t,x'-y)\big]\\
&+|x-x'|^{\beta_0}|x-y|^{\varepsilon}\mathds 1_{\{|x-y|>R_0\}}\rho^{y,0}_{-\gamma_2}(t,x-y)\\
&+|x-x'|^{\beta_0}|x'-y|^{\varepsilon}\mathds 1_{\{|x'-y|>R_0\}}\rho^{y,0}_{-\gamma_2}(t,x'-y).
\end{align*}
Then, by the same argument for \eqref{p3-1-6} and all the conclusions above, we can immediately show that \eqref{p3-1-2a-1} holds.

nodes.statement: (1) The proof is split into three cases.

nodes.name: Case $|x-y|>2$
nodes.statement_short: Case $|x-y|>2$

nodes.name: Intermediate case
nodes.statement:
{\bf Case (b): $2t^{{1}/{\overline{\alpha}(y;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})}}\leqslant |x-y|\leqslant 2$.}

Let $J_1$ and $J_2$ be defined by \eqref{l3-2-1a}. If $|z-y|\geqslant
{|x-y|}/{2}$ and $0<s<t<1$, then $|z-y|\geqslant {|x-y|}/{2}$,
and so
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
\rho_0^{y,0}(s,z-y)&\preceq
\begin{cases}
|z-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)},& |z-y|\leqslant 1,\\
 |z-y|^{-d-\alpha_1},& |z-y|>1
\end{cases}
\\
&\preceq \begin{cases}
|x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)},&|z-y|\leqslant 1,\\
|x-y|^{-d-\alpha_1},& |z-y|>1
\end{cases}
\\
&\preceq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)}\preceq \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y),
\end{split}
\end{equation}
where in
the third inequality we have used the fact that
$$|x-y|^{-d-\alpha_1}\preceq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)}\quad \textrm{ for all }|x-y|\leqslant 2 ,$$ and the last
inequality follows from
$$|x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)} \preceq  \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y)\quad\textrm{ for all } |x-y|\geqslant 2t^{{1}/{\overline{\alpha}(y;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})}}\geqslant 2t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}.$$
Using \eqref{l3-2-6} and following the same argument of \eqref{l3-2-4}, we know that \eqref{l3-2-4} is satisfied too.


If $|z-y|<{|x-y|}/{2}$, then $|x-z|\geqslant {|x-y|}/{2}$,
and so we obtain
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
\rho_0^{z,0}(t-s,x-z)&\preceq
\begin{cases}
|x-z|^{-d-\alpha(z)},& |x-z|\leqslant 1,\\
|x-z|^{-d-\alpha_1}, & |x-z|>1
\end{cases}
\\
&\preceq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha(z)} \preceq |x-y|^{\alpha(y)-\alpha(z)}\cdot|x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)}\\
&\preceq |x-y|^{-|\alpha(y)-\alpha(z)|}\cdot|x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)}\\
&\preceq |x-y|^{-C|x-y|^{\beta_0}}\cdot|x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)}\\
&\preceq \exp\big(C|\log|x-y||\cdot|x-y|^{\beta_0}\big)\cdot|x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)}\\
&\preceq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)}\preceq \rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y),
\end{split}
\end{equation}
where in the second inequality we used the fact that if $|x-z|\geqslant {|x-y|}/{2}$ and $|x-y|\leqslant 2$, then
$|x-z|^{-d-\alpha_1}\preceq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha_1}\preceq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha(z)},$
the fifth inequality follows from the fact that
$$|\alpha(y)-\alpha(z)|\preceq |z-y|^{\beta_0}\leqslant C |x-y|^{\beta_0}\quad\textrm{ for all }|z-y|\leqslant {|x-y|}/{2},$$
in the seventh inequality we used $$\sup_{z\in \mathds R^d: |z|\leqslant 2}\exp\big(C|\log
|z||\cdot|z|^{\beta_0}\big)<\infty,$$ and the last inequality is due to
the same argument of the last one in \eqref{l3-2-6}.


Using the above inequality for $\rho_0^{z,0}(t-s,x-z)$ and following the same procedure of \eqref{l3-2-5a},
we know that \eqref{l3-2-5a} still holds.

Therefore, according to the estimates for $J_1$ and $J_2$, \eqref{l3-2-1} also holds in this case.
nodes.statement_short: Intermediate case

nodes.name: Near-diagonal case with two subcases
nodes.statement:
{\bf Case (c): $|x-y|\leqslant
2t^{{1}/{\overline{\alpha}(y;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})}}$.}


Note that for any $t \in (0,1]$ and $y \in \mathds R^d$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
1\leqslant&
\frac{t^{{1}/{\overline{\alpha}(y;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})}}}{t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}}\leqslant
t^{-\frac{\overline{\alpha}(y;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})-\alpha(y)}{\alpha(y)\overline{\alpha}(y;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})}}
\leqslant
t^{-\frac{Ct^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}}}{\alpha_1^2}}\leqslant \exp\big(C|\log
t|\cdot t^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}} \big)\leqslant C_1 ,
\end{split}
\end{equation}
hence $|x-y|\leqslant 2t^{{1}/{\overline{\alpha}(y;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})}}$
implies that $|x-y|\leqslant C_2 t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$ for some constant
$C_2>0$.

On the other hand,
\begin{align*}
 \int_{\mathds R^d}\rho_{\theta_1}^{z,\beta_1}(t-s,x-z)\rho_{\theta_2}^{y,\beta_2}(s,z-y)\,dz
&\leqslant \int_{\{|z-y|> t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}\}}\rho_{\theta_1}^{z,\beta_1}(t-s,x-z)\rho_{\theta_2}^{y,\beta_2}(s,z-y)\,dz\\
&\quad+\int_{\{|z-y|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}\}}\rho_{\theta_1}^{z,\beta_1}(t-s,x-z)\rho_{\theta_2}^{y,\beta_2}(s,z-y)\, dz\\
&=:J_1+J_2.
\end{align*}

If $|z-y|\geqslant t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}>s^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$, then
\begin{align*}
\rho_0^{y,0}(s,z-y)\preceq |z-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)}\preceq t^{-({d+\alpha(y)})/{\alpha(y)}}\preceq \rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y),
\end{align*}
where the second inequality follows from $|z-y|\geqslant t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$, and the last inequality
is due to $t^{-({d+\alpha(y)})/{\alpha(y)}}\preceq \rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y)$ for all $|x-y|\leqslant C_2t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$. Applying the above estimate for $\rho_0^{y,0}(s,z-y)$ and following the same argument of \eqref{l3-2-4}, we can find that \eqref{l3-2-4} still holds
for $J_1$ here.



Now we turn to estimate for $J_2$, which is divided into the following two subcases:

{\bf Subcase (c1): $s>{t}/{2}$.}

If $|z-y|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$, then
\begin{align*}
\rho_0^{y,0}(s,z-y)&\preceq s^{-({d/\alpha(y)})-1}\preceq t^{-({d/\alpha(y)})-1}\preceq \rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y),
\end{align*}
where the second inequality follows
from $s>{t}/{2}$, and in the last inequality we have used the fact that
$t^{-({d/\alpha(y)})-1}\preceq \rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y)$ for all $|x-y|\leqslant C_2t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$.

Having the above estimate for $\rho_0^{y,0}(s,z-y)$ at hand, we also can follow the same procedure of \eqref{l3-2-4} to get that \begin{align*}
J_2&\preceq (t-s)^{\theta_1+(({\beta_1+\beta_2})/{\alpha(x)})-1}s^{\theta_2}\rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y)+
(t-s)^{\theta_1+({\beta_1}/{\alpha(x)})-1}s^{\theta_2}\rho_0^{y,\beta_2}(t,x-y).
\end{align*}


{\bf Subcase (c2): $s\leqslant {t}/{2}$.}

If $|z-y|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$,
then we have
\begin{align*}
\rho_0^{z,0}(t-s,x-z)&\preceq (t-s)^{-({d}/{\alpha(z)})-1}\preceq t^{-({d}/{\alpha(z)})-1}\preceq t^{-|({d}/{\alpha(z)})-({d/\alpha(y)})|}\cdot t^{-({d/\alpha(y)})-1}\\
&\preceq t^{-Ct^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}}}\cdot t^{-({d/\alpha(y)})-1}\preceq t^{-({d/\alpha(y)})-1}\preceq \rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y),
\end{align*}
where the second inequality is due to $(t-s)\geqslant {t}/{2}$, in the
fourth inequality we used the fact that
$|\alpha(y)-\alpha(z)|\preceq |z-y|^{\beta_0}\preceq t^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha(y)}}\preceq
t^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}},$ the fifth inequality follows from
$$\sup_{t \in (0,1]}t^{-Ct^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}}}\preceq \sup_{t \in (0,1]}
\exp\big(C|\log t|t^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}}\big)<\infty,$$ and the last
inequality is again due to the fact that $t^{-({d/\alpha(y)})-1}\preceq
\rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y)$ for all $|x-y|\leqslant C_2t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$.

Using the above estimate for $\rho_0^{z,0}(t-s,x-z)$ and following the same procedure of \eqref{l3-2-5a},  we
can also get \eqref{l3-2-5a}.

Combining both estimates for $J_1$ and $J_2$, we know \eqref{l3-2-1} holds for {\bf Case (c)}.
Therefore, the proof of \eqref{l3-2-0} is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Near-diagonal case with two subcases

nodes.statement:
{\bf Subcase (c2): $s\leqslant {t}/{2}$.}

If $|z-y|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$,
then we have
\begin{align*}
\rho_0^{z,0}(t-s,x-z)&\preceq (t-s)^{-({d}/{\alpha(z)})-1}\preceq t^{-({d}/{\alpha(z)})-1}\preceq t^{-|({d}/{\alpha(z)})-({d/\alpha(y)})|}\cdot t^{-({d/\alpha(y)})-1}\\
&\preceq t^{-Ct^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}}}\cdot t^{-({d/\alpha(y)})-1}\preceq t^{-({d/\alpha(y)})-1}\preceq \rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y),
\end{align*}
where the second inequality is due to $(t-s)\geqslant {t}/{2}$, in the
fourth inequality we used the fact that
$|\alpha(y)-\alpha(z)|\preceq |z-y|^{\beta_0}\preceq t^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha(y)}}\preceq
t^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}},$ the fifth inequality follows from
$$\sup_{t \in (0,1]}t^{-Ct^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}}}\preceq \sup_{t \in (0,1]}
\exp\big(C|\log t|t^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}}\big)<\infty,$$ and the last
inequality is again due to the fact that $t^{-({d/\alpha(y)})-1}\preceq
\rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y)$ for all $|x-y|\leqslant C_2t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$.

Using the above estimate for $\rho_0^{z,0}(t-s,x-z)$ and following the same procedure of \eqref{l3-2-5a},  we
can also get \eqref{l3-2-5a}.

Combining both estimates for $J_1$ and $J_2$, we know \eqref{l3-2-1} holds for {\bf Case (c)}.
Therefore, the proof of \eqref{l3-2-0} is complete.

\eqref{l3-2-4} and \eqref{l3-2-5a}, and follow the same arguments as above to prove \eqref{l3-2-1}.

nodes.name: Inductive bounds on $q_n$, convergence of the series, $q$ solves the equation
nodes.statement:
(i) According to \eqref{l2-1-2}, if $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$, then
$$|q_0(t,x,y)|\preceq \rho_{-\gamma}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x-y),\quad t\in(0,1] \textrm{ and } x,y \in \mathds R^d.$$
Therefore, by Corollary \ref{l3-3},
\begin{align*}|q_1(t,x,y)|\preceq&\int_0^t\int \rho_{-\gamma}^{z,\beta_0}(t-s,x-z) \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}(s,z-y)\,dz\,ds\\
\preceq& \mathscr{B}\big(({\widehat\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma, ({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma\big)
\big(\rho_{2(({\widehat
\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma+(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,\beta_0}\big)(t,x-y),\end{align*}
where $\widehat \beta_0:=\beta_0 \wedge (\alpha_2/2)$.


Suppose now that
$$|q_n(t,x,y)|\leqslant \omega_n\Big(\rho_{(n+1)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma+n(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y),\quad n\geqslant0,$$
where the constant $\omega_n$ is to be determined later.
Hence, according to Corollary \ref{l3-3} again,
\begin{align*}|q_{n+1}(t,x,y)|\leqslant& C\int_0^t\int \rho_{-\gamma}^{z,\beta_0}(t-s,x-z) \omega_n \Big(\rho_{(n+1)(({\widehat\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma+n(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(s,z-y)\,dz\,ds\\
\leqslant&C \omega_n \mathscr{B}(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma, (n+1)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)) \Big(\rho_{(n+2)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma+(n+1)(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y)\\
=&: \omega_{n+1}\Big(\rho_{(n+2)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma+(n+1)(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y), \end{align*} where $$ \omega_{n+1}= C \mathscr{B}\big(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma, (n+1)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)\omega_n ,$$
and $C$ is a constant independent of $t,n,x$ and $y$.
Note that $\omega_0\leqslant C$ and $\mathscr{B}(\gamma, \beta)=\frac{\Gamma(\gamma)\Gamma(\beta)}{\Gamma(\gamma+\beta)}$, where $\Gamma$ is the standard Gamma function. By iteration procedure we have
\begin{align*}\omega_n\leqslant &C^{n+1}\mathscr{B}\big(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma, n(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)\\
&\times\mathscr{B}\big(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma, (n-1)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)\cdots\mathscr{B}\big(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma, ({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma\big)\\
=&\frac{\big[C \Gamma(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma )\big]^{n+1}}{\Gamma\big((n+1)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)}.\end{align*}
Therefore,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
|q_n(t,x,y)|\leqslant &\frac{\big[C \Gamma(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma )\big]^{n+1}}{\Gamma\big((n+1)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)} \Big(\rho_{(n+1)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}
+\rho_{-\gamma+n(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y),\end{split}
\end{equation}
and so combing all estimates together
$$\sum_{n=0}^\infty |q_n(t,x,y)|\leqslant \left(\sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{\big[C \Gamma(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma )\big]^{n+1}}{\Gamma\big((n+1)(({\widehat\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)}\right)\Big(\rho_{2(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y),$$ which means that $q(t,x,y):=\sum_{n=0}^\infty q_n(t,x,y)$ is absolutely convergent, and
$$|q(t,x,y)|\leqslant C_1  \Big(\rho_{2(({\widehat\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y).$$
Thus, \eqref{p3-1-1} is proved by using the fact that $\beta_0\leqslant 2\widehat \beta_0$ and changing the constant $\gamma$ properly. From \eqref{eq3-1}
and the fact $q(t,x,y)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}q_n(t,x,y)$, it is easy to see that $q(t,x,y)$ solves the equation \eqref{eq2-2}.

nodes.name: Hölder estimate of $q$
nodes.statement:
(iii) It suffices to prove \eqref{p3-1-1a} for the case that $|x-x'|\leqslant R_1$  holds with some $R_1>0$, since the case
that $|x-x'|>1$ follows from \eqref{p3-1-1} immediately.
For any (fixed) $\varepsilon>0$ small enough, let $\tilde \rho^{y,\beta}_{\gamma}$ be defined by \eqref{p3-1-7}.  By \eqref{p3-1-1a-1}, we have
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
&|q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|\\
&\preceq (|x-x'|^{\tilde \theta}\wedge 1)\times \bigg[\left(\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x)})}\right)(t,x-y)  + \left(\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x')})}\right)(t,x'-y)\bigg],
\end{split}
\end{equation}
where $\tilde \theta:=\alpha_1(\beta_0-\alpha_2\theta)/{\alpha(x)}$. Since $\beta_0^*=\beta_0<\alpha(x)$, by  \eqref{e1-3} we can find a constant
$R_1>0$ small enough such that $\beta_0< \alpha(x)\wedge\alpha(x')$ for any $x'\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|\leqslant R_1$.
Then, according to \eqref{eq2-2}, it holds that
\begin{align*}
&|q(t,x,y)-q(t,x',y)|\\
&\leqslant |q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|+\int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d}
|q_0(t-s,x,z)-q_0(t-s,x',z)||q(s,z,y)|\,dz\,ds\\
&\preceq (|x-x'|^{\tilde \theta}\wedge 1)\\
&\quad\times\bigg\{ \Big[\big(\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x)})}\big)(t,x-y)
+ \left(\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x')})}\right)(t,x'-y)\Big]\\
&\quad \quad+\int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d} \Big[\big(\tilde \rho^{z,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{z,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x)})}\big)(t-s,x-z)\\
&\qquad\qquad\quad\qquad+ \big(\tilde \rho^{z,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{z,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x')})}
\big)(t-s,x'-z)\Big]
\Big[\big(
\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}\big)(s,z-y)\Big]\,dz\,ds \bigg\}\\
&\preceq (|x-x'|^{\tilde \theta}\wedge 1)\cdot\Big[\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-2\gamma
+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}(t,x-y)
+ \tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-2\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}(t,x'-y)\Big].
\end{align*}
Here the second inequality follows from \eqref{p3-1-1} and \eqref{p3-1-8a}, thanks to the fact that
$\beta_0< \alpha(x)\wedge \alpha(x')$, and the last inequality is due to Remark \ref{r3-3}(2) (which indicates that the convolution inequality \eqref{l3-3-0} holds for $\tilde \rho$) and the fact that $\gamma<\theta$.

(v) Suppose that the assumptions in part (2) of the Proposition hold, and that there are some $y_0\in \mathds R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(y_0)$ for all $z \in B(y_0,r_0)$. Then, using \eqref{l2-1-33} and repeating the arguments in part (ii) above,

nodes.name: Sum the bounds on $q_n$ in the $z$-independent case
nodes.statement:
Without loss of generality, throughout the proof we still assume that $\beta_0< \alpha_2/2$ and $\beta_0^{**}=\beta_0$.

We first suppose that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$.
As in the proof of Proposition \ref{p3-1}(1), we know that
$q(t,x,y)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}q_n(t,x,y)$
is absolutely convergent. In particular, \begin{equation} |q(t,x,y)|\leqslant |q_0(t,x,y)|+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}|q_n(t,x,y)|.
\end{equation}
According to \eqref{p3-1-6a}, we have
\begin{align*}
 \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}|q_n(t,x,y)|
& \leqslant
 \left(\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{\big[C \Gamma(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big]^{n+1}}{\Gamma\big((n+1)(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)}
 \right)\Big(\rho_{3(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-2\gamma}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y) \preceq \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y),
\end{align*}
where in the last inequality we choose $\gamma>0$ small enough such that
$\gamma<{\beta_0}/({2\alpha_2})$.
Combining this estimate with \eqref{p2-1-1} and  \eqref{p3-1-9},  we obtain \eqref{p3-1-2e} immediately.

nodes.statement: Without loss of generality, throughout this proof we will assume that $2\beta_0<\alpha_2$ and $\beta_0^{**}=\beta_0$; otherwise, we will replace $\beta_0$ by $\beta_0^{**}\in (0,\beta_0]\cap (0,{\alpha_2}/{2}).$ For simplicity, we only verify the case that $c_0=1$.
