nodes.name: $z$-independent $\kappa$: bound the Levi integral
nodes.statement:
(i) We first consider the case that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$.
Note that $$p^z(t,x-z)\preceq \rho_1^{z,0}(t,x-z),\quad t\in (0,1],x,z\in \mathds R^d.$$ This, along with
\eqref{p3-1-1} and \eqref{l3-3-1}, yields that for every $(t,x,y)\in
(0,1]\times \mathds R^d \times \mathds R^d$ and {any constant
$0<\gamma<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2},$}
\begin{equation*}
\int_0^t \int_{\mathds R^d} p^z(t-s,x-
z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\,ds\preceq
\big(\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{1-\gamma}+
\rho^{y,0}_{1+({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}\big)\big(t,x-y\big).
\end{equation*}
Therefore, $p(t,x,y)$ is well defined by \eqref{eq2-1}, and
\begin{equation} p(t,x,y)\preceq \Big(\rho^{y,0}_1+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{1-\gamma}+
\rho^{y,0}_{1+({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}\Big)\big(t,x-y\big)\preceq
\big(\rho^{y,0}_1+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{1-\gamma}\big)\big(t,x-y\big).
\end{equation}

When $|x-y|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha_2}}$,
$$\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{1-\gamma}\big(t,x-y\big)\preceq t^{-\gamma}|x-y|^{\beta_0}\rho^{y,0}_1\big(t,x-y\big)
\preceq t^{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}\rho^{y,0}_1\big(t,x-y\big).$$
Hence, due to $\gamma<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$, we get
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
p(t,x,y)\preceq \rho^{y,0}_1\big(t,x-y\big)\preceq t^{-{d/\alpha(y)}}\preceq
t^{-{d}/{\overline{\alpha}(y;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})}}\preceq t^{-{d/\alpha(x)}},
\end{split}
\end{equation}
where the third inequality follows from \eqref{l3-2-8}.

Next, we will verify the other two cases in the upper bound \eqref{p3-2-1}. Observe that
for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ such that
$|x-y|\leqslant 1$ and $|z|\leqslant 1$,
\begin{align*}
 \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(y)}}
&=
\frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}t^{({1/\alpha(y)})-({1/\alpha(x)})}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(y)}}
 \preceq \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}t^{{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1^2}}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(y)}}\\
&\preceq \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}t^{{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1^2}}+|z|t^{{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1^2}})^{d+\alpha(y)}}\\
&=t^{-{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|(d+\alpha(y))}/{\alpha_1^2}}\cdot\frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}+|z|)^{\alpha(y)-\alpha(x)}}\cdot
\frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(x)}}\\
&\preceq t^{-{(d+\alpha_2)|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1^2}}\cdot
t^{-{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1}}\cdot
\frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(x)}} \preceq
\frac{t^{-C_1R_0^{\beta_0}}}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(x)}},
\end{align*}
where the second inequality we used
$t^{{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1^2}}\leqslant 1$, and the third inequality follows from the fact that for all $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ with $|z|\leqslant 1$,
\begin{align*}
\frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}+|z|)^{\alpha(y)-\alpha(x)}}\preceq t^{-{|\alpha(y)-\alpha(x)|}/{\alpha(x)}}.
\end{align*}
Thus, choosing $R_0:=R_0(\alpha,\gamma)$ small enough  such that
$C_1R_0^{\beta_0}<\gamma$ and using the definition of $\rho^{x,0}_0$, we can
get that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ with
$|x-y|\leqslant R_0$ and $|z|\leqslant 1$,
\begin{equation} \rho^{y,0}_0(t,z)\preceq t^{-\gamma}\rho^{x,0}_0(t,z).
\end{equation}
By the definition of \eqref{e3-0}, we know immediately that \eqref{l4-1-5} still holds for
every $|x-y|\leqslant R_0$ and $|z|> 1$. This is, \eqref{l4-1-5} holds for all $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_0$.

Hence, combining \eqref{p3-2-3}, \eqref{p3-2-3a} with \eqref{l4-1-5} and changing the constant $\gamma$ properly, we find that
\begin{align*}
p(t,x,y)&\preceq
 \big(\rho^{y,0}_{1}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{1-\gamma}
\big)\big(t,x-y\big)\preceq \begin{cases}t^{-{d/\alpha(x)}}, & |y-x|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(x)}},\\
\frac{t^{1-\gamma}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}},& t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}\leqslant |y-x|\leqslant R_0,\\
\frac{t^{1-\gamma}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}},&|y-x|> R_0.
\end{cases}
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: $z$-independent $\kappa$: bound the Levi integral

nodes.name: Locally constant index: sharper bound
nodes.statement:
(ii) If there are some $x_0 \in \mathds R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such
that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(x_0)$ for all $z \in B(x_0,r_0)$, then for
every $y \in B(x_0,{r_0}/{2})$ and $z \in
B(y,{r_0}/{2})$,
$
\alpha(z)=\alpha(y)=\alpha(x_0).
$
Hence, by \eqref{p3-1-2b}, we have
\begin{equation*}
|q(t,x,y)|\preceq
\Big(\rho^{y,0}_{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_0\Big)(t,x-y)\quad\textrm{ for all }
x\in \mathds R^d\textrm{ and }y \in B\big(x_0,{r_0}/{2}\big).
\end{equation*}
Based on the inequality above, the computation in part (i) is valid
with $\gamma=0$ for $x=x_0$ and $y \in B(x_0,{r_0}/{2})$, which
proves \eqref{p3-2-2} for the case that $y \in
B(x_0,{r_0}/{2})$. The upper bound for the case
$|y-x_0|>{r_0}/{2}$ is just the same as that of \eqref{p3-2-1}.
nodes.statement_short: Locally constant index: sharper bound

nodes.name: General $\kappa$ case
nodes.statement:
(iii) If $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and
${(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}-1<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$, then, according to
\eqref{p3-1-2}, we know that the computation in part (i) holds with
$\gamma$ replaced by $\tilde\gamma$. Thus, following the argument in part
(i), we can obtain \eqref{p3-2-1a}. Similarly as in (ii),
\eqref{p3-2-2a} could be verified by using \eqref{p3-1-2c}.
nodes.statement_short: General $\kappa$ case

nodes.name: WLOG reductions
nodes.statement: Throughout the proof, we assume that $\beta_0<\alpha_2/2$ and that $\beta_0=\beta_0^{**}.$ We only verify the case that $c_0=1$.
nodes.statement_short: WLOG reductions

nodes.name: $z$-independent $\kappa$
nodes.statement_short: $z$-independent $\kappa$

nodes.name: Assume $\kappa$ independent of $z$
nodes.statement: (1) We first suppose that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$.
nodes.statement_short: Assume $\kappa$ independent of $z$

nodes.name: Near-diagonal case from Proposition 4.1
nodes.statement:
{\bf Case (a): $|x-y|\leqslant t^{1/\alpha(x)}$.}


According to \eqref{p3-2-1}, we can easily see that \eqref{p3-3-1} holds.
nodes.statement_short: Near-diagonal case from Proposition 4.1

nodes.name: Case $|x-y|>2$
nodes.statement_short: Case $|x-y|>2$

nodes.name: Intermediate case
nodes.statement:
{\bf Case (c): $t^{{1}/ \alpha(x)}\leqslant |x-y|\leqslant 2$.}

We still define $J_1$ and $J_2$ by those in \eqref{p3-3-2}.
If $|z-y|\geqslant {|x-y|}/{2}$,
then, by  \eqref{p3-1-2e}, we have
\begin{align*}
|q(s,z,y)|&\preceq
\begin{cases}
s^{-d/\alpha(y)},& |z-y|\leqslant s^{1/\alpha(y)},\\
|z-y|^{-d-\alpha_2},& s^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}\leqslant|z-y|\leqslant 1,\\
 |z-y|^{-d-\alpha_1},& |z-y|>1
\end{cases}
\\
&\preceq
\begin{cases}
|x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)},& |z-y|\leqslant s^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}},\\
|x-y|^{-d-\alpha_2},& s^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}\leqslant|z-y|\leqslant 1,\\
|x-y|^{-d-\alpha_1},& |z-y|>1
\end{cases}
\\
&\preceq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha_2},
\end{align*}
where in the second inequality we have used that fact that if
$|z-y|\leqslant s^{1/\alpha(y)}$ and $|x-y|\preceq |z-y|$, then
$$s^{-d/\alpha(y)}\preceq |z-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)}\preceq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)},$$
the last inequality follows from the fact that $|x-y|^{-d-\alpha_1}\preceq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha_2}$, thanks to $|x-y|\leqslant 2$.
Hence,
\begin{align*}
J_1&\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_2}} \int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x-z)\,dz \preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_2}}.
\end{align*}
At the same time, if $|z-y|\leqslant {|x-y|}/{2}$, then
\begin{align*}
p^z(t-s,x-z)&\preceq \frac{t-s}{|x-z|^{d+\alpha(z)}}\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(z)}}\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_2}},
\end{align*}
where the last inequality follows from $|x-y|^{-d-\alpha(z)}\preceq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha_2}$ since $|x-y|\leqslant 2$.
Combining this estimate with \eqref{p3-1-1},  we arrive at
$$
J_2 \preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_2}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\left(
\rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}\right)(s,z-y)\,dz \preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_2}}\cdot s^{-1+(\beta_0/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}.
$$

Using all the estimates above and choosing $0<\gamma<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$, we get
\begin{align*}
 \left|\int_0^t \int_{\mathds R^d}p^z(t-s,x-z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\,ds\right|
&\preceq \int_0^t (J_1+J_2)\,ds\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_2}}\cdot \left(1+t^{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}\right)\!\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_2}}.
\end{align*}
This, along with \eqref{eq2-1} immediately yields \eqref{p3-3-1}.
nodes.statement_short: Intermediate case

nodes.name: General $\kappa$ case
nodes.statement:
(2) If $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and ${\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}>({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1$, then, applying \eqref{p3-1-2f} and following the same arguments as above, we can prove
\eqref{p3-1-1a}. The details are omitted here.
nodes.statement_short: General $\kappa$ case

nodes.name: Decompose $\mathcal L^y$ into a stable part and a remainder
nodes.statement:
We write  $ {\mathcal L}^y={\mathcal L}_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}^y+{\mathcal L}_{\widehat \kappa}^y$ with
\begin{align*}
{\mathcal L}_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}^y f(x)&=\frac{1}{2}\int_{\mathds R^d}\delta_{f}(x;z)\frac{\kappa_1}{2}\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\,dz,\quad f\in C_c^2(\mathds R^d),\\
{\mathcal L}_{\widehat \kappa}^y f(x)&=\frac{1}{2}\int_{\mathds R^d}\delta_{f}(x;z)\frac{\widehat \kappa(y,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\,dz,\quad f\in C_c^2(\mathds R^d),
\end{align*}
where $\kappa_1>0$ is the constant in \eqref{e1-2}, $\widehat \kappa(y,z):=\kappa(y,z)-\kappa_1/2$ and
$$\delta_f(x;z)=f(x+z)+f(x-z)-2f(x).$$ Then, we have
\begin{equation} p^y(t,x)=\int_{\mathds R^d}p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(t,x-z)p^y_{\widehat \kappa}(t,z)\,dz,\ \ x\in \mathds R^d, t\in (0,1],
\end{equation}
where $p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}$ and $p^y_{\widehat \kappa}$ denote the fundamental solutions (i.e.\ heat kernel) associated with
the operators ${\mathcal L}_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}^y$ and ${\mathcal L}_{\widehat \kappa}^y$, respectively.
nodes.section: 4.2 H\"{o}lder regularity and gradient estimates of $p(t,x,y)$
nodes.statement_short: Decompose $\mathcal L^y$ into a stable part and a remainder

nodes.name: Prove the estimate for the stable part and transfer it
nodes.statement:
We first show that \eqref{l4-4-1} holds for $p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}$. Indeed, for every $x,x'\in \mathds R^d$ such that $|x-x'|\leqslant 1$,
\begin{align*}
\big|\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(1,x)-\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(1,x')\big|&=
\left|\int_0^1 \frac{d}{d \theta}\left(\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}
\left(1,x+\theta(x'-x)\right)\right)\,d\theta\right|\\
&\leqslant |x-x'|\cdot\int_0^1 \left|\nabla^2 p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}
\left(1,x+\theta(x'-x)\right)\right|\,d\theta\\
&\preceq |x-x'|\cdot \int_0^1 \left(1+\left|x+\theta(x'-x)\right|\right)^{-d-\alpha(y)-2}\,d\theta\\
&\preceq |x-x'|\cdot \left(1+|x|\right)^{-d-\alpha(y)-2},
\end{align*}
where in the third inequality we have used \eqref{p1-1-1}, and the last inequality is due to
the fact that for all $\theta\in [0,1]$ and $x,x'\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|\leqslant 1$
\begin{equation*}
\left(1+\left|x+\theta(x'-x)\right|\right)^{-1}\preceq \left(1+|x|\right)^{-1}.
\end{equation*}
Also by \eqref{p1-1-1}, we have that for every
$x,x'\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|>1$,
\begin{align*}
\big|\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(1,x)-\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(1,x')\big|&
\leqslant \big|\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(1,x)\big|+
\big|\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(1,x')\big|\\
&\preceq (1+|x|)^{-d-\alpha(y)-1}+
(1+|x'|)^{-d-\alpha(y)-1}.
\end{align*}
Combining both estimates above yields that for all $x,x'\in \mathds R^d$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
\big|\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(1,x)-\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(1,x')\big|
\preceq &\left(|x-x'|\wedge 1\right)\left(
(1+|x|)^{-d-\alpha(y)}+
(1+|x'|)^{-d-\alpha(y)}\right).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Since the Markov process $(X_t^{y,{\kappa_1}/{2}})_{t\geqslant0}$ associated with
$ {\mathcal L}^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}$ is a constant time-change of standard rotationally invariant $\alpha(y)$-stable process, by
the scaling property, for all $t>0$ and $x \in \mathds R^d$,
$$
 p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(t,x)= t^{-d/\alpha(y)} p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(1,t^{-1/\alpha(y)}x).
$$
This along with \eqref{l4-4-3} yields that for all $x,x'\in \mathds R^d$ and $t\in (0,1]$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
\big|\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(t,x)-\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(t,x')\big|
\preceq &\left[\left(t^{-1/\alpha(y)}|x-x'|\right)\wedge 1\right]\left(
\rho_{1-(1/\alpha(y))}^{y,0}(t,x)+\rho_{1-(1/\alpha(y))}^{y,0}(t,x')\right).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Therefore,  for every $x,x'\in \mathds R^d$ and $t\in (0,1]$,
\begin{align*}
&\left|\nabla p^y(t,x)-\nabla p^y(t,x')\right|\\
&=\left|\int_{\mathds R^d}\big(\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(t,x-z)-\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(t,x'-z)\big)
\cdot p^y_{\widehat \kappa}(t,z)\,dz\right|\\
&\leqslant \int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(t,x-z)-\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(t,x'-z)\big|
\cdot p^y_{\widehat \kappa}(t,z)\,dz\\
&\preceq \left[\left(t^{-1/\alpha(y)}|x-x'|\right)\wedge 1\right]\cdot
\Bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{y,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(y))}(t,x-z)\rho^{y,0}_1(t,z)\,dz+\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{y,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(y))}(t,x'-z)\rho^{y,0}_1(t,z)\,dz\Bigg)\\
&\preceq  \left[\left(t^{-1/\alpha(y)}|x-x'|\right)\wedge 1\right]\cdot
\left(\rho^{y,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(y))}(t,x)
+\rho^{y,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(y))}(t,x')\right),
\end{align*}
where the equality above is due to \eqref{l4-4-2}, the second inequality follows from
\eqref{l4-4-4} and \eqref{p1-1-1-1-0}, and in the last inequality we have used
\eqref{l3-2-1-}. By now we have finished the proof.

nodes.name: Duhamel identity and bound for $p^x-p^y$
nodes.section: 4.2 H\"{o}lder regularity and gradient estimates of $p(t,x,y)$
nodes.statement_short: Duhamel identity and bound for $p^x-p^y$

nodes.name: Same for gradients
nodes.statement:
(ii) Following the  argument of  \eqref{l4-1-2}, we can verify that
for all $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y,z \in \mathds R^d$,
\begin{align*}
&\nabla p^x(t,z)-\nabla p^y(t,z)\\
&=\int_0^t \frac{d}{ds}\left(\int_{\mathds R^d}
\nabla p^x(s,w)p^y(t-s,z-w)\,dw\right)\,ds\\
&=\int_0^t\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\Big( {\mathcal L}^x p^x(s,w)\nabla p^y(t-s,z-w) -\nabla p^x(s,w)\, {\mathcal L}^y
p^y(t-s,z-w)\Big)\,dw\bigg)\,ds\\
&=\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big) p^x(s,w)\,\nabla p^y(t-s,z-w)\,dw\,ds\\
&\quad +\int_{{t}/{2}}^t\int_{\mathds R^d} \nabla p^x(s,w)\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)
p^y(t-s,z-w)\,dw\,ds\\
&=\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big) p^x(s,w)
\big(\nabla p^y(t-s,z-w)-\nabla p^y(t-s,z)\big)\,dw\bigg)\,ds\\
&\quad +\int_{{t}/{2}}^t\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d} \big(\nabla p^x(s,w)-\nabla p^x(s,z)\big)  \big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)
p^y(t-s,z-w)\,dw\bigg)\,ds\\
&=:I_1+I_2,
\end{align*} where in the first and the second equalities we used the integration by part formula
and  in the second equality we also used the fact that $\nabla  {\mathcal L}^x p^y(t,w)= {\mathcal L}^x \nabla p^y(t,w)$.

Observe that
$$
t^{-d/\alpha(y)}\leqslant t^{-d/\alpha(x)}t^{-\big|\frac{d}{\alpha(y)}-\frac{d}{\alpha(x)}\big|}\leqslant
t^{-d/\alpha(x)}t^{-\frac{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(z)|}{\alpha_1^2}}\leqslant t^{-d/\alpha(x)}t^{-C|x-z|^{\beta_0}}.
$$
Then, according to \eqref{l4-4-1} and the proof of \eqref{l4-1-6},
for any $\theta \in (0,1)$, $\gamma\in (0,1)$, there exists a
constant $R_1:=R_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma)\in(0,R_0)$ such that for all $0<t \leqslant 1$ and
 $x,y\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
&\left|\nabla p^y(t,z-w)-\nabla p^y(t,z)\right|\\
&\preceq \big(|w|^{\theta}\wedge 1\big)\cdot
\big[\rho^{x,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x))-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,z-w)+\rho^{x,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x))-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,z)\big].
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Choosing $\theta\in(0,1\wedge \alpha_1)$ and $0<\gamma<({\theta}/{\alpha_2})\wedge ((1-({\theta}/{\alpha_1}))/2)$, and using
\eqref{l4-1-4} and \eqref{l4-1-7}, we arrive at that for any $t\in(0,1]$ and $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$,
\begin{align*}
I_1&\preceq |x-y|^{\beta_0}\cdot\bigg(\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{x,\theta}_{-\gamma}(s,w)\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x))-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t-s,z-w)\,dw\,ds\\
&\qquad\qquad \qquad\quad +\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{x,\theta}_{-\gamma}(s,w)
\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x))-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t-s,z)\,dw\,ds\bigg)\\
&=:|x-y|^{\beta_0}\cdot \big(I_{11}+I_{12}\big).
\end{align*}
Noticing that, by Remark \ref{r3-3}(2),  \eqref{l3-2-1-} still holds for $\tilde \rho$, we have
\begin{align*}
I_{11}&\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_0(t,z)\int_0^{t/2}
\Big(s^{-\gamma}(t-s)^{-(1/\alpha(x))-\gamma-(\theta/\alpha_1)}+s^{-1+\theta/\alpha_2-\gamma}(t-s)^{1-(1/\alpha(x))-\gamma-(\theta/\alpha_1)}\Big)\,ds\\
&\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_0(t,z) \cdot t^{1-(1/\alpha(x))-2\gamma-(\theta/\alpha_1)}\preceq
 \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x))-2\gamma-(\theta/\alpha_1)}(t,z).
\end{align*}
On the other hand, following the argument of  \eqref{l4-1-8}, we can obtain that
\begin{align*}
I_{12}&\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x))-\gamma-(\theta/\alpha_1)}(t,z)\cdot\int_0^{t/2}
\int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{x,\theta}_{-\gamma}(s,w)\,dw\,ds\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x))-2\gamma-(\theta/\alpha_1)}(t,z).
\end{align*}

By the same argument as that for $I_1$, we can also obtain that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and
$x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$,
\begin{equation*}
I_2\preceq |x-y|^{\beta_0}\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x))-2\gamma-(\theta/\alpha_1)}(t,z).
\end{equation*}
Combining all estimates together, we have shown
\eqref{l4-1-1-1}.

nodes.name: $z$-independent $\kappa$: estimate increments of both Levi terms
nodes.statement:
(1) We first suppose that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$. According
to  \eqref{p1-1-3}, for any $\gamma>0$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
&\big|p^z(t-s,x-z)-p^z(t-s,x'-z)\big|\\
&\preceq \big[\big((t-s)^{-{1}/{\alpha(z)}}|x-x'|\big)\wedge 1\big]\cdot
\big[\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x-z)+\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x'-z)\big]\\
&\preceq
\big[\big((t-s)^{-{1}/{\alpha(z)}}|x-x'|\big)^{(\alpha(x)-\gamma)_+\wedge
1}\wedge 1\big]
\big[\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x-z)+\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x'-z)\big]\\
&\preceq |x-x'|^{(\alpha(x)-\gamma)_+\wedge
1}(t-s)^{-{(\alpha(x)-\gamma)_+}/{\alpha(z)}}
\times\big[\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x-z)+\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x'-z)\big].
\end{split}
\end{equation}

On the one hand, observing that
$$\frac{\alpha(x)-\gamma}{\alpha(z)}\leqslant 1+\frac{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(z)|}{\alpha_1}-\frac{\gamma}{\alpha_2}\leqslant
1+\frac{C|x-z|^{\beta_0}}{\alpha_1}-\frac{\gamma}{\alpha_2},$$ we can find a constant
$R_2:=R_2(\alpha,\gamma)>0$ such that for every $x,x',z\in \mathds R^d$ satisfying
$|x-x'|\leqslant R_2$ and $|x-z|\leqslant 2R_2$ (which imply that $|x'-z|\leqslant
3R_2$), it holds
\begin{equation*}
\frac{\alpha(x)-\gamma}{\alpha(z)}\leqslant 1-\frac{2\gamma}{3\alpha_2},
\end{equation*}
which in turn yields that for every $0<s\leqslant t\leqslant 1$ and $x,x',z\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|\leqslant
R_2$ and $|x-z|\leqslant 2R_2$
\begin{align*}
\big|p^z(t-s,x-z)-p^z(t-s,x'-z)\big|
&\preceq
|x-x'|^{(\alpha(x)-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}\left(\rho^{z,0}_{{2\gamma}/({3\alpha_2})}(t-s,x-z)+\rho^{z,0}_{{2\gamma}/({3\alpha_2})}(t-s,x'-z)\right).
\end{align*}

On the other hand, when $|x-x'|\leqslant R_2$ and $|z-x|>2R_2$ (which
imply that $|z-x'|>R_2$), we obtain from \eqref{p1-1-1} and the mean
value theorem that
\begin{align*}
|p^z(t-s,x-z)-p^z(t-s,x'-z)|
&\leqslant |x-x'|\cdot|\nabla p^z(t-s,x-z+\tilde \theta_{x,x',z}(x'-x))|\\
&\preceq |x-x'|\cdot \frac{t-s}{((t-s)^{{1}/{\alpha(z)}}+|x-z|)^{d+\alpha(z)+1}}\\
&\preceq |x-x'|\cdot \frac{t-s}{|x-z|^{d+\alpha_1}}\preceq |x-x'|\cdot \rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x-z).
\end{align*}
where in the first inequality $|\tilde \theta_{x,x'z}|\leqslant 1$ is a
constant (which may depend on $x$, $x'$ and $z$), in the second inequality
we have used the fact that
$$|x-z+\tilde \theta_{x,x',z}(x'-x)|\geqslant |x-z|-|x'-x|\geqslant {|x-z|}/{2},$$
and the fourth inequality follows from
$|z-x|>R_2>C(t-s)^{{1}/{\alpha(z)}}$.

As a result, we obtain that for all $x,x',z\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|\leqslant R_2$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
\big|p^z(t,x-z)-p^z(t,x'-z)\big|
&\preceq
|x-x'|^{(\alpha(x)-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}\Big(\rho^{z,0}_{{2\gamma}/({3\alpha_2})}(t,x-z)
+\rho^{z,0}_{{2\gamma}/({3\alpha_2})}(t,x'-z)\Big).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Then, using \eqref{p3-1-1} and \eqref{l3-3-1} and changing the constant $\gamma$ properly, we arrive at for every
$|x-x'|\leqslant R_2$,
\begin{align*}
&\int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d}|p^z(t-s,x-z)-p^z(t-s,x'-z)||q(s,z,y)|\,dz\,ds\\
&\preceq |x-x'|^{(\alpha(x)-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}\!\cdot\Big[\Big(\rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})\!+({\gamma}/({2\alpha_2}))}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{{\gamma/(2\alpha_2)}}\Big)(t,x-y)\!+
\Big(\rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})\!+({\gamma}/({2\alpha_2}))}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{{\gamma/(2\alpha_2)}}\Big)(t,x'-y)\Big].
\end{align*}

Combining all the estimates together with \eqref{eq2-1} and using again \eqref{pppxy}, we can prove \eqref{t4-2-1} immediately.
nodes.section: 4.2 H\"{o}lder regularity and gradient estimates of $p(t,x,y)$
nodes.statement_short: $z$-independent $\kappa$: estimate increments of both Levi terms

nodes.name: General $\kappa$ case
nodes.statement:
(2) Now we assume that $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and ${(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}-1<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$.
Replacing $\alpha(x)$ by $\alpha(z)$ in \eqref{t4-2-1a}, we find that for every
$x,x'\in \mathds R^d$,
\begin{align*}
&\big|p^z(t-s,x-z)-p^z(t-s,x'-z)\big|\\
&\preceq (|x-x'|^{(\alpha_1-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}\wedge 1)(t-s)^{-{(\alpha(z)-\gamma)_+}/{\alpha(z)}} \big(\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x-z)+\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x'-z)\big)\\
&\preceq (|x-x'|^{(\alpha_1-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}\wedge 1)
\big[\rho^{z,0}_{{\gamma}/{\alpha_2}}(t-s,x-z)+\rho^{z,0}_{{\gamma}/{\alpha_2}}(t-s,x'-z)\big].
\end{align*}
Combining this with \eqref{eq2-1}, \eqref{p3-1-2} and \eqref{l3-3-1}, and following the
same arguments above,  we arrive at for all $x,x'\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|\leqslant R_2$,
\begin{align*}
 \big|p(t,x,y)-p(t,x',y)\big|
&\preceq |x-x'|^{(\alpha_1-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}\\
&\quad\times
\Big[\big(\rho^{y,0}_{{\gamma}/{\alpha_2}}(t,x-y)+
\rho^{y,0}_{{\gamma}/{\alpha_2}}(t,x'-y)\big)\\
&\qquad\,\,+\int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d}
\big(\rho^{z,0}_{{\gamma}/{\alpha_2}}(t-s,x-z)+\rho^{z,0}_{{\gamma}/{\alpha_2}}(t-s,x'-z)\big)\\
&\qquad \qquad  \times \big(\rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-[{(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}-1+{\gamma}/({2\alpha_2})]}+
\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-[{(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}-1+{\gamma}/({2\alpha_2})]}\Big)(s,z-y)\,dz\, ds \Big]\\
&\preceq |x-x'|^{(\alpha_1-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}
\big[\big(\rho^{y,0}_{\beta_0/\alpha_2+\gamma_1}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\gamma_1}\big)(t,x-y)+
\big(\rho^{y,0}_{\beta_0/\alpha_2+\gamma_1}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\gamma_1}\big)(t,x'-y)\big],
\end{align*}
where $\gamma_1:=1-\alpha_2/\alpha_1+\gamma/(2\alpha_2)$. By now we have verified \eqref{t4-2-1aa}. The proof is complete.
nodes.section: 4.2 H\"{o}lder regularity and gradient estimates of $p(t,x,y)$
nodes.statement_short: General $\kappa$ case

nodes.name: $z$-independent $\kappa$: differentiate under the integral and bound the gradient
nodes.statement:
(1) We first suppose that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$. For simplicity, we assume
that $\beta_0< \alpha(x_0)$, and so $\beta_0^*=\beta_0$ and
$\tilde \beta_0(x_0)={\alpha_1\beta_0}/{\alpha(x_0)}$. We will show that we can take the gradient with respect to variable $x$ in the equation \eqref{eq2-1}.
Note that
\begin{align*}
&\int_0^t \left|\int_{\mathds R^d}\nabla p^z(t-s,x_0-z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\right|\,ds\\
&=\int_0^{t/2}\left|\int_{\mathds R^d}\nabla p^z(t-s,x_0-z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\right|\,ds\\
&\quad+\int_{t/2}^t\left|\int_{\mathds R^d}\nabla p^z(t-s,x_0-z)\left(q(s,z,y)-q(s,x_0,y)\right)\,dz\right|\,ds\\
&\quad+\int_{t/2}^t\left|\int_{\mathds R^d}\left(\nabla p^z(t-s,x_0-z)-\nabla p^{x_0}(t-s,x_0-z)\right)
q(s,x_0,y)\,dz\right|\,ds\\
&=:\int_0^{t/2}\left|\int_{\mathds R^d}J_1(s,z)\,dz\right|\,ds+\int_{t/2}^t
\left|\int_{\mathds R^d}J_2(s,z)\,dz\right|\,ds+\int_{t/2}^t
\left|\int_{\mathds R^d}J_3(s,z)\,dz\right|\,ds.
\end{align*}



According to \eqref{p1-1-1},
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
|\nabla p^z(t,x-z)|&\preceq \frac{t}{(t^{{1}/{\alpha(z)}}+|x-z|)^{d+\alpha(z)+1}}.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Observing that
\begin{equation*}
\Big|\frac{1}{\alpha(z)}-\frac{1}{\alpha(x)}\Big|\leqslant
\frac{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(z)|}{\alpha_1^2}\leqslant C|x-z|^{\beta_0},
\end{equation*}
we find by \eqref{t5-1-3} that for every (small enough) $\gamma>0$, there is a constant $R_1:=R_1(\alpha, \kappa,\gamma)>0$ such that
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
|\nabla p^z(t,x-z)|&\preceq
\begin{cases}
\rho^{z,0}_{1-({1}/{\alpha(z)})}(t,x-z),\ &|x-z|\leqslant R_1,\\
\frac{t}{|x-z|^{d+\alpha_1+1}}
,\ & |x-z|>R_1
\end{cases}\\
&\preceq \rho^{z,0}_{1-({1/\alpha(x)})-\gamma}(t,x-z). \end{split}
\end{equation}

Thus, choosing $\gamma>0$ small enough such that $\gamma<\beta_0/\alpha_2$, and using \eqref{l3-2-0}, \eqref{p3-1-1} and
\eqref{t5-1-4}, we can find that
\begin{align*}
&\int_0^{t/2}\int_{\mathds R^d}|J_1(s,z)|\,dz\,ds\\
&\preceq
\int_0^{t/2}\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{z,0}_{1-({1/\alpha(x_0)})-\gamma}(t-s,x_0-z)
\big(
\rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}(s,z-y)+
\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}(s,z-y)\big)\,dz\,ds\\
&\preceq \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x_0-y)\!\bigg(\!\int_0^{t/2}\!(t\!-\!s)^{-(1/\alpha(x_0))-\gamma}s^{(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-\gamma}\! +\!
(t\!-\!s)^{1-(1/\alpha(x_0))-\gamma}s^{-1+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-\gamma}\,ds \bigg)\\
&\preceq \rho^{y,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x_0))-2\gamma}(t,x-y).
\end{align*}

On the other hand, according to \eqref{p3-1-1a}, \eqref{t5-1-4} and the fact that $\beta_0<\alpha(x_0)$, we arrive at
\begin{align*}
 \int_{t/2}^t\int_{\mathds R^d}|J_2(s,z)|\,dz\,ds
&\preceq \int_{t/2}^t\int_{\mathds R^d}
\bigg(\rho^{z,\widehat \beta_0}_{1-({1/\alpha(x_0)})-\gamma}(t-s,x_0-z)\tilde\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-{(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}}
(s,z-y)
\\
&\qquad\qquad
+\rho^{z,\widehat \beta_0}_{1-({1/\alpha(x_0)})-\gamma}(t-s,x_0-z)\tilde\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-{(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}}(s,x_0-y)\bigg)\,dz\,ds\\
&=:\int_{t/2}^t \int_{\mathds R^d}(J_{21}(s,z)+J_{22}(s,z))\,dz\,ds,
\end{align*}
where $\widehat \beta_0=\widehat \beta_0(\theta):={\alpha_1(\beta_0-\alpha_2\theta)}/{\alpha(x_0)}$.

Since $\tilde \beta_0(x_0)>1-\alpha(x_0)$, we can choose
$\theta, \gamma>0$ small enough such that $1+(\widehat \beta_0/\alpha(x_0))-(1/\alpha(x_0))-\gamma>0$, which along with
\eqref{l3-2-0} yields
\begin{align*}
\int_{t/2}^t \int_{\mathds R^d}J_{21}(s,z)\,dz\,ds
&\preceq \tilde \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x_0-y)\cdot\Big(
\int_{t/2}^t (t-s)^{1-(1/\alpha(x_0))-\gamma}s^{-1+\theta-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}\\
&\quad \quad +(t-s)^{(\widehat \beta_0/\alpha(x_0))-
(1/\alpha(x_0))-\gamma}s^{\theta-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}\,ds\Big)\\
&\preceq\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x_0))+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)-2\gamma}(t,x_0-y).
\end{align*}
On the other hand, noting that for $t/2<s\leqslant t$, it holds that
\begin{equation} \tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-{(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}}(s,x_0-y)\preceq
\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-{(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}}(t,x_0-y).
\end{equation}
Since $\tilde \beta_0>1-\alpha(x_0)$, by \eqref{l3-1-1} we have
\begin{align*}
 \int_{t/2}^t \int_{\mathds R^d}J_{22}(s,z)\,dz\,ds
&\preceq
\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}(t,x_0-y)
\int_{t/2}^t\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{z,\widehat \beta_0}_{1-({1/\alpha(x_0)})-\gamma}(t-s,x_0-z)\,dz\,ds\\
&\preceq \tilde \rho^{y,0}_{1+(\widehat \beta_0/\alpha(x_0))-(1/\alpha(x_0))+
(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)-2\gamma}(t,x_0-y).
\end{align*}



According to \eqref{l4-1-1-1} for the case that $|x_0-z|\leqslant R_1$ and \eqref{t5-1-4} for the case
that $|x_0-z|>R_1$), we arrive at that (by changing the constant $\gamma$ properly) for any $t>0$ and $x_0,z\in \mathds R^d$,
\begin{align*}
\left|\nabla p^{x_0}(t,x_0-z)-\nabla p^z(t,x_0-z)\right|\preceq
\tilde \rho^{z,\beta_0}_{1-1/\alpha(x_0)-\gamma}(t,x_0-z).
\end{align*}
This, along with \eqref{p3-1-1} yields
\begin{align*}
\int_{t/2}^t\int_{\mathds R^d}|J_3(s,z)|\,dz\,ds
&\preceq \tilde \rho^{y,0}_{-\gamma}(t,x_0-y)\int_{t/2}^t\int_{\mathds R^d} \rho^{z,\beta_0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x_0))-\gamma}(t-s,x_0-z)\,dz\,ds\\
&\preceq \tilde \rho^{y,0}_{1+(\beta_0/\alpha(x_0))-1/\alpha(x_0)-2\gamma}(t,x_0-y),
\end{align*} where in the last inequality we used the fact that $\beta_0\geqslant\tilde \beta_0(x_0)>1-\alpha(x_0)$.

Combining all estimates together, we obtain that
\begin{equation*}
\int_0^t \left|\int_{\mathds R^d}\nabla p^z(t-s,x_0-z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\right|\,ds
\preceq  \tilde \rho^{y,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x_0))+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)-2\gamma}(t,x_0-y).
\end{equation*}
According to the estimate above and the dominated convergence theorem,  we know that
$\nabla p(t,\cdot)(x_0)$ exists, and \eqref{t5-1-1} holds by changing $\theta$ and $\gamma$ properly.
nodes.section: 4.2 H\"{o}lder regularity and gradient estimates of $p(t,x,y)$
nodes.statement_short: $z$-independent $\kappa$: differentiate under the integral and bound the gradient

nodes.name: General $\kappa$ case
nodes.statement:
(2) Suppose that $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and
${(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}-1<{\beta_0^{**}}/{\alpha_2}$. If for some $x_0\in \mathds R^d$,
$\tilde \beta_0(x_0)-({\alpha_1\alpha_2}/{\alpha(x_0)})
\big(({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1\big)>1-\alpha_1$, then, by \eqref{l4-1-1-1} and
\eqref{t5-1-3},
$$
|\nabla p^z(t,x-z)|\preceq t^{-{1}/{\alpha(z)}}\rho^{z,0}_1(t,x-z)\preceq
\rho^{z,0}_{1-(1/\alpha_1)}(t,x-z)
$$
and $$
|\nabla p^x(t,x-z)-\nabla p^z(t,x-z)|\preceq
\tilde \rho^{z,\beta_0}_{1-(1/\alpha_1)-\gamma}(t,x-z).
$$
In the following, we choose $\theta,\gamma$ small enough such that
$$\widehat \beta_0:={\alpha_1}\big(\beta_0-\alpha_2\theta\big)/{\alpha(x_0)}>-1+(1/\alpha_1)+\gamma.$$
Using estimates and following the same argument in part (1), we can obtain that
for every fixed $t \in (0,1]$ and $y \in \mathds R^d$, $p(t,\cdot,y)$ is differentiable at $x_0\in \mathds R^d$ and
\eqref{t5-1-2} holds.
nodes.section: 4.2 H\"{o}lder regularity and gradient estimates of $p(t,x,y)$
nodes.statement_short: General $\kappa$ case

nodes.name: Reduce to continuity in the space variables
nodes.statement:
We only consider the case that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$, and the other case can be verified similarly.

According to \eqref{eq2-1}, \eqref{p3-1-1} and \eqref{p3-2-1}, we know
immediately the continuity of $p$ with respect to time variable.
It remains to show the continuity of $p$ with respect to space variables.
nodes.section: 4.2 H\"{o}lder regularity and gradient estimates of $p(t,x,y)$
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to continuity in the space variables

nodes.name: Continuity in space via estimates on $p^{y+\varepsilon z}-p^y$ and dominated convergence
nodes.statement:
For $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ and any $\varepsilon>0$
\begin{align*}
|p^{y+\varepsilon z}(t,x-y-\varepsilon)-
p^{y}(t,x-y)|
&\leqslant  |p^{y+\varepsilon z}(t,x-y-\varepsilon)-
p^{y+\varepsilon z}(t,x-y)|+
|p^{y+\varepsilon z}(t,x-y)-p^{y}(t,x-y)|.
\end{align*}
According to \eqref{p1-1-3} and \eqref{l4-1-1}, we can show that
$(x,y)\mapsto p^y(t,x-y)$ is continuous. On the other hand,  \eqref{p1-1-4}, \eqref{p3-1-1a-1} and \eqref{l4-1-1a} imply that
$(x,y)\mapsto q_0(t,x,y)$ is continuous. By the iteration estimates in Proposition \ref{p3-1} and the
dominated convergence theorem, we also can verify that $(x,y)\mapsto q(t,x,y)$ is continuous.
Due to the expression \eqref{eq2-1} and again the dominated convergence theorem,  we know that
$(x,y)\mapsto p(t,x,y)$ is continuous. The proof is finished.
nodes.section: 4.2 H\"{o}lder regularity and gradient estimates of $p(t,x,y)$
nodes.statement_short: Continuity in space via estimates on $p^{y+\varepsilon z}-p^y$ and dominated convergence

nodes.name: Split the integral into near and far parts $J_1$, $J_2$
nodes.statement:
Throughout the proof, we will assume that $\beta_0<\alpha_2$ and $\beta_0^*=\beta_0$ for simplicity.
Noting that $\int_{\mathds R^d}p^x(t,x-y)\,dy=1$ for all $x\in \mathds R^d$ and $t\in (0,1]$, we have
\begin{align*}
\bigg|\int_{\mathds R^d}p^y(t,x-y)\,dy-1\bigg|&=\bigg|
\int_{\mathds R^d}p^y(t,x-y)\,dy-\int_{\mathds R^d}p^x(t,x-y)\,dy\bigg|\\
&\leqslant \int_{\mathds R^d}|p^x(t,x-y)-p^y(t,x-y)|\,dy\\
&\leqslant \int_{\{|x-y|\leqslant R_1\}}|p^x(t,x-y)-p^y(t,x-y)|\,dy\\
&\quad +\int_{\{|x-y|>R_1\}}|p^x(t,x-y)-p^y(t,x-y)|\,dy\\
&=:J_1+J_2,
\end{align*}
where $R_1$ is the constant in Lemma \ref{l4-1}.
nodes.statement_short: Split the integral into near and far parts $J_1$, $J_2$

nodes.name: Bound $J_1$ by Lemma 4.5
nodes.statement_short: Bound $J_1$ by Lemma 4.5

nodes.name: Bound $J_2$ and combine
nodes.statement_short: Bound $J_2$ and combine

nodes.name: Choose parameters to get the limit
nodes.statement: Choosing $\gamma,\theta>0$ small enough such that $2\gamma+({\theta}/{\alpha_1})<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$, we immediately get \eqref{p4-1-1}.
nodes.statement_short: Choose parameters to get the limit

nodes.name: Decompose $\delta_{p^x}-\delta_{p^y}$ into $J_1+J_2$
nodes.statement:
By using \eqref{l4-1-2}, we can verify that
\begin{align*}
& \delta_{p^x}(t,x-y;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)\\
&=\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)p^x(s,w)
\big(\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y-w;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y;z)\big)\,dw\bigg)\,ds\\
&\quad+\int_{{t}/{2}}^t\!\!\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)p^y(t-s,x-y-w)
\big(\delta_{p^x}(s,w;z)-\delta_{p^x}(s,x-y;z)\big)\,dw\bigg)\,ds.
\end{align*}
Therefore,
\begin{align*}
& \int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\delta_{p^x}(t,x-y;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)\big|\cdot\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\
& \leqslant \int_0^{{t}/{2}}\bigg[\int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)p^x(s,w)\big|
\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y-w;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y;z)\big|\cdot \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\bigg)\,dw\bigg]\,ds\\
&+\int_{{t}/{2}}^t\bigg[\int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)p^y(t-s,x-y-w)\big|
\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\delta_{p^x}(s,w;z)-\delta_{p^x}(s,x-y;z)\big|\cdot \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\bigg)\,dw\bigg]\,ds\\
&=:J_1+J_2.
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Decompose $\delta_{p^x}-\delta_{p^y}$ into $J_1+J_2$

nodes.name: Increment bounds for $\delta_{p^y}$ and jump integrals
nodes.statement:
According to \eqref{p1-1-4} and \eqref{l4-1-5}, for every $\theta \in (0,1)$ and $\gamma>0$, there exists a constant
$R_1:=R_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma)>0$ such that for every $0<s<t<1$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
&\big|\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y-w;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y;z)\big|\\
&\preceq \big[\left((t-s)^{-{1/\alpha(y)}}|w|\right)^{\theta}\wedge 1\big]\cdot
\left[\left((t-s)^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\right)\wedge 1\right]
\\
&\quad\times\big[
\rho_1^{y,0}(t-s,x-y)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t-s,x-y-w)
+\rho_1^{y,0}(t-s,x-y\pm z)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t-s,x-y-w\pm z)\big]\\
&\preceq \left(|w|^{\theta}\wedge 1\right)\cdot
\left[\left((t-s)^{-{2}/{\alpha(x)}}|z|^2\right)\wedge 1\right]
 \cdot\big[
\rho_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}^{x,0}(t-s,x-y)+\rho_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}^{x,0}(t-s,x-y-w)\\
&\qquad\qquad\qquad\quad
+\rho_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}^{x,0}(t-s,x-y\pm z)+\rho_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}^{x,0}(t-s,x-y-w\pm z)\big].
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Furthermore, following the argument of Lemma \ref{l1-1}, we can derive that for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y \in \mathds R^d$
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
&\int_{\mathds R^d} \left[\left(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(x)}}|z|^2\right)\wedge 1\right]
\cdot \rho_{1}^{x,0}(t,y \pm z)\cdot |z|^{-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz
\preceq \rho^{x,0}_{0}(t,y),\\
&\int_{\mathds R^d} \left[\left(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(x)}}|z|^2\right)\wedge 1\right]
\cdot \rho_{1}^{x,0}(t,y)\cdot |z|^{-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz
\preceq \rho^{x,0}_{0}(t,y).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Increment bounds for $\delta_{p^y}$ and jump integrals

nodes.name: Bound $J_1$ by convolution inequalities
nodes.statement_short: Bound $J_1$ by convolution inequalities

nodes.name: Bound $J_2$ similarly
nodes.statement:
By estimates for
 the terms
$$\big|\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)p^y(t-s,x-y-w)\big|$$ and $$\big|
\delta_{p^x}(s,w;z)-\delta_{p^x}(s,x-y;z)\big|,$$ we can deal with the singularity
as $s$ near $t$ by the same arguments above and obtain that for all $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$,
\begin{equation*}
J_2 \preceq \tilde \rho^{x,\beta_0}_{-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y).
\end{equation*}

nodes.name: Bounds and continuity for $\partial_t\phi$
nodes.statement:
{(ii)} By the proof of \eqref{l4-2-3} (also see \cite[Theorem 2.4]{CZ}), it holds that
\begin{equation} | {\mathcal L}^zp^z(t-s,x-z)|\preceq \rho^{z,0}_0(t-s,x-z),
\end{equation} and so we can verify that for every $0<s<t<1$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$,
$$\int_{\mathds R^d}| {\mathcal L}^z p^z(t-s,x-z)||q(s,z,y)|\,dz<\infty.$$
Thus, by the dominated convergence theorem, for every $0<s<t$ and $x,y \in \mathds R^d$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
\partial_t \phi(t,s,x,y)&=\int_{\mathds R^d} {\mathcal L}^zp^z(t-s,x-z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\\
&=\int_{\mathds R^d} {\mathcal L}^zp^z(t-s,x-z)(q(s,z,y)-q(s,x,y))\,dz\\
&\quad +q(s,x,y)\int_{\mathds R^d}( {\mathcal L}^z- {\mathcal L}^x)p^z(t-s,x-z)\,dz\\
&\quad +q(s,x,y)\int_{\mathds R^d} {\mathcal L}^x p^z(t-s,x-z)\,dz\\
&=:\tilde J_1+ \tilde J_2+ \tilde J_3.
\end{split}
\end{equation}

Combining \eqref{t4-1-4} with \eqref{p3-1-1a} yields that for any $0<\gamma<\theta<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$,
\begin{align*}
|\tilde J_1| &\preceq \int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{z,\tilde \theta}_0(t-s,x-z)\cdot
\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma+({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-({\beta_0}/{\alpha_1})}(s,z-y)\,dz\\
&\quad +\int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{z,\tilde \theta}_0(t-s,x-z)\cdot
\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma+({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-({\beta_0}/{\alpha_1})}(s,x-y)\,dz\\
&=:\tilde J_{11}+ \tilde J_{12},
\end{align*}
where $\tilde \theta:=\alpha_1(\beta_0-\alpha_2\theta)/{\alpha_2}$.
According to \eqref{l3-2-1} (which holds for $\tilde \rho$), we obtain that
for every ${t}/{2}\leqslant s \leqslant t$,
\begin{align*}
\tilde J_{11}&\preceq \tilde \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y)\cdot\big[(t-s)^{-1+({\tilde \theta}/{\alpha_2})}s^{\theta-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-({\beta_0}/{\alpha_1})-1}\big]\preceq t^{-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha_1})-({d}/{\alpha_1})-2}(t-s)^{-1+({\tilde \theta}/{\alpha_2})},
\end{align*}
where in the last inequality we have used the fact that $\tilde\rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y)\preceq t^{-1-d/\alpha_1}$ and
$s^{-1}\preceq t^{-1}$ for ${t}/{2}\leqslant s \leqslant t$. Note that $\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha_1})}(s,x-y)\preceq t^{-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha_1})-({d}/{\alpha_1})-1}$ for
every ${t}/{2}\leqslant s \leqslant t$,
and \eqref{l3-1-1} holds for $\tilde \rho$, then we have
\begin{align*}
\tilde J_{12}& \preceq t^{-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha_1})-({d}/{\alpha_1})-1}\int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{z,\tilde \theta}_{0}(t-s,x-z)\,dz\preceq t^{-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha_1})-({d}/{\alpha_1})-1}(t-s)^{-1+({\tilde \theta}/{\alpha_2})}.
\end{align*}

By \eqref{l2-1-2} and \eqref{p3-1-1}, we arrive at that for any $0<\gamma<\theta<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$ and every
${t}/{2}\leqslant s \leqslant t$,
\begin{equation*}
|( {\mathcal L}^z- {\mathcal L}^x)p^z(t-s,x-z)|\preceq
|q_0(t-s,x, z)|\preceq \rho^{z,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}(t-s,x-z)
\end{equation*} and \begin{equation*}
|q(s,x,y)|\preceq \big(\rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}\big)(s,x-y)\preceq t^{-\gamma-({d}/{\alpha_1})-1}.
\end{equation*}
Hence, combining both estimates above with \eqref{l3-1-1},  we obtain
\begin{align*}
|\tilde J_{2}|&\preceq t^{-\gamma-({d}/{\alpha_1})-1}\int_{\mathds R^d} \rho^{z,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}(t-s,x-z)\,dz
 \preceq t^{-\gamma-({d}/{\alpha_1})-1}(t-s)^{-1+({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}.
\end{align*}
Furthermore, \eqref{p3-1-1} and \eqref{p4-2-1} yield that for every ${t}/{2}\leqslant s \leqslant t$ and
constants $\gamma,\theta \in (0,1)$ such that $\gamma<{\theta}/{\alpha_2}$ and
$2\gamma+({\theta}/{\alpha_1})<\beta_0/\alpha_2$,
\begin{equation*}
|\tilde J_3| \preceq t^{-\gamma-({d}/{\alpha_1})-1}(t-s)^{-1+({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}.
\end{equation*}


On the other hand, when $0<s\leqslant {t}/{2}$,  it follows from \eqref{t4-1-4}, \eqref{p3-1-1} and \eqref{l3-2-1} that
\begin{align*}
\big|\partial_t \phi(t,s,x,y)\big|
 &\preceq
\int_{\mathds R^d}\big| {\mathcal L}^z p^z(t-s,x-z)\big|\big|q(s,z,y)\big|\,dz\\
&\preceq \int_{\mathds R^d} \rho^{z,0}_0(t-s,x-z)\cdot
\big(\rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}\big)(s,z-y)\,dz\\
&\preceq \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y)\cdot\big[(t-s)^{-1}s^{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}+
(t-s)^{-1+({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})}s^{-\gamma}+s^{-1+({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}\big]\\
&\quad +\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{0}(t,x-y)\cdot(t-s)^{-1}s^{-\gamma}\\
&\preceq t^{-2-({d}/{\alpha_1})}s^{-1+({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma},
\end{align*}
where in the last inequality we have used the facts that $\rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y)\preceq t^{-1-({d}/{\alpha_1})}$ and $(t-s)^{-1}\preceq t^{-1}$ for every
$0<s\leqslant {t}/{2}$.
Therefore, choosing $\gamma,\theta \in (0,1)$ such that $\gamma<{\theta}/{\alpha_2}$ and
$2\gamma+({\theta}/{\alpha_1})<\beta_0/\alpha_2$, and combining all the estimates above,  we
know that \eqref{e:lkk} is well defined, and that for every $t \in (0,1)$,
$
\sup_{t_0 \in (t,t+\varepsilon_1)}|
\partial_t\phi(t_0,s,x,y)|\leqslant \eta(t,s),
$
where $\eta$ is a non-negative measurable function such that
$\int_0^t \eta(t,s)\,ds<\infty$ and $\varepsilon_1>0$ is a constant small enough (which may depend on $t$).
Now, according to the dominated convergence theorem, for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
\lim_{\varepsilon \downarrow 0}\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\cdot
\bigg(\int_0^t \big(\phi(t+\varepsilon,s,x,y)-\phi(t,s,x,y)\big)\,ds\bigg)=
\int_0^t \partial_t \phi(t,s,x,y)\,ds.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Bounds and continuity for $\partial_t\phi$

(i) We first assume that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$.
We will prove that $p(t,x,y)$ constructed by \eqref{eq2-1} satisfies all the assertions.

According to Proposition \ref{t4-1}, \eqref{t1-1-1} holds. By
Propositions \ref{p3-2} and \ref{p3-3}, \eqref{t1-1-4} and \eqref{t1-1-4a} hold true.
Propositions \ref{t4-2} and \ref{t5-1} imply
\eqref{t1-1-7} and \eqref{t1-1-7a}, respectively. By Proposition \ref{p4-5},  we know that
$p:(0,1]\times\mathds R^d\times \mathds R^d\rightarrow \mathds R_+$ is continuous. The lower bounds
\eqref{t1-1-4b}  will be shown in Corollary \ref{c-lower}, which is a consequence of Propositions

nodes.statement:
(ii) According to  the proof of Proposition \ref{t4-1}, we can
obtain that for every $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$, there exist a constant
$C(\varepsilon)>0$ and a measurable function $\eta:\mathds R^d \to  \mathds R_+$ such that
$\int_{\mathds R^d}\eta(y)\,dy<\infty$,

\begin{equation*}
\sup_{t \in (\varepsilon,1)}\Big|\frac{\partial p(t,x,y)}{\partial t}\Big|\leqslant C(\varepsilon)\eta(x-y)
\end{equation*} and
\begin{equation*}\begin{split}
&\sup_{t \in (\varepsilon,1),\sigma>0}\bigg|\int_{\{|z|>\sigma\}}\big(p(t,x+z,y)+p(t,x-z,y)-2p(t,x,y)\big)
\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\bigg|\leqslant C(\varepsilon)\eta(x-y).\end{split}
\end{equation*}
Thus, by the dominated convergence theorem, it is easy to verify
that ${\mathcal L} u_f (t, \cdot) (x)$ exists for each $t>0$ and $x\in \mathds R^d$, $t\mapsto {\mathcal L} u_f (t, \cdot) (x)$
is continuous,  and that \eqref{t1-1-2} holds.

(vi)
Suppose that $\widehat p(t,x,y)$ is another
jointly continuous function  on $(0, 1]\times \mathds R^d\times \mathds R^d$
that is bounded for each $t>0$ and
 satisfies  \eqref{t1-1-7} and \eqref{t1-1-2a}-\eqref{t1-1-3}.
For every $f \in C_{b,u}(\mathds R^d)$, let
$$\widehat u_f(t,x):=\int_{\mathds R^d}\widehat p(t,x,y)f(y)\,dy \quad \hbox{and} \quad
\widehat w_f(t,x):=u_f(t,x)-\widehat u_f(t,x).
$$
 Then both $u_f$ and $\widehat u_f$ satisfy \eqref{t1-1-2}. By the same argument above, we have
$\widehat w_f(t,x)=0$ for each $(t,x)\in (0,1]\times \mathds R^d$. This implies
that for every $f \in C_{b,u}(\mathds R^d)$,
\begin{equation*}
\int_{\mathds R^d} p(t,x,y)f(y)\,dy=\int_{\mathds R^d} \widehat p(t,x,y)f(y)\,dy.
\end{equation*}
Consequently, $p(t,x,y)=\widehat p(t,x,y)$ for a.e.\ $y \in \mathds R^d$ and hence for every $y\in \mathds R^d$.
nodes.statement_short: Uniqueness via maximum principle

(vii) Suppose that $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$.  The desired upper and lower estimates and the regularity can be proved in a similar way as before. On the other hand, the condition ${(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}-1<\beta_*/\alpha_2<{1}/{2}$ implies that
$\alpha_2-\alpha_1<{\alpha_1}/{2}<1$, which ensures that
\eqref{t4-3-2} holds with $u_f(t,x):=\int_{\mathds R^d}p(t,x,y)f(y)\,dy$ for every
$f \in C_{b,u}(\mathds R^d)$. Therefore, following the arguments in steps (i)-(vi), we can verify that \eqref{t1-1-5}-\eqref{t1-1-5b} hold in such case.

nodes.name: Isolate the role of the gradient estimate
nodes.statement:
In Theorem \ref{t1-1} we assume that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$.
According to its proof, the reason why we need such condition is only due to that this implies the
gradient estimate \eqref{p1-1-1}. Thus, for the upper bound estimates for $|\nabla p^y(t,x)|$
and  $|\nabla^2 p^y(t,x)|$, the time singularity factor $t^{-{1/\alpha(y)}}$ will not appear when $|x|$ is large and $t$ is small. This point is
crucial for estimates \eqref{l2-1-2} and \eqref{p3-1-1a-1}, which yield Theorem \ref{t1-1}.
nodes.statement_short: Isolate the role of the gradient estimate

nodes.name: Gradient estimates for radial kernels from the literature
nodes.statement:
Now, we turn to these two assumptions in Remark \ref{rrr-000}(1). According to \cite[Theorem 1.5]{KR} and  \cite[Corollary 7 and Theorem 21]{BGR}, the following gradient estimate \begin{equation*}
|\nabla^k p^y(t,x)|\preceq \frac{t}{|x|^{d+\alpha(y)+k}},\quad k=1,2
\end{equation*} holds for all $t \in (0,1]$ and $x\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x|$ is large,
which also ensures that
the required estimates \eqref{l2-1-2} and \eqref{p3-1-1a-1} hold true.
nodes.statement_short: Gradient estimates for radial kernels from the literature

nodes.name: Reduce to one case and compare $p$ with $p^y$
nodes.statement:
For simplicity, we only prove the case that $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and $({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1<\beta_0^{**}/{\alpha_2}$, since the other case can be
tackled similarly and easily.

First, according to \eqref{l3-2-8}, for any $t\in(0,1]$ and $x,y\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant 5
(t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}}\vee t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}})\leqslant 5t^{{1}/{\alpha_2}}$,
\begin{equation} t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}}\asymp t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}.
\end{equation}
It is well known that for any $t>0$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$, $$p^y(t,x-y)\asymp \frac{t}{(t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}+|x-y|)^{d+\alpha(y)}}.$$
Thus, for all $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in\mathds R^d$,
\begin{equation} p^y(t,x-y)\succeq t^{-{d}/{\alpha(y)}}
\quad\textrm{ when }|x-y|\leqslant 5(t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}}\vee t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}).
\end{equation}

Second, \eqref{p3-1-2} and \eqref{l3-3-1}  yield that for all $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant 5t^{{1}/{\alpha_2}}$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
&\int_0^t \int_{\mathds R^d}
p^z(t-s,x-z)|q(s,z,y)|\,dz\,ds\\
&\preceq\int_0^t \int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x-z)
\cdot\Big(\rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0^{**}}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma_2 }+\rho^{y,\beta_0^{**}}_{-\gamma_2 }\Big)(s,z,y)\,dz\,ds\\
&\preceq \rho^{y,\beta_0^{**}}_{1-\gamma_2 }(t,x-y)+\rho^{y,0}_{1+({\beta_0^{**}}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma_2 }(t,x-y)\\
& \preceq
|x-y|^{\beta_0^{**}}t^{-{d}/{\alpha(y)}-\gamma_2 }+t^{-({d}/{\alpha(y)})+({\beta_0^{**}}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma_2 }\preceq t^{-({d}/{\alpha(y)})+({\beta_0^{**}}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma_2 },
\end{split}
\end{equation}
where in the first inequality $\gamma_2: =({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1+\gamma$ and the fourth inequality
follows from the fact that $|x-y|\leqslant 5t^{{1}/{\alpha_2}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to one case and compare $p$ with $p^y$

nodes.name: Choose $\gamma$ and conclude for small $t$
nodes.statement:
The assumption $({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1<{\beta_0^{**}}/{\alpha_2}$ ensures that we can choose
$\gamma>0$ small enough such that $\gamma_2 <{\beta_0^{**}}/{\alpha_2}$. Combining \eqref{p4-3-4}
with \eqref{p4-3-3}, \eqref{eq2-1} and \eqref{p4-3-2}, we arrive at that there is a constant $t_0\in(0,1]$ such that for all $t\in (0,t_0]$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant 5(t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}}\vee t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}})$,
\begin{equation} p(t,x,y)\succeq t^{-{d}/{\alpha(y)}}\asymp t^{-{d}/{\alpha(x)}}.
\end{equation}
Note that, according to the argument above, \eqref{pnte} still holds for all $t\in (0,t_0]$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\preceq
(t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}}\vee t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}})$. Furthermore, due to \eqref{p4-3-2}, for any $y,z\in \mathds R^d$ with $|z-y|\leqslant 5t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}$, we have $|x-z|\leqslant |z-y|+|x-y|\preceq t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}}$ for any $x\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\preceq (t^{1/\alpha(x)}\vee t^{1/\alpha(y)})$, and so $$p(t,x,z)\succeq t^{-{d}/{\alpha(z)}}\asymp t^{-{d}/{\alpha(x)}},\quad t\in (0,t_0],$$ thanks to \eqref{p4-3-2} again. Therefore, according to the Chapman-Kolmogorov equation
\eqref{t1-1-5} and \eqref{pnte}, for every $t\in [t_0,2t_0]$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant
5t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}}$,
\begin{align*}
p(t,x,y)&=\int_{\mathds R^d}p(t_0,x,z)p(t-t_0,z,y)\,dz\succeq (t-t_0)^{-{d}/{\alpha(y)}}\int_{\{|z-y|\leqslant 5(t-t_0)^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}\}}
p(t_0,x,z)\,dz\\
&\succeq (t-t_0)^{-{d}/{\alpha(y)}}t_0^{-{d}/{\alpha(x)}}(t-t_0)^{{d}/{\alpha(y)}}\succeq
t^{-{d}/{\alpha(x)}}.
\end{align*}
Iterating the arguments above $[{1}/{t_0}]+1$ times, we can
obtain \eqref{p4-3-1}.
nodes.statement_short: Choose $\gamma$ and conclude for small $t$

nodes.name: Lower bound via the Lévy system
nodes.statement:
For any $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in\mathds R^d$, it holds that
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
&\mathds P_x\big(X_{\lambda t}\in B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}})\big)\\
&\geqslant \mathds P_x\big(\sigma_{B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2)}\leqslant \lambda t;
\sup_{s \in (\sigma_{B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2)},\lambda t)}\big|X_s-X_{\sigma_{B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2)}}\big|\leqslant t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2\big)\\
&\geqslant\mathds P_x\big(\sigma_{B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2)}\leqslant \lambda t ;\mathds P_{X_{\sigma_{B(y,
t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2)}}}\big(\sup_{0\leqslant s \leqslant \lambda t}|X_s-X_0|\leqslant
 t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2\big)\big)\\
&\geqslant \mathds P_x\big(\sigma_{B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2)}\leqslant \lambda t\big)
\cdot \inf_{z \in B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2)}\mathds P_z\big(
\tau_{B(z,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2)}>\lambda t\big),
\end{split}
\end{equation}
where in the second inequality we have used the strong Markov property.
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound via the Lévy system

nodes.name: Comparison of indices near $y$ and conclusion
nodes.statement:
Following the proof of \eqref{l3-2-8}, we know that
$t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}\geqslant C_1 t^{{1}/{\alpha(z)}}$ for every $z \in B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2)$.
Hence, there exists a constant $0<\lambda_0<1$ such that for all $0<\lambda<\lambda_0$
and $z \in B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2)$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
&\mathds P_z\big(\tau_{B(z,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2)}>\lambda t\big)
\geqslant \mathds P_z\big(\tau_{B(z,{C_1t^{{1}/{\alpha(z)}}}/{2})}>\lambda t\big)\geqslant {1}/{2},
\end{split}
\end{equation}
where the last inequality  follows from \eqref{l4-3-1}.
On the other hand, by the L\'evy system \eqref{p4-4-1}, for $\lambda>0$ small enough and for any $x,y\in \mathds R^d$ with $
|x-y|>5\max\{t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}},t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}\}$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
 \mathds P_x\big(\sigma_{B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2)}\leqslant \lambda t\big)
&\geqslant \mathds P_x\big(X_{\lambda t \wedge \tau_{B(x,t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}})}}\in B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2)\big)\\
&=\mathds E_x\bigg(\int_0^{\lambda t \wedge \tau_{B(x,t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}})}}
\int_{B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2)}\frac{du}{|X_s-u|^{d+\alpha(X_s)}}\,ds\bigg)\\
&\succeq \lambda t^{1+({d}/{\alpha(y)})}\cdot \inf_{z \in B(x,t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}})}\frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(z)}}
\cdot \mathds P_x\big(\tau_{B(x,t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}})}\geqslant \lambda t\big)\\
&\succeq \frac{t^{1+({d}/{\alpha(y)})}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}},
\end{split}
\end{equation}
where in the first inequality we used the fact that
$|x-y|\geqslant 5\max\{t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}},t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}\}$ implies $B(x,t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}})\cap
B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2)=\emptyset$, the second inequality follows from the fact that
$|z-u|\preceq |x-y|$ for any $z \in B\big(x,t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}}\big)$
and $u \in B\big(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2\big)$, and in the last inequality we used
\eqref{l4-3-1} and the fact that for any $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\geqslant 5t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}}$ and $z \in
B(x,t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}})$ and for every $0<t\leqslant 1$,
\begin{align*}
|x-y|^{-d-\alpha(z)}&\succeq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha(x)+C_2|x-z|^{\beta_0}}\succeq t^{C_2t^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_1}}}|x-y|^{-d-\alpha(x)}\succeq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha(x)}.
\end{align*}

According to \eqref{t4-4-2}, \eqref{t4-4-3} and \eqref{t4-4-4}, we obtain
that for any $|x-y|>5t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}}$ and $\lambda$ small enough,
\begin{equation} \mathds P_x\big(X_{\lambda t}\in B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}})\big)\succeq
\frac{t^{1+({d}/{\alpha(y)})}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}}.
\end{equation}
Hence, we arrive at
\begin{align*}
p(t,x,y)&=\int_{\mathds R^d}p(\lambda t,x,z)p((1-\lambda)t,z,y)\,dz\\
&\geqslant \int_{B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}})}
p(\lambda t,x,z)p((1-\lambda)t,z,y)\,dz\\
&\geqslant \inf_{|z-y|\leqslant t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}}p((1-\lambda)t,z,y)
\int_{B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}})}p(\lambda t,x,z)\,dz\\
&\succeq \inf_{|z-y|\leqslant C_3t^{{1}/{\alpha(z)}}}p((1-\lambda)t,z,y)
\int_{B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}})}p(\lambda t,x,z)\,dz\\
&\succeq t^{-{d}/{\alpha(y)}} \mathds P_x\big(X_{\lambda t}\in B(y,t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}})\big)\succeq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}},
\end{align*}
where the third inequality follows from the fact that $t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}\asymp t^{{1}/{\alpha(z)}}$ for every
$|y-z|\leqslant t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}$, in the forth inequality we used \eqref{p4-3-1}, and in the last inequality we used \eqref{t4-4-5}.
Therefore, \eqref{t4-4-1} has been proved.
